- **10-ft overhead utility zone** from energized conductor where overhead lines remain on a Core Transit Corridor or Urban Roadway frontage (LDC Subchapter E § 2.2.2.B.3.b; § 2.2.3.B.3). Same 10-ft zone applies inside Plaza Saltillo TOD (§ 3.3.2.A.3.b) and NBG (§ 3.3.2.B.4.b). Confirm whether the frontage street triggers Subchapter E or a regulating plan, then whether overhead is feasible to underground vs. relocate to rear-of-site.
- **Building-to-property-line undergrounding** mandatory on all CTC, Urban Roadway, Plaza Saltillo TOD, NBG, and Hill Country Roadway Corridor frontages (LDC Subchapter E § 2.2.2.B.3.a, § 2.2.3.B.3; Plaza Saltillo TOD § 3.3.2.A.3 / .3.3.A.3 / .3.4.A.3; NBG § 3.3.2.B.4.a; LDC § 25-2-1125). Budget service-lateral undergrounding cost.
- **ROW undergrounding "to the maximum extent practicable"** on the same frontages (same citations). This is judgment-driven; expect AE to negotiate which existing overhead is left in place vs. relocated to rear of site. Identify the existing overhead pattern early.
- **Transmission proximity** (60 kV+: 69 / 138 / 345 kV AE circuits): clearance envelopes are site-specific and require AE engineering (UCM § 1.14.3.1); circuits cannot be de-energized for nearby work. If a transmission line or labeled transmission easement abuts the site, treat as a binding envelope constraint and engage AE Transmission before locking massing. 25-ft × 16-ft vertical ROW access corridor must be preserved throughout construction (UCM § 1.14.4); plat notes per AEDC 1.16.0(8) become mandatory.
- **Service-drop vertical clearance** over driveways and access — 16 ft (no-truck) / 18 ft (truck/public street) (UCM § 1.10.6.2). Constrains canopy/porte-cochère height and loading-dock geometry.

### Underground routing & easements

- **AW planting-zone prohibition** (UCM § 2.9.1.C): no AW main, service, or appurtenance within the ROW street-tree planting zone. Root barriers required 7 ft from trunk; 2-ft AW offset from barrier; minimum 8-ft Street Tree Utility Gap between zones. Constrains where water service can leave the building when street trees are required.
- **No parallel routing within AE / public utility easement** (UCM § 2.9.1.A.3) — only perpendicular or up to 45° crossings. Constrains site utility layout when easements bisect the parcel.
- **Easement encroachment**: no permanent structures, pools, or buildings in AE easements (UCM § 1.10.10.2); landscaping/paving/walls in private AE easements require License Agreement from AE Public Involvement (UCM § 1.10.10.3); same items in public utility easements / public ROW require Chapter 14 license (§ 14-11-41). Evaluate whether the desired site plan crosses easements and whether the licensing pathway is workable.
- **Transformer pad siting** (UCM §§ 1.5.2.6, 1.10.4): hot-stick (padlocked) side 10 ft from any adjacent building; non-operator sides 3 ft from fence; operator side 5 ft; pad within 6 ft of paved truck-accessible surface; pad must be on customer property (not ROW or parkland); dedicated AE easement encumbers the pad. Reserve ~150–250 sf of usable frontage for the pad early in concept design.
- **AE truck access** (UCM § 1.3.16): 12-ft horizontal × 16-ft vertical clear path to AE equipment, with 20 × 35 ft set-up area at 35-ft vertical clearance. AE facilities normally at front of property or adjacent to paved surface (UCM § 1.3.15).
- **AE underground separations** (UCM § 1.10.5.A): 12 in min from other utilities at perpendicular crossings; 36 in from ≥60 psi gas. Joint trench with other utilities requires written AE agreement.
- **Water/wastewater main crossings** (UCM § 2.9.1.B.3, § 2.9.2.B.17): 12 in (AW above) / 18 in (AW below) for open-cut; trenchless = greater of 2× excavation diameter or 36 in.
- **ROW assignment / 24-in proximity** (§ 14-11-180(C)): facilities within 24 in of an existing ROW facility require AULCC ROW assignment change approval — a process, not a prohibition, but it consumes time.
- **Light rail corridors**: UCM § 5.2.2 Downtown Rail Corridor Permit for E-W 4th Street corridor (IH-35 to Seaholm); UROP consultation for other Project Connect alignments. Materially affects feasibility for parcels along Project Connect.
- **Moonlight towers** (downtown / central Austin): 25-ft ROW-installation prohibition (§ 14-11-205); 100-ft permit threshold for any construction near tower or guy wire (§ 14-11-201). Locations are not mapped in code — confirm by field survey early if site is in downtown or central Austin.

### Drainage-utility interactions

- **SCM staging area + maintenance access drive vertical clearance**: 14 ft from existing/proposed vegetation at maturity (DCM § 1.2.4.E.2.e and § 1.2.4.E.1.e.ii). Applies to COA-maintained and residential-development SCMs above 5,000 cf / 3-ft depth thresholds. Constrains canopy planting along maintenance routes.
- **No utility routing under detention/retention ponds** (reviewer convention; common-violation pattern). Affects site utility layout when ponds dominate the site.
- **Storm drain manhole vs. AE pole separation**: minimum 5 ft horizontal between storm drain manholes and AE overhead poles (reviewer convention). Constrains drainage outfall layout where existing poles are present.
- **Encasement under roads/structures** (UCM § 2.9.1.D): encased crossings under roadways require material, dimensional, and longitudinal extent specifications on plans. Budget bored/encased crossings on any utility leaving the site under a public street.

### Construction-phase impacts

- **Transmission demolition sequence** (UCM § 1.14.9): pre-construction safety meeting ≥48 hr before work; barricades 10 ft from all transmission structures including guys/anchors; warning signs under overhead facilities; no spoils or materials in transmission easement; crane and temporary-structure setbacks so they cannot fall within 20 ft of transmission. Forces an alternate spoils/laydown area when transmission abuts the site.
- **Work-zone vertical clearance below overhead** (UCM § 1.10.6.2; § 1.3.16): 18 ft where truck traffic is anticipated; 16 ft for affirmatively non-truck driveways; 35 ft set-up area in front of AE equipment. Affects crane staging and tilt-up sequencing.

### Connectivity & frontage

- **Table B utility-in-drive-aisle option** (LDC Subchapter E § 2.3.1.B.2): on subject sites (≥3 ac nonresidential, or surface parking between building and principal street), site must select ≥2 Table B options (3 if parking >125% of formerly required). Routing utilities under parking stalls is only a deficiency if utility-in-drive-aisle is the selected option but not implemented, or if Table B count is otherwise short. Evaluate whether the site can hit its Table B count without forcing utilities under parking.

### Administrative & service-capacity

- **AE Service Availability Letter** (AEDC § 1.4.1) — only where it is unclear which utility serves the site. Confirm AE service area on edge-of-territory parcels before design.
- **Service capacity**: AE Design has sole authority over available voltage / service characteristics (AEDC § 1.3.2). For large loads (>320 A continuous → instrument-rated CT service per AEDC § 1.4.0; or any Network Area service downtown), engage AE Design early; available capacity at the nearest feeder may itself be a constraint.
- **Street lighting**: AE develops the lighting installation plan. Developer responsibilities differ by location (AEDC §§ 1.6.4–1.6.7). Inside the Great Streets boundary (MLK / Lady Bird Lake / IH-35 / Lamar), Chapter 6 dictates fixture type (Gardco Circa/Form 10; Kim ERA), spacing (8 poles/block), and mounting heights (24-ft street / 12-ft pedestrian) — non-standard poles permitted at developer cost differential.
- **Four mandatory Standard AE Plan Notes** (verbatim) plus AEDC § 1.16.0(7) site-specific notes. Missing or altered text = rejection. Low-effort compliance issue but a frequent rejection cause.
- **AULCC Completeness Letter** gates ROW Review approval.
- **Addressing plan approval** (AMS) — distinct from an Address Validation Letter; AVL is **not** an approved addressing plan (common confusion). Gates site plan approval when new addresses or street names are involved.

## Opportunities to evaluate

- **Frontage selection on corner lots**: CTC designation takes priority as principal street; if a non-CTC corner is the practical service frontage, undergrounding cost may concentrate there. Conversely, choosing the non-CTC face for the building front can avoid the 10-ft overhead zone constraint on the CTC frontage entirely.
- **CTC short-lot alternative tree exception** (LDC Subchapter E § 2.2.2.B.3.c; Plaza Saltillo TOD § 3.3.2.A.3.c): on lots ≤120 ft deep, utility-compatible alternative tree species may be used **beneath** the overhead utilities rather than offset from them. Avoids removing/relocating street trees to clear an overhead corridor.
- **Plaza Saltillo TOD § 3.3.2.A.3.c facade-setback alternative**: same alternative-tree path also available when full compliance would push the facade ≥30 ft beyond the curb face. Material on tight TOD parcels.
- **AE relocation at customer expense** (UCM § 1.3.19): AE will relocate facilities at the customer's expense where feasible; build the cost into the pro forma rather than treating overhead as immovable. Note that AE will not relocate to an adjacent property without that owner's written consent — that consent is a feasibility variable.
- **UCM § 2.9.6 waiver pathway**: applicants who cannot meet UCM § 2 requirements have a formal waiver route. Worth evaluating on constrained urban sites instead of forcing a redesign.
- **Sub-AULCC-threshold scoping**: if ROW utility work can be kept below 300 LF citywide (or 25 LF in DAPCZ), with no pole relocations and no main assignments, AULCC review is avoided entirely. On small infill projects this can compress the schedule by 2–4 months — evaluate whether trenching can be confined to private property.
- **Rear-of-site undergrounding** vs. front-frontage undergrounding: where alley or rear access exists, "maximum extent practicable" can be argued for relocation to the rear, sometimes reducing the lateral length compared with undergrounding the entire frontage span.
- **Service-Only ESPA path**: keeping the total load under 350 A single-phase / 225 A three-phase (non-network) keeps the project on the Service-Only path and out of Design Services — a meaningful schedule compression where load can be managed.
- **AE License Agreement vs. easement relocation**: many AE-easement encroachments (paving, retaining walls, landscaping) can be resolved through a License Agreement from AE Public Involvement (UCM § 1.10.10.3) rather than relocating the easement. Faster and cheaper, when AE will agree.
- **Plat-note compliance for transmission easements**: where a transmission easement crosses the site, the AEDC § 1.16.0(8) plat notes (AE tree pruning, additional easement provision, erosion control, NESC clearance, 24-hr AE access, 48,000-lb axle load roads, 48-hr notice) are mandatory but can be added to the plat at low cost — treat as administrative, not feasibility-blocking, unless coupled with a physical envelope conflict.

## Inputs needed from Phase 2

- **environmental.md** / **GIS** — Plaza Saltillo TOD boundary, NBG boundary, CTC/Urban Roadway frontage classification, Hill Country Roadway Corridor proximity (1,000 ft of named roadways), DAPCZ boundary (Code § 14-11-161(7)), Great Streets boundary, light rail corridor proximity, parkland boundaries.
- **utility-survey.md** — existing overhead and underground AE facilities on or adjacent to site (poles, conductors, vaults, transformers, guys/anchors); transmission easement boundaries; existing AE easements / PUEs; existing ROW utilities (AW mains, gas, telecom); existing moonlight towers if downtown/central.
- **transportation.md** — frontage street classifications; truck-access expectations (for service-drop 16 vs. 18 ft determination); driveway locations.
- **property-records.md** — recorded easements (private AE, PUE, transmission, drainage); plat notes referencing transmission easement obligations.
- **zoning.md** — base zoning + any regulating-plan overlay (Plaza Saltillo TOD subdistrict, NBG subdistrict prefix TOD/CMU/NMU/NR/WMU/CI, UNO, ERC, downtown).
- **program intent** — service-load estimate (amps / phase), continuous-load expectation, presence of vaults or generators, exterior wall modifications (for BSPA trigger).

## Output structure

Standard discipline output shape — see `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.

## Severity heuristics

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| Transmission line on or abutting site with envelope conflict that cannot be cleared without relocating the line | `significant` |
| AE service capacity insufficient at the nearest feeder for projected load (Network Area downtown or large industrial) | `significant` |
| Required overhead-to-underground conversion along entire CTC/Urban Roadway frontage materially impacts pro forma | `significant` |
| Site within 25 ft of a moonlight tower (ROW prohibition) blocking proposed ROW work | `significant` |
| 10-ft overhead utility zone (Subchapter E / Plaza Saltillo / NBG) crosses desired building footprint with no short-lot alternative-tree exception | `significant` |
| AULCC trigger met (≥300 LF citywide, ≥25 LF DAPCZ, pole relocation, main assignment) — adds 2–4 months schedule | `moderate` |
| Hill Country Roadway Corridor — all on-site utilities must go underground; cost adder vs. mixed-mode | `moderate` |
| Transformer pad placement constrains frontage usable width or requires AE easement reservation | `moderate` |
| AW planting-zone routing conflict requires re-routing water service away from frontage | `moderate` |
| Site within 100 ft of moonlight tower or guy wire — permit required, no prohibition | `moderate` |
| Light rail corridor proximity (non-4th Street) — UROP consultation required | `moderate` |
| Service-load size pushes project from Service-Only to Design Services ESPA path | `note` |
| Standard AE plan notes verbatim compliance | `note` |
| Addressing plan / street-name reservation required for new private drives | `note` |
| Existing AE facility locations not field-verified (only AE record-drawing data) | `data-gap` |
| Moonlight tower proximity unknown (downtown / central Austin site without field survey) | `data-gap` |
| AE Service Availability uncertain at parcel (edge of service territory) | `data-gap` |

## Common pitfalls

- Treating "the utility provider operates overhead in the vicinity" as authorization to leave the building-to-property-line service overhead on a CTC, Urban Roadway, Plaza Saltillo TOD, NBG, or Hill Country frontage — undergrounding is mandatory regardless.
- Anchoring overhead clearance dimensions to the **pole centerline** rather than the **outermost conductor** — on three-phase configurations the outer conductor may be several feet offset; clearances that appear adequate on plan can be non-compliant in the field.
- Conflating the UCM § 1.10.3 universal 7.5-ft / 15-ft clearances (apply everywhere overhead AE exists) with the LDC Subchapter E 10-ft overhead utility zone (applies only on CTC / Urban Roadway / Plaza Saltillo / NBG). Both can apply simultaneously on those frontages; only UCM 1.10.3 applies elsewhere.
- Assuming AULCC is universal — it is only triggered by the four specific thresholds. Small infill projects often slide under and shouldn't carry AULCC time in the schedule.
- Citing **§ 14-11-205** for the 100-ft moonlight tower permit — that section is the 25-ft ROW prohibition. The 100-ft permit threshold is **§ 14-11-201**.
- Citing **LDC § 25-9-173** for service availability — this section does not exist; correct authority is AEDC §§ 1.4.1 / 1.3.2.
- Accepting an Address Validation Letter (AVL) as an approved addressing plan — they are distinct; the addressing plan must be separately approved by AMS before site plan approval.
- Assuming Hill Country undergrounding applies near US 183 or US 290 West — LDC § 25-2-1104(A) carves these out; only the five named Hill Country Roadways trigger § 25-2-1125.
- Drawing transformer pad in the public ROW or labeling its area as parkland — both prohibited; the pad must be on customer property within a dedicated AE easement.
- Treating UCM § 2.9.1.A.1 as the basis for pole/transmission separation rules — that section governs easement width, not pole placement; the pole-placement requirement currently lacks a confirmed code anchor and should be coordinated with AE directly.
- Routing non-electrical utilities parallel within an AE / public utility easement boundary — only perpendicular (up to 45°) crossings are permitted.
- Failing to budget post-approval ESPA time — ESPA is submitted after site plan approval; AE design can run 6–12 weeks (Service-Only) to 16+ weeks (Design Services / Network Area) before an Electric Permit number is issued, gating downstream work.
- Confusing the Building Service Planning Application (BSPA — required for building permits with exterior modifications) with the ESPA (required for new/modified electric service). Both can apply.
- Sizing transformer pads to a "standard" 10×10 dimension — pad dimensions are determined by AE Design based on the customer's AutoCAD submittal (UCM § 1.5.2.6); no universal fixed dimension exists in code text.
- Showing a vault near overhead power lines with a plan note "vault approved by AE Design" but no AE written clearance letter in the project file — UCM § 1.10.3 requires the letter to be filed, not merely referenced.
- Routing AE underground conduit in a joint trench with other utilities without a written AE joint-trench agreement (UCM § 1.10.5.A) — the 12-in separation rule covers perpendicular crossings only; parallel/joint runs require the separate agreement.

1→# Erosion, Trees & Plants Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Tree protection, erosion and sedimentation control (ESC), vegetation removal, heritage tree rules, root zone protection, landscape compliance, Critical Environmental Features (CEFs), and revegetation. Bridges with `el` (Environmental Layers: floodplain, CWQZ, BSZ pollutant loading) at the CEF/wetland boundary and with `sde` (Site Drainage/Engineering) at grading, utility, and SCM planting interfaces.
     6→
     7→## Authoritative sources
     8→
     9→- Tree ordinance: Austin LDC § 25-8 Subchapter B Article 2 (Trees), §§ 25-8-601 through 25-8-646
    10→- Tree survey & preservation standards: ECM Section 3.3 (tree survey) and ECM Section 3.5.2 (preservation criteria, restated in entirety by Rule R161-22.16, December 14, 2022)
    11→- Heritage species list: LDC § 25-8-602(1) — Texas Ash, Bald Cypress, American Elm, Cedar Elm, Texas Madrone, Bigtooth Maple, all Oaks, Pecan, Arizona Walnut, Eastern Black Walnut
    12→- Mitigation rates and methods: ECM § 3.5.4 (and Appendix F species list)
    13→- Tree protection details: ECM § 3.6.1 and SSM Item No. 610
    14→- Erosion / sediment control: LDC § 25-8-181, ECM Section 1.4 (and Appendices P-1, P-3, P-4)
    15→- Landscape and parking lot tree requirements: LDC § 25-2-1001 et seq.; ECM Section 2
    16→- Native tree replacement (Hill Country Roadway Corridor only): LDC § 25-2-1022 / 1025; corridor defined at LDC § 25-2-1103
    17→- Critical Environmental Features and ERI: LDC § 25-8-1(6), § 25-8-121, § 25-8-281(C); ECM §§ 1.3.0, 1.10.3, 1.10.4
    18→- Save Our Springs Ordinance (BSZ): LDC §§ 25-8-481, 25-8-514, 25-8-515, 25-8-516
    19→
    20→## Regulatory pathway
    21→
    22→| Trigger | Path | Decision body | Typical timeline |
    23→|---|---|---|---|
    24→| Any regulated tree (≥ 8" DBH) on site, on adjacent property with CRZ entering LOC, or in adjacent ROW | RPLS-certified tree survey + tree protection plan with site plan submittal | DSD City Arborist | Included in site plan cycle |
    25→| Protected tree (≥ 19" DBH, any species) proposed for removal | Removal permit with documentation of one of six LDC § 25-8-624(A) criteria | City Arborist | Concurrent with site plan |
    26→| Heritage tree (≥ 24" DBH + listed species), no stem ≥ 30" | Administrative Variance under LDC § 25-8-642; requires § 25-8-646 prerequisite-variance exhaustion (unless DDI) | DSD Director on City Arborist recommendation | ~2–4 months including pre-meeting + fiscal posting |
    27→| Heritage tree with at least one stem ≥ 30" | Land Use Commission variance with Environmental Commission review under LDC § 25-8-643 | LUC + EC | ~4–8 months; public hearings |
    28→| DDI (dead/diseased/imminent hazard) heritage tree | Administrative variance still required, but no fee and 0% mitigation — City Arborist letter (not private arborist alone) determines DDI | City Arborist + Director | ~1–2 months |
    29→| LOC > 25 acres OR any LOC in Barton Springs Zone | Phased ESC plan required (ECM 1.4.4.B.5.I.a; LDC § 25-8-184); BSZ adds 18-month clearing-to-revegetation cap | DSD Environmental | Within site plan cycle |
    30→| Site in EARZ, contains slope > 15%, contains CWQZ, or within 150 ft of mapped wetland | Environmental Resource Inventory (ERI) with three sub-reports (Hydrogeologic, Vegetation, Wastewater); 7-year validity | WPD | 2–4 months for field work + sealed report |
    31→| Karst feature (cave, sinkhole, fault, fracture) over EARZ | 50-ft walking transect karst survey by Texas Licensed Professional Geoscientist (ECM 1.10.3); 150–300 ft buffer to catchment | WPD | Adds 1–3 months |
    32→| Wetland CEF on or within 150 ft of site | 150-ft buffer; reducible to 50-ft avg via 1:1 in-kind on-site mitigation (ECM 1.10.4(D)(2)–(3)) | WPD | 2–4 months |
    33→| Hill Country Roadway Corridor (within 1,000 ft of Loop 360, RM 620, RM 2222, RM 2244, or Southwest Pkwy) | Native tree replacement (LDC § 25-2-1022) + 40% natural-area set-aside (LDC § 25-2-1025) | DSD | Constrains massing from concept stage |
    34→
    35→## Constraints to evaluate
    36→
    37→**Tree inventory and survey**
    38→- All trees ≥ 8" DBH must be surveyed by an RPLS within 5 years of submittal (ECM 3.3.1.A; ECM 3.3.2.A). Off-site and ROW trees count if their CRZ reaches the LOC — a 30-inch tree 28 ft beyond the boundary still triggers survey because its 30-ft CRZ enters the site (ECM 3.3.2.A.1).
    39→- Heritage trees (≥ 24" DBH + listed species) must be marked "H"; protected trees (≥ 19" DBH any species) annotated. Multi-trunk DBH formula: largest stem + ½ each additional stem ≥ 1" (ECM 3.3.2.A.2).
    40→- For initial diligence, satellite imagery is not a substitute — DBH cannot be inferred from canopy and field survey is the precondition to any reliable site plan. Budget RPLS + ISA-certified arborist field work before committing to massing.
    41→
    42→**Critical Root Zone (CRZ) geometry — the buildable envelope killer**
    43→- CRZ radius (ft) = DBH (in); Half CRZ = DBH ÷ 2 ft; Quarter CRZ = DBH ÷ 4 ft (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). For a 30" heritage oak: 30-ft CRZ, 15-ft Half CRZ, 7.5-ft Quarter CRZ.
    44→- Three nested rules apply simultaneously: ≥ 50% of total CRZ area preserved at natural grade with natural ground cover; cut/fill ≤ 4" in the Half CRZ; **zero cut/fill of any depth in the Quarter CRZ** (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). Failing any of the three means the tree is legally "removed" — mitigation and variance triggered whether or not the developer intends removal.
    45→- "Construction impacts" are measured at the line of excavation, not the visible face of improvements — over-excavation behind curbs, scaffolding, concrete form bracing, staging, and utility trenching all count (ECM 3.5.2.A.3). A curb shown right at the Half-CRZ line is non-compliant.
    46→- City Arborist may (discretionary, not automatic) require an enlarged CRZ at 1¼ to 1½ × standard radius for Post Oak (*Quercus stellata*), rare trees, or trees in sensitive conditions (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). Assume the larger radius for Post Oak when massing.
    47→
    48→**Heritage tree removal**
    49→- Removal prohibited without a permit; permit only issues with an approved variance under LDC § 25-8-642 (admin, < 30" stem) or § 25-8-643 (LUC + EC, ≥ 30" stem). Tree must meet one of the five § 25-8-624(A) criteria: prevents reasonable access, prevents reasonable use, imminent hazard, dead, or diseased and not restorable.
    50→- Prerequisite-variance rule (LDC § 25-8-646): applicant must have first sought and been denied every other applicable Code variance, waiver, exemption, or alternative compliance (setbacks, AEC, compatibility, etc.) before requesting heritage removal. This adds calendar time and forces concept-stage exploration of layout alternatives.
    51→- Mitigation: standard heritage rate is **300% of removed caliper inches** (ECM 3.5.4.A.1); reduced 150% rate is City-Arborist-discretionary for verified poor condition; DDI is 0% (City Arborist determination required). 19"+ protected tree (Appendix F species) is 100%; non-Appendix F 19"+ is 50%; 8–18.9" is 50%/25%.
    52→- Three mitigation forms (ECM 3.5.4.B): on-site replanting, preserved-undersized-tree inch-for-inch credit, or fee-in-lieu to the Urban Forest Replenishment Fund (UFRF) at $200/caliper inch (private) — but UFRF is only available when the City Arborist determines the site is unsuitable for planting. ROW/parkland trees route to the Planting for the Future Trust (PFTF), tracked separately.
    53→- Replacement trees: at least 75% of total caliper must be Significant Shade Provider species (Appendix F "SS" column — 39 species).
    54→
    55→**Erosion and sedimentation control (ESC)**
    56→- Every site requires an ESC plan (LDC § 25-8-181; ECM § 1.4). The Limit of Construction (LOC) is the operative boundary and must encompass all disturbance including off-site work and staging; ESC quantities (silt fence, mulch sock) are computed from actual LOC and disturbed area (ECM 1.4.4.B.3).
    57→- Phasing trigger: LOC > 25 acres requires a phased ESC plan (ECM 1.4.4.B.5.I.a). **Any site in the Barton Springs Zone requires phasing regardless of LOC size**, plus the 18-month clearing-to-revegetation cap (LDC § 25-8-184; ECM Appendix P-3).
    58→- Default plan scale is 1"=50' (Environmental Review Requirements § 3); 1"=100' only with express DSD authorization for large sites.
    59→- Cut/fill > 4 ft must be disclosed for Suburban, Water Supply Suburban, Water Supply Rural, and BSZ sites; Urban watersheds are exempt.
    60→- Silt fence: J-hooks at 100-ft intervals, individual sections ≤ 200 ft (ECM 1.4.5.G.4.A.1.1 / 1.4.5.G.4.A.1.4). Triangular Filter Dikes allowed only in sheet flow (≈ first 100 ft of flow path); concentrated flow areas need rock berms (ECM 1.4.5.H).
    61→- Stabilized construction entrance: 4–8" open-graded crushed stone, ≥ 8" thick, ≥ 50 ft long, full ingress/egress width (ECM 1.4.5.N; SSM 641S).
    62→
    63→**Environmental zones and CEFs**
    64→- Critical Water Quality Zone (CWQZ) along any waterway with ≥ 64-ac drainage area (LDC § 25-8-92). Widths vary by watershed class: urban watersheds = 100-yr fully developed floodplain; suburban = 100/200/300 ft by waterway size; water supply / BSZ = floodplain-based with min/max from centerline. CWQZ within LOC requires hatching and native grassland seeding per Spec 609S.6.
    65→- CEFs (LDC § 25-8-1(6)): bluffs, canyon rimrocks, caves, faults/fractures, seeps, sinkholes, springs, wetlands. Standard 150-ft three-dimensional buffer (LDC § 25-8-281(C)). Karst point-recharge features over EARZ extend to topographic catchment (150–300 ft); wetland buffer measured from outer delineation edge.
    66→- Save Our Springs (BSZ) impervious cover caps: 15% recharge zone, 20% contributing zone within Barton Creek watershed, 25% remainder. **No variance or waiver available** (LDC § 25-8-515); only the pre-1991 small-lot exemption (≤ 8,000 SF total IC) or Chapter 245/HB 1704 vested-rights determination provides relief. Plan to design under the cap from day one.
    67→- Slope > 15% anywhere on site triggers ERI requirement and slope-stabilization design (LDC § 25-8-121(B)).
    68→
    69→**Vegetation removal and landscape compliance**
    70→- Removal permit required for every regulated tree (≥ 8" DBH) including the 15 mitigation-exempt invasive species (Arizona Ash, Chinaberry, Chinese Parasol, Chinese Pistache, Chinese Tallow, Koelreuteria, Ligustrum, Mimosa, Paper Mulberry, White Mulberry, Photinia, Salt Cedar, Siberian Elm, Tree of Heaven, Vitex) — no mitigation but the permit is still required (ECM 3.5.4.A.2.b).
    71→- Excessive pruning (> 25% foliage in an annual growing season) is statutorily defined as removal (LDC § 25-8-602(4)(d); ECM 3.5.2.A.2). Scaffolding clearance pruning counts toward the 25% — if a building can't be built without exceeding it, the building must move.
    72→- Landscape plan + parking lot / street tree requirements under LDC § 25-2-1001 and ECM Section 2; SCM plantings (biofiltration, rain gardens) bridge with `sde` and have their own native-species and buffer rules.
    73→
    74→**Hill Country Roadway Corridor (if applicable)**
    75→- Native tree replacement under LDC § 25-2-1022 for each removed native (live oak, Spanish oak, cedar elm, shin oak, bald cypress, post oak, pecan, bur oak, black walnut), small native, or cluster of 3+ native trees 2–6" within 10 ft.
    76→- Small natives subject to replacement: Texas madrone, black cherry, Texas mountain laurel, evergreen sumac, Mexican buckeye, flameleaf sumac, Texas persimmon.
    77→- 40% of site in natural state (LDC § 25-2-1025). Check "Hill Country Roadways Overlay" in facts.md — applies only inside the corridor, not to general BSZ/EARZ sites.
    78→
    79→**Tree protection physical detailing (constructability)**
    80→- Chain-link fence ≥ 5 ft tall at or beyond the CRZ boundary; trunk wrap (2×4 lumber wired, first 8 ft of trunk, retightened every 6 months) required when fence is within 5 ft of trunk (ECM 3.6.1; SSM 610.4.A).
    81→- Mulch ≥ 8" deep in any unfenced section of CRZ; no material storage within fenced CRZ.
    82→- Boring pits within CRZ must be ≥ 4 ft below existing grade; bore pits within Half CRZ are flagged as a deficiency (ECM 3.5.2.B.2).
    83→- All work within CRZ by hand; small equipment only with 8" mulch + plywood/mats (ECM 3.6.1.C.2–3).
    84→
    85→**BSZ-specific non-degradation and operating requirements**
    86→- BSZ sites must demonstrate zero-net-increase in annual average loadings for 10 regulated pollutants (LDC § 25-8-514(A)) via SLAT, ECM 1.6.9.3 manual equations, or independent engineering analysis.
    87→- Two SCMs in series required (ECM 1.6.9.3): first retention-type, second volume-reduction-type — design implication for site plan layout and elevations from concept.
    88→- Commercial and multifamily BSZ projects require annual water-quality operating permit (LDC § 25-8-233); ECM 1.2.2.1 standard cover-sheet block required.
    89→- BSZ redevelopment > 25 dwelling units requires City Council approval after EC review (LDC § 25-8-26(F)(1)) — significant political/calendar risk.
    90→
    91→## Opportunities to evaluate
    92→
    93→- **DDI pathway**: if the City Arborist determines a heritage or protected tree is dead, diseased, or an imminent hazard, removal is no-fee and 0% mitigation. Private arborist reports alone do not establish DDI — pursue the City Arborist letter early when condition is genuinely poor.
    94→- **150% poor-condition rate** for heritage trees: City-Arborist-discretionary halving of the 300% mitigation if a qualified arborist documents poor condition and the City Arborist approves. Worth pursuing on declining heritage oaks.
    95→- **Modified CRZ (MCRZ)** (ECM 3.5.2.B.4.b): City Arborist may reconfigure CRZ boundary when prior development blocked root growth, as long as total area equals standard CRZ and it stays inside the protection fence. Half/Quarter CRZ rules still apply.
    96→- **Like-for-like existing impacts** (ECM 3.5.2.B.4.a): rebuilding within the footprint of existing Half- or Quarter-CRZ impacts is allowable if no deeper or wider — useful on infill with existing slabs/curbs within CRZ.
    97→- **Elevated foundations within Half CRZ** (ECM 3.5.2.B.3): allowed with ≥ 4" air gap, natural-grade soil beneath, non-leaching barrier for concrete; cannot span the Quarter CRZ; footprint still counts toward the 50% impact ceiling.
    98→- **Low-impact excavation** (ECM 3.5.2.B.2): hand digging or compressed-air ("air spade") permitted in restricted zones; significant roots (≥ 1.5" diameter) cannot be cut without City Arborist authorization.

   126→| Wetland CEF on or within 150 ft of site | `significant` — 150-ft buffer compresses envelope; ERI waiver unavailable; 1:1 mitigation pathway reduces to 50-ft avg if pursued |

   128→| Karst feature suspected over EARZ | `moderate` to `significant` — Licensed Professional Geoscientist karst survey + 150–300 ft catchment buffer |

   137→- Inferring heritage status from canopy in aerial imagery — DBH at 4.5 ft above natural grade is the only valid measure; field survey by RPLS is the precondition.

# Erosion, Trees & Plants Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

Tree protection, erosion and sedimentation control (ESC), vegetation removal, heritage tree rules, root zone protection, landscape compliance, Critical Environmental Features (CEFs), and revegetation. Bridges with `el` (Environmental Layers: floodplain, CWQZ, BSZ pollutant loading) at the CEF/wetland boundary and with `sde` (Site Drainage/Engineering) at grading, utility, and SCM planting interfaces.

## Authoritative sources

- Tree ordinance: Austin LDC § 25-8 Subchapter B Article 2 (Trees), §§ 25-8-601 through 25-8-646
- Tree survey & preservation standards: ECM Section 3.3 (tree survey) and ECM Section 3.5.2 (preservation criteria, restated in entirety by Rule R161-22.16, December 14, 2022)
- Heritage species list: LDC § 25-8-602(1) — Texas Ash, Bald Cypress, American Elm, Cedar Elm, Texas Madrone, Bigtooth Maple, all Oaks, Pecan, Arizona Walnut, Eastern Black Walnut
- Mitigation rates and methods: ECM § 3.5.4 (and Appendix F species list)
- Tree protection details: ECM § 3.6.1 and SSM Item No. 610
- Erosion / sediment control: LDC § 25-8-181, ECM Section 1.4 (and Appendices P-1, P-3, P-4)
- Landscape and parking lot tree requirements: LDC § 25-2-1001 et seq.; ECM Section 2
- Native tree replacement (Hill Country Roadway Corridor only): LDC § 25-2-1022 / 1025; corridor defined at LDC § 25-2-1103
- Critical Environmental Features and ERI: LDC § 25-8-1(6), § 25-8-121, § 25-8-281(C); ECM §§ 1.3.0, 1.10.3, 1.10.4
- Save Our Springs Ordinance (BSZ): LDC §§ 25-8-481, 25-8-514, 25-8-515, 25-8-516

## Regulatory pathway

| Trigger | Path | Decision body | Typical timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Any regulated tree (≥ 8" DBH) on site, on adjacent property with CRZ entering LOC, or in adjacent ROW | RPLS-certified tree survey + tree protection plan with site plan submittal | DSD City Arborist | Included in site plan cycle |
| Protected tree (≥ 19" DBH, any species) proposed for removal | Removal permit with documentation of one of six LDC § 25-8-624(A) criteria | City Arborist | Concurrent with site plan |
| Heritage tree (≥ 24" DBH + listed species), no stem ≥ 30" | Administrative Variance under LDC § 25-8-642; requires § 25-8-646 prerequisite-variance exhaustion (unless DDI) | DSD Director on City Arborist recommendation | ~2–4 months including pre-meeting + fiscal posting |
| Heritage tree with at least one stem ≥ 30" | Land Use Commission variance with Environmental Commission review under LDC § 25-8-643 | LUC + EC | ~4–8 months; public hearings |
| DDI (dead/diseased/imminent hazard) heritage tree | Administrative variance still required, but no fee and 0% mitigation — City Arborist letter (not private arborist alone) determines DDI | City Arborist + Director | ~1–2 months |
| LOC > 25 acres OR any LOC in Barton Springs Zone | Phased ESC plan required (ECM 1.4.4.B.5.I.a; LDC § 25-8-184); BSZ adds 18-month clearing-to-revegetation cap | DSD Environmental | Within site plan cycle |
| Site in EARZ, contains slope > 15%, contains CWQZ, or within 150 ft of mapped wetland | Environmental Resource Inventory (ERI) with three sub-reports (Hydrogeologic, Vegetation, Wastewater); 7-year validity | WPD | 2–4 months for field work + sealed report |
| Karst feature (cave, sinkhole, fault, fracture) over EARZ | 50-ft walking transect karst survey by Texas Licensed Professional Geoscientist (ECM 1.10.3); 150–300 ft buffer to catchment | WPD | Adds 1–3 months |
| Wetland CEF on or within 150 ft of site | 150-ft buffer; reducible to 50-ft avg via 1:1 in-kind on-site mitigation (ECM 1.10.4(D)(2)–(3)) | WPD | 2–4 months |
| Hill Country Roadway Corridor (within 1,000 ft of Loop 360, RM 620, RM 2222, RM 2244, or Southwest Pkwy) | Native tree replacement (LDC § 25-2-1022) + 40% natural-area set-aside (LDC § 25-2-1025) | DSD | Constrains massing from concept stage |

## Constraints to evaluate

**Tree inventory and survey**
- All trees ≥ 8" DBH must be surveyed by an RPLS within 5 years of submittal (ECM 3.3.1.A; ECM 3.3.2.A). Off-site and ROW trees count if their CRZ reaches the LOC — a 30-inch tree 28 ft beyond the boundary still triggers survey because its 30-ft CRZ enters the site (ECM 3.3.2.A.1).
- Heritage trees (≥ 24" DBH + listed species) must be marked "H"; protected trees (≥ 19" DBH any species) annotated. Multi-trunk DBH formula: largest stem + ½ each additional stem ≥ 1" (ECM 3.3.2.A.2).
- For initial diligence, satellite imagery is not a substitute — DBH cannot be inferred from canopy and field survey is the precondition to any reliable site plan. Budget RPLS + ISA-certified arborist field work before committing to massing.

**Critical Root Zone (CRZ) geometry — the buildable envelope killer**
- CRZ radius (ft) = DBH (in); Half CRZ = DBH ÷ 2 ft; Quarter CRZ = DBH ÷ 4 ft (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). For a 30" heritage oak: 30-ft CRZ, 15-ft Half CRZ, 7.5-ft Quarter CRZ.
- Three nested rules apply simultaneously: ≥ 50% of total CRZ area preserved at natural grade with natural ground cover; cut/fill ≤ 4" in the Half CRZ; **zero cut/fill of any depth in the Quarter CRZ** (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). Failing any of the three means the tree is legally "removed" — mitigation and variance triggered whether or not the developer intends removal.
- "Construction impacts" are measured at the line of excavation, not the visible face of improvements — over-excavation behind curbs, scaffolding, concrete form bracing, staging, and utility trenching all count (ECM 3.5.2.A.3). A curb shown right at the Half-CRZ line is non-compliant.
- City Arborist may (discretionary, not automatic) require an enlarged CRZ at 1¼ to 1½ × standard radius for Post Oak (*Quercus stellata*), rare trees, or trees in sensitive conditions (ECM 3.5.2.A.1). Assume the larger radius for Post Oak when massing.

**Heritage tree removal**
- Removal prohibited without a permit; permit only issues with an approved variance under LDC § 25-8-642 (admin, < 30" stem) or § 25-8-643 (LUC + EC, ≥ 30" stem). Tree must meet one of the five § 25-8-624(A) criteria: prevents reasonable access, prevents reasonable use, imminent hazard, dead, or diseased and not restorable.
- Prerequisite-variance rule (LDC § 25-8-646): applicant must have first sought and been denied every other applicable Code variance, waiver, exemption, or alternative compliance (setbacks, AEC, compatibility, etc.) before requesting heritage removal. This adds calendar time and forces concept-stage exploration of layout alternatives.
- Mitigation: standard heritage rate is **300% of removed caliper inches** (ECM 3.5.4.A.1); reduced 150% rate is City-Arborist-discretionary for verified poor condition; DDI is 0% (City Arborist determination required). 19"+ protected tree (Appendix F species) is 100%; non-Appendix F 19"+ is 50%; 8–18.9" is 50%/25%.
- Three mitigation forms (ECM 3.5.4.B): on-site replanting, preserved-undersized-tree inch-for-inch credit, or fee-in-lieu to the Urban Forest Replenishment Fund (UFRF) at $200/caliper inch (private) — but UFRF is only available when the City Arborist determines the site is unsuitable for planting. ROW/parkland trees route to the Planting for the Future Trust (PFTF), tracked separately.
- Replacement trees: at least 75% of total caliper must be Significant Shade Provider species (Appendix F "SS" column — 39 species).

**Erosion and sedimentation control (ESC)**
- Every site requires an ESC plan (LDC § 25-8-181; ECM § 1.4). The Limit of Construction (LOC) is the operative boundary and must encompass all disturbance including off-site work and staging; ESC quantities (silt fence, mulch sock) are computed from actual LOC and disturbed area (ECM 1.4.4.B.3).
- Phasing trigger: LOC > 25 acres requires a phased ESC plan (ECM 1.4.4.B.5.I.a). **Any site in the Barton Springs Zone requires phasing regardless of LOC size**, plus the 18-month clearing-to-revegetation cap (LDC § 25-8-184; ECM Appendix P-3).
- Default plan scale is 1"=50' (Environmental Review Requirements § 3); 1"=100' only with express DSD authorization for large sites.
- Cut/fill > 4 ft must be disclosed for Suburban, Water Supply Suburban, Water Supply Rural, and BSZ sites; Urban watersheds are exempt.
- Silt fence: J-hooks at 100-ft intervals, individual sections ≤ 200 ft (ECM 1.4.5.G.4.A.1.1 / 1.4.5.G.4.A.1.4). Triangular Filter Dikes allowed only in sheet flow (≈ first 100 ft of flow path); concentrated flow areas need rock berms (ECM 1.4.5.H).
- Stabilized construction entrance: 4–8" open-graded crushed stone, ≥ 8" thick, ≥ 50 ft long, full ingress/egress width (ECM 1.4.5.N; SSM 641S).

**Environmental zones and CEFs**
- Critical Water Quality Zone (CWQZ) along any waterway with ≥ 64-ac drainage area (LDC § 25-8-92). Widths vary by watershed class: urban watersheds = 100-yr fully developed floodplain; suburban = 100/200/300 ft by waterway size; water supply / BSZ = floodplain-based with min/max from centerline. CWQZ within LOC requires hatching and native grassland seeding per Spec 609S.6.
- CEFs (LDC § 25-8-1(6)): bluffs, canyon rimrocks, caves, faults/fractures, seeps, sinkholes, springs, wetlands. Standard 150-ft three-dimensional buffer (LDC § 25-8-281(C)). Karst point-recharge features over EARZ extend to topographic catchment (150–300 ft); wetland buffer measured from outer delineation edge.
- Save Our Springs (BSZ) impervious cover caps: 15% recharge zone, 20% contributing zone within Barton Creek watershed, 25% remainder. **No variance or waiver available** (LDC § 25-8-515); only the pre-1991 small-lot exemption (≤ 8,000 SF total IC) or Chapter 245/HB 1704 vested-rights determination provides relief. Plan to design under the cap from day one.
- Slope > 15% anywhere on site triggers ERI requirement and slope-stabilization design (LDC § 25-8-121(B)).

**Vegetation removal and landscape compliance**
- Removal permit required for every regulated tree (≥ 8" DBH) including the 15 mitigation-exempt invasive species (Arizona Ash, Chinaberry, Chinese Parasol, Chinese Pistache, Chinese Tallow, Koelreuteria, Ligustrum, Mimosa, Paper Mulberry, White Mulberry, Photinia, Salt Cedar, Siberian Elm, Tree of Heaven, Vitex) — no mitigation but the permit is still required (ECM 3.5.4.A.2.b).
- Excessive pruning (> 25% foliage in an annual growing season) is statutorily defined as removal (LDC § 25-8-602(4)(d); ECM 3.5.2.A.2). Scaffolding clearance pruning counts toward the 25% — if a building can't be built without exceeding it, the building must move.
- Landscape plan + parking lot / street tree requirements under LDC § 25-2-1001 and ECM Section 2; SCM plantings (biofiltration, rain gardens) bridge with `sde` and have their own native-species and buffer rules.

**Hill Country Roadway Corridor (if applicable)**
- Native tree replacement under LDC § 25-2-1022 for each removed native (live oak, Spanish oak, cedar elm, shin oak, bald cypress, post oak, pecan, bur oak, black walnut), small native, or cluster of 3+ native trees 2–6" within 10 ft.
- Small natives subject to replacement: Texas madrone, black cherry, Texas mountain laurel, evergreen sumac, Mexican buckeye, flameleaf sumac, Texas persimmon.
- 40% of site in natural state (LDC § 25-2-1025). Check "Hill Country Roadways Overlay" in facts.md — applies only inside the corridor, not to general BSZ/EARZ sites.

**Tree protection physical detailing (constructability)**
- Chain-link fence ≥ 5 ft tall at or beyond the CRZ boundary; trunk wrap (2×4 lumber wired, first 8 ft of trunk, retightened every 6 months) required when fence is within 5 ft of trunk (ECM 3.6.1; SSM 610.4.A).
- Mulch ≥ 8" deep in any unfenced section of CRZ; no material storage within fenced CRZ.
- Boring pits within CRZ must be ≥ 4 ft below existing grade; bore pits within Half CRZ are flagged as a deficiency (ECM 3.5.2.B.2).
- All work within CRZ by hand; small equipment only with 8" mulch + plywood/mats (ECM 3.6.1.C.2–3).

**BSZ-specific non-degradation and operating requirements**
- BSZ sites must demonstrate zero-net-increase in annual average loadings for 10 regulated pollutants (LDC § 25-8-514(A)) via SLAT, ECM 1.6.9.3 manual equations, or independent engineering analysis.
- Two SCMs in series required (ECM 1.6.9.3): first retention-type, second volume-reduction-type — design implication for site plan layout and elevations from concept.
- Commercial and multifamily BSZ projects require annual water-quality operating permit (LDC § 25-8-233); ECM 1.2.2.1 standard cover-sheet block required.
- BSZ redevelopment > 25 dwelling units requires City Council approval after EC review (LDC § 25-8-26(F)(1)) — significant political/calendar risk.

## Opportunities to evaluate

- **DDI pathway**: if the City Arborist determines a heritage or protected tree is dead, diseased, or an imminent hazard, removal is no-fee and 0% mitigation. Private arborist reports alone do not establish DDI — pursue the City Arborist letter early when condition is genuinely poor.
- **150% poor-condition rate** for heritage trees: City-Arborist-discretionary halving of the 300% mitigation if a qualified arborist documents poor condition and the City Arborist approves. Worth pursuing on declining heritage oaks.
- **Modified CRZ (MCRZ)** (ECM 3.5.2.B.4.b): City Arborist may reconfigure CRZ boundary when prior development blocked root growth, as long as total area equals standard CRZ and it stays inside the protection fence. Half/Quarter CRZ rules still apply.
- **Like-for-like existing impacts** (ECM 3.5.2.B.4.a): rebuilding within the footprint of existing Half- or Quarter-CRZ impacts is allowable if no deeper or wider — useful on infill with existing slabs/curbs within CRZ.
- **Elevated foundations within Half CRZ** (ECM 3.5.2.B.3): allowed with ≥ 4" air gap, natural-grade soil beneath, non-leaching barrier for concrete; cannot span the Quarter CRZ; footprint still counts toward the 50% impact ceiling.
- **Low-impact excavation** (ECM 3.5.2.B.2): hand digging or compressed-air ("air spade") permitted in restricted zones; significant roots (≥ 1.5" diameter) cannot be cut without City Arborist authorization.
- **Transplant** (ECM 3.5.2.B.5): City-Arborist-discretionary alternative to removal; requires qualified large-tree transplant arborist, fiscal surety, and 5-year hold before release.
- **Fee-in-lieu** (UFRF) at $200/caliper inch private, **$75/caliper inch for certified affordable developments** — meaningful savings on dense affordable projects, but only available when site is "unsuitable for planting" per City Arborist.
- **Wetland buffer 1:1 mitigation** (ECM 1.10.4(D)(3)): standard 150-ft wetland buffer can be reduced to 50-ft average via on-site in-kind mitigation — not an admin variance, a separate pathway.
- **ERI waiver** (LDC § 25-8-121(E), Form ECM 1.3.2 to wpderi@austintexas.gov): available before application; never granted if any wetland is on or within 150 ft.
- **AEC for landscape only** (ECM § 2.5.0): Alternative Equivalent Compliance for LDC § 25-2-1001 landscape requirements (Director of Planning). Does **not** apply to environmental requirements — don't conflate with CEF or SOS relief.

## Inputs needed from Phase 2

- **environmental.md** — CWQZ delineation, watershed classification (urban/suburban/water supply/BSZ), EARZ status, mapped CEFs and wetlands within 150 ft, slope analysis with any >15% area, Hill Country Roadway Corridor flag
- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — proposed LOC, building footprints, parking, grading limits, utility runs, drives; any tree symbology on concept plans (usually approximate)
- **zoning-pathway.md** — overlays that trigger additional tree rules (HCRC, Waterfront, BSZ), compatibility and setback constraints (drive prerequisite-variance analysis)
- **arborist field survey (if any)** — RPLS-certified survey with DBH, species, multi-stem stems, condition rating; otherwise flag as data gap requiring field work before site plan
- **aerial imagery + historic** — identify trees that may have appeared (now > 8") or been removed without permit since last survey
- **City Arborist Addendum (if any prior submittal)** — any enlarged-CRZ directives, prior MCRZ approvals, DDI letters

## Output structure

Standard discipline output shape per `references/phase3-disciplines.md`. Order findings: (1) heritage-tree CRZ conflicts with proposed footprint, (2) protected-tree removal exposure and mitigation cost band, (3) ESC phasing / scale / cut-fill compliance, (4) CEF and CWQZ buffer impacts, (5) SOS impervious-cover headroom (BSZ only), (6) HCRC native-replacement and 40% natural-area set-aside, (7) landscape and replacement-tree caliper budget, (8) data gaps requiring field survey.

## Severity heuristics

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| Heritage tree CRZ or Quarter CRZ overlaps proposed building footprint with no like-for-like existing impact | `significant` — likely LUC variance (if any stem ≥ 30") or admin variance + 300% mitigation; reshape massing |
| Heritage tree Half CRZ overlaps proposed impervious; >4" cut/fill required | `moderate` — workable via elevated foundation, MCRZ, or hardship review; quantify mitigation if reclassified as removal |
| Multiple protected trees (19"+) in proposed parking area | `moderate` — 100%/50% mitigation cost; consider angled parking or layout shift |
| Site in Barton Springs Zone with proposed impervious approaching or exceeding 15/20/25% SOS cap | `significant` — no variance pathway; redesign required unless small-lot or HB 1704 vested |
| Wetland CEF on or within 150 ft of site | `significant` — 150-ft buffer compresses envelope; ERI waiver unavailable; 1:1 mitigation pathway reduces to 50-ft avg if pursued |
| Slope > 15% on portions of site | `moderate` — ERI required; slope stabilization and ESC design uplift |
| Karst feature suspected over EARZ | `moderate` to `significant` — Licensed Professional Geoscientist karst survey + 150–300 ft catchment buffer |
| LOC > 25 ac or any LOC in BSZ — no phased ESC plan budgeted | `moderate` — schedule impact, EPM designation, 18-month BSZ revegetation cap |
| Tree survey absent or > 5 years old | `data-gap` — RPLS field survey required before reliable Phase 3 findings; assume worst case in interim |
| Standard erosion controls suffice (low slope, urban watershed, contained drainage, < 25 ac LOC) | `note` |
| Hill Country Roadway Corridor applies (≤ 1,000 ft of one of the 5 corridor roadways) | `moderate` — 40% natural-area set-aside is a hard massing constraint; native-replacement cost |
| Heritage tree with at least one stem ≥ 30" proposed for any impact that would reclassify as removal | `significant` — LUC + EC hearing track adds 4–8 months and public risk |

## Common pitfalls

- Inferring heritage status from canopy in aerial imagery — DBH at 4.5 ft above natural grade is the only valid measure; field survey by RPLS is the precondition.
- Treating only the building footprint as the impact line — Austin measures impacts at the line of excavation, which extends behind curbs, into form bracing, and through scaffolding swing (ECM 3.5.2.A.3).
- Forgetting the Quarter CRZ. The 50% rule is the famous one, but the Quarter-CRZ prohibition on any cut/fill of any depth (ECM 3.5.2.A.1) is the one that most often kills proposed sidewalks, curbs, and utility runs near heritage oaks.
- Assuming a 1.5x CRZ automatically applies to Post Oaks. Enlargement is City-Arborist-discretionary and only governs if directed in writing — but assume the enlarged radius for diligence on any Post Oak.
- Citing ECM 3.5.3 or Appendix P-6 — both repealed by Rule R161-22.16 (December 2022); the operative sections are ECM 3.5.2.A.2 (crown), ECM 3.5.2.A.3 (construction impacts), and ECM 3.5.2.B.1 (remedial tree care). The ECM 3.6.2 standard plan note still contains stale cross-references.
- Conflating BSZ and EARZ. They overlap but are distinct: a site may be in one and not the other; SOS impervious caps key on watershed + zone combination.
- Conflating ECM 2.5.0 AEC with environmental relief. AEC covers landscape (LDC § 25-2-1001) only; CEF buffers, CWQZ, SOS impervious, and wetland setbacks have their own pathways.
- Counting elevated-foundation soil-preserved areas as "preserved" in the 50% CRZ calculation. ECM 3.5.2.B.3 explicitly counts them as impacts.
- Underestimating prerequisite-variance time (LDC § 25-8-646). The applicant must seek and be denied every other applicable variance/waiver/AEC before requesting heritage removal — this cannot be parallelized with the heritage variance itself.
- Forgetting that mitigation-exempt invasive species still require a removal permit — no mitigation fee, but the permit gate remains.
- Ignoring CRZs of ROW and off-site trees that reach into the LOC. They are subject to the same 50% / Half / Quarter CRZ rules as on-site trees (ECM 3.5.2.A applied via ECM 3.3.2.A.1).
- Tree survey older than 5 years. ECM 3.3.2.A invalidates surveys past 5 years from survey date; re-survey before relying on it for protected/heritage determinations.
- Confusing the SOS Ordinance impervious cap with general BSZ rules. The SOS caps (LDC § 25-8-514) have no variance pathway (LDC § 25-8-515) — there is no design-around. Verify watershed + recharge/contributing zone combination at the parcel level.
- Treating the Erosion Impact Zone (EIZ) around an existing building as a basis for removing a heritage or protected tree. EIZ proximity is not an approved removal criterion under LDC § 25-8-624(A).

    22→
    23→## Regulatory pathway
    24→
    25→| Pathway | Decision body | Typical timeline | When triggered |
    26→|---|---|---|---|
    27→| Floodplain Development Permit | WPD / DSD floodplain administrator | concurrent with site plan | Any development in or affecting the 100-yr or 25-yr floodplain |
    28→| CLOMC / CLOMR (FEMA) | FEMA + COA acknowledgment | 6–12 months for review; CLOMC acknowledgment required **before preliminary plan or site plan permit** | Pre-construction map revision (e.g. fill, channel work that alters FEMA SFHA) |
    29→| LOMR (FEMA) | FEMA | 6–12 months; final acceptance required **before CO** | Post-construction map revision |
    30→| Administrative environmental variance (LDC § 25-8-42) | WPD Director, no hearing | weeks; ECM 1.3.3 form required | Enumerated items only: cut/fill 4–8 ft in DDZ, CEF buffer reduction, interbasin diversion below threshold, etc. |
    31→| LUC environmental variance (LDC § 25-8-41) | Land Use Commission after Environmental Commission recommendation | 3–6 months | Cut/fill >8 ft, cut/fill in DWPZ, CWQZ encroachment, floodplain modification with adverse impact, slopes >15%, within 100 ft of classified waterway |
    32→| Floodplain encroachment variance (LDC § 25-7-92) | Council (or LUC under some scenarios) | 6+ months | Buildings or parking in 25-yr or 100-yr floodplain not covered by §§ 25-7-93 / 25-7-96 exceptions |
    33→| Floodway encroachment variance (LDC § 25-12-54) | Council | 6+ months; **cannot be granted if any flood-level rise results** (§ 25-12-54(F)(5)) | Any work in COA 25-yr floodplain (floodway) with rise |
    34→| Save Our Springs (Article 13) | **No variance available** | — | Any project in the Barton Springs Zone — SOS is inviolable |
    35→
    36→Project file must show CLOMC acknowledgment letter from FEMA **before** preliminary plan / site plan permit issues; LOMC acknowledgment **before** final acceptance / BP; LOMR final acceptance **before** CO.
    37→
    38→## Constraints to evaluate
    39→
    40→### Mapping & delineation
    41→
    42→- **Two floodplains, not one.** Always map both the FEMA SFHA (copy directly from current FIRM shapefile per DCM 1.2.6.B — do not re-delineate to onsite topo) and the COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain (derived from approved City hydraulic models intersected with site topo). For pre-feasibility, assume the COA boundary is larger than FEMA wherever Atlas 14 has been applied.
    43→- **Hydraulic study trigger:** any creek, channel, or area of concentrated flow with ≥64 acres contributing drainage area requires a COA floodplain delineation (DCM 1.2.6.A.1). Below 64 acres, no COA floodplain is defined unless City or FEMA already mapped it.
    44→- **Preliminary FIRM in process?** Check whether the watershed has a pending FEMA restudy. Using an effective FIRM when a preliminary is published is a common deficiency.
    45→
    46→### Floodway (COA 25-yr) — the hardest constraint
    47→
    48→- **0.00-ft rise standard.** Any encroachment in the COA 25-yr floodplain requires PE-certified zero rise, delivered as a **separate** sealed letter (LDC § 25-12-54(D)(11)) — not just the WSE comparison table.
    49→- **Council cannot grant variance for floodway encroachment if any rise would result** (LDC § 25-12-54(F)(5)). Buildings, parking, or fill in the floodway with rise are categorically infeasible — design must avoid the floodway.
    50→
    51→### 100-yr floodplain — buildings & parking
    52→
    53→- Buildings and parking are prohibited in both 25-yr and 100-yr floodplains absent an enumerated exception (§ 25-7-93 for 100-yr; § 25-7-96 for 25-yr) or a Council encroachment variance (§ 25-7-92(C)) finding all seven criteria.
    54→- **§ 25-7-93 exception conditions:** ≥2 ft above 100-yr WSE, volume compensation (compensatory storage), no additional adverse impact. Five enumerated categories (e.g. parking <5,000 sq ft with director "no adverse effect" determination).
    55→- **Finished floor elevation:** minimum 2-ft freeboard above design flood elevation (LDC § 25-12-53(C)(1)). Design flood elevation = higher of Atlas 14 100-yr or FEMA 500-yr WSEL.
    56→- **Safe access:** building access at or above 1 ft above DFE, equivalent to the Regulatory Flood Datum (LDC § 25-12-53(C)(4)(a)).
    57→- **ASCE 24-14 certification** required for structures in the floodplain — separate engineer-sealed letter per structure type (retaining walls, fill, culverts, bridges, piers, fencing, buildings).
    58→- **Below-grade structures, MEP equipment elevation, flood openings for enclosed areas, safe refuge space** — all separately addressed by LDC § 25-12-53.
    59→- **Post-construction elevation certificate** (FEMA Form 086-0-33) by licensed surveyor — required prior to CO.
    60→
    61→### Floodplain modification
    62→
    63→- Any fill, grading, or channel work in the regulatory floodplain triggers LDC § 25-8-263 modification analysis: no-rise WSE, no increase in downstream peak flows, no loss of floodplain storage. WSE comparison table for 2/10/25/100-yr storms required.
    64→- **Functional Assessment of Floodplain Health (FAFH)** per ECM 1.7.4 + Appendix X required for modifications. Zone-specific.
    65→- **Restoration ratios (ECM 1.7.5):** Outside CWQZ (Zone 1): 2:1 / 3:1 / 4:1 for Poor / Fair / Good-or-Excellent condition (Good+ requires LUC variance). Inside CWQZ (Zone 2): 4:1 / 6:1 / 8:1 — all require LUC variance.
    66→- **Note re ECM cross-reference:** ECM § 1.7.1 still references the repealed § 25-8-364; current governing provision is LDC § 25-8-263.
    67→
    68→### Critical Water Quality Zone (CWQZ) — the buffer system
    69→
    70→- **Suburban watersheds — fixed buffer widths from centerline:** 100 ft (minor, 64–320 ac); 200 ft (intermediate, 320–640 ac); 300 ft (major, >640 ac). Buffer averaging permitted per ECM 1.5.2.D.
    71→- **CWQZ is largely undevelopable.** Most encroachments require an LUC variance under the enhanced § 25-8-41(B) standard (must prevent reasonable, economic use of the **entire** property).
    72→- Ponds, fill, retaining walls, parking, buildings, and spray irrigation are prohibited in CWQZ outright in most cases. Trails permitted at ≥50 ft from CEF edge under § 25-8-281(C)(3) without variance.
    73→- WQTZ is less restrictive but still constrains pond siting and stormwater controls.
    74→
    75→### Erosion Hazard Zone (EHZ)
    76→
    77→- EHZ analysis triggered when development is within 100 ft of a classified waterway centerline (≥64 acres drainage) or 200 ft of the Colorado River OHWM downstream of Longhorn Dam (LDC § 25-7-32(C)).
    78→- Seven-step DCM Appendix E procedure: meander belt delineation (if sinuosity ≥1.2), bankfull geometry, incision depth, side slope projections to 100 ft max (steep terrain) or 20 ft min setback from tops of bank.
    79→- WPD/ERM concurrence on protective works required.
    80→
    81→### Critical Environmental Features (CEFs)
    82→
    83→- 150-ft standard setback (LDC § 25-8-281). Reduction requires administrative variance under § 25-8-42(B)(5) only if all CEF characteristics can be preserved.
    84→- Point recharge features (caves, sinkholes) — admin variance minimum 50 ft, with 12 ECM 1.10.4.B conditions precluding further reduction.
    85→- Canyon rimrock / bluff admin variance unavailable on upslope grade ≥15% or average grade ≥10% — LUC variance required.
    86→- Cave footprint assumption: 300 ft from entrance when subsurface extent unmapped (ECM 1.10.3.C).
    87→
    88→### Cut / fill grading limits
    89→
    90→- **4-ft standard limit** in non-urban watersheds (LDC §§ 25-8-341 / 25-8-342); urban watersheds exempt.
    91→- **8-ft administrative variance maximum** in the Desired Development Zone (DDZ); ECM 1.3.3 form. Unavailable on slopes >15% or within 100 ft of a classified waterway, or anywhere in the Drinking Water Protection Zone (DWPZ — Barton Springs Zone, Barton Creek watershed, all water supply rural and suburban watersheds), except for public primary/secondary educational facilities.
    92→- **>8 ft cut/fill** anywhere, or **any** cut/fill above 4 ft in DWPZ: LUC variance under § 25-8-41 required.
    93→- **Cover sheet citation watch:** flag any reference to "§ 25-8-42(B)(6)" — that subsection was renumbered to (B)(7) by Ord. No. 20221027-045 (effective 2022-11-07).
    94→
    95→### Watershed impervious cover limits
    96→
    97→- **Urban IC:** set by zoning code (LDC § 25-2-492); gross site area; no Q-1/Q-2 tables.
    98→- **Suburban IC:** 45–80% gross site area depending on use type and whether transfer of development intensity is used (LDC § 25-8-392).
    99→- **Barton Springs Zone IC:** 15% over EARZ/recharge; 20% Barton Creek contributing zone; 25% remainder of BSZ contributing zone (net site area; LDC § 25-8-514). **No variance available — Save Our Springs (Article 13).**
   100→- **Interbasin diversion threshold:** lesser of 20% of gross site area or 1 acre (LDC § 25-8-365). Above this, admin variance via § 25-8-42(B)(9) or LUC variance.
   101→
   102→### Drainage easement
   103→
   104→- Regulatory 100-yr floodplain must be **entirely contained** within a drainage easement on the plat. Easement dedication variances available at LDC § 25-7-152(E) for full-purpose city limits only.
   105→
   106→## Opportunities to evaluate
   107→
   108→- **Redevelopment Exception (LDC §§ 25-8-25 / -26 / -27).** Existing developed sites in Urban or Suburban watersheds may retain existing impervious cover that exceeds current limits. Substantive eligibility requires water quality treatment for the full 0.5" / 1.0" capture and other procedural conditions. Often decisive for infill projects.
   109→- **CLOMR / LOMR.** Where the FEMA boundary is conservative relative to actual topography, a no-rise modification + LOMR can remove parts of the parcel from SFHA, unlocking buildable area. Budget 6–12 months for FEMA review and stage CLOMC acknowledgment before site plan permit.
   110→- **Compensatory storage / fill in 100-yr (non-floodway).** Cut/fill to raise pad elevation can work in the 100-yr floodplain (outside the floodway) with proper no-rise + volume compensation + 2-ft freeboard. Not available in floodway.
   111→- **Buffer averaging in CWQZ (ECM 1.5.2.D).** Suburban watersheds allow buffer width averaging so long as total area is preserved — can free up usable land while still meeting CWQZ obligations.
   112→- **Atlas 14 watershed amendment status.** Watersheds not yet updated to Atlas 14 may still produce smaller COA boundaries than updated neighbors. Verify status; the boundary you map at concept may grow before site plan.
   113→- **Conservation easements / parkland dedication.** Floodplain-encumbered area unsuitable for development can satisfy parkland dedication or conservation easement obligations, potentially yielding fee credits.
   114→- **Public-facility cut/fill pathway.** Public primary/secondary educational facilities have a unique exemption to the DWPZ ban on cut/fill admin variances (AISD Interlocal Agreement § 10.2.4.1 / LDC § 25-2-835).
   115→- **TIRZ / Waller Creek tunnel exception.** Sites discharging directly to Lady Bird Lake, Lake Travis, Lake Austin, the Colorado River, or Waller Creek below the tunnel inlet within the TIRZ are exempt from no-increased-peak-flow-rate requirements (DCM 1.2.2.F).
   116→- **ECM 1.7.3 floodplain-modification exemptions** from restoration ratios: (A) public health/safety necessity (with WPD Director letter); (B) significant demonstrable environmental benefit; (C) conditionally-allowed CWQZ development. Useful when restoration ratios would otherwise make a project infeasible.
   117→
   118→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
   119→
   120→- **environmental.md** — FEMA flood zone determination, FIRM panel number + effective date, COA fully-developed floodplain extent, CWQZ / WQTZ / EHZ overlay results, classified waterway proximity, EARZ status, Barton Springs Zone status, CEF inventory from ERI or GIS, watershed classification (Urban / Suburban / Water Supply Suburban / Water Supply Rural / Barton Springs Zone), Atlas 14 amendment status for the watershed.
   121→- **property-records.md** — recorded drainage easements, plat conditions referencing flood/drainage, prior CLOMR/LOMR letters, prior environmental or floodplain variance approvals (check expiration under LDC § 25-1-217 — variances expire 1 year after effective date unless associated with an approved plan).
   122→- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — proposed grading depths, building footprint relative to mapped floodplain boundaries, proposed FFE, pond locations (water quality + detention), driveway/parking layout relative to CWQZ and EHZ, proposed disturbance area relative to CEF buffers.
   123→- **adjacent-context.md** — upstream/downstream conditions for no-adverse-impact framing; nearby preliminary FIRMs in process.
   124→
   125→## Output structure
   126→
   127→Standard discipline output shape. See `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.
   128→
   129→## Severity heuristics
   130→
   131→| Finding | Severity |
   132→|---|---|
   133→| Building footprint or parking within COA 25-yr floodplain (floodway) | `significant` — 0.00-ft rise required; Council variance unavailable if any rise results |
   134→| Project in Barton Springs Zone exceeding 15% IC (or 20% / 25% per sub-zone) | `significant` — SOS Article 13, no variance available |
   135→| Building footprint within FEMA SFHA + COA 100-yr, freeboard + compensatory storage achievable | `moderate` |
   136→| Building or parking within FEMA SFHA but outside COA fully-developed boundary, freeboard achievable | `moderate` — § 25-7-93 exception pathway likely |
   137→| COA fully-developed 100-yr floodplain materially larger than FEMA SFHA, encroaches on developable area | `moderate` to `significant` depending on coverage |
   138→| Site within 100 ft of classified waterway centerline, cut/fill needed >4 ft | `moderate` — administrative variance unavailable; LUC variance required |
   139→| CWQZ encroachment proposed for parking, pond, or building | `significant` — enhanced § 25-8-41(B) standard (must prevent reasonable economic use of entire property) |
   140→| EHZ overlaps proposed disturbance | `moderate` — analysis required; protective works concurrence with WPD/ERM |
   141→| CEF setback reduction needed for non-wetland CEF | `moderate` — admin variance pathway via ECM 1.3.3 |
   142→| Cut/fill 4–8 ft in DDZ, slopes <15%, >100 ft from classified waterway | `moderate` — admin variance available |
   143→| Cut/fill >8 ft anywhere, or cut/fill in DWPZ | `significant` — LUC variance only; not available in BSZ for cut/fill on slopes >15% |
   144→| Watershed has pending preliminary FIRM (effective FIRM in transition) | `moderate` — boundary may grow before site plan; design to preliminary |
   145→| Floodplain study not yet performed for ≥64-acre waterway on or adjacent to site | `moderate` — Phase 3 cannot finalize FP boundary without it |
   146→| Parcel entirely outside FEMA SFHA, COA 100-yr, CWQZ, EHZ, and CEF buffers | `note` |
   147→| LOMA / LOMR pathway available for portion of parcel | `opportunity` |
   148→| Redevelopment Exception eligibility for IC | `opportunity` |
   149→| Buffer averaging in CWQZ unlocks developable area while preserving total buffer | `opportunity` |
   150→| TIRZ / Waller Creek tunnel discharge exception applies | `opportunity` |
   151→
   152→## Common pitfalls
   153→
   154→- **Citing only FEMA SFHA.** The COA fully-developed floodplain is broader in Atlas 14 watersheds — design only to FEMA and you will land in COA-floodplain encroachment at site plan review.
   155→- **Treating COA 25-yr as a "minor" boundary.** The COA 25-yr floodplain **is** the COA floodway. 0.00-ft rise is required; Council cannot grant variance if any rise results. It is the hardest line on the map.
   156→- **Re-delineating FEMA boundary to onsite topo.** FEMA must be copied directly from the FIRM panel shapefile. Re-delineating is a deficiency signature.
   157→- **COA boundary matching FEMA exactly.** Indicates the engineer used FEMA data rather than the City's regulatory hydraulic model — also a violation signature.
   158→- **Stale code citations.** Cover sheet referencing "§ 25-8-42(B)(6)" for cut/fill admin variance (renumbered to (B)(7) in 2022); plans or variance letters citing repealed §§ 25-8-691 through 25-8-696 for notification requirements (repealed 2022-11-07); ECM § 1.7.1 cross-reference to repealed § 25-8-364 (now § 25-8-263).
   159→- **Assuming compensatory storage anywhere.** Volume compensation works for fill in the 100-yr floodplain outside the floodway; it does **not** create a pathway through the floodway.
   160→- **Conflating EHZ with CWQZ.** Different boundaries, different rules. The EHZ may extend beyond the CWQZ in steep terrain (up to 100-ft setback) or be contained within it.
   161→- **Missing the 64-acre threshold.** Below 64 acres of contributing drainage area, no COA floodplain is required to be delineated — but if City or FEMA has already mapped one, it still applies.
   162→- **Missing the Atlas 14 watershed status check.** Watersheds updated post-2019-11-25 require Atlas 14 rainfall (Rule R161-20.01); older models in non-updated watersheds will be rejected for new floodplain studies.
   163→- **Assuming variance pathways exist in the Barton Springs Zone.** Save Our Springs (Article 13) cannot be varied — not by admin variance, not by LUC variance, not by Council.
   164→- **Variance expiration.** Variances expire 1 year after effective date (LDC § 25-1-217) unless a plan/permit application was timely filed. Old approval letters on a parcel may already be void.
   165→- **Drainage easement scope.** The regulatory 100-yr floodplain must be **entirely contained** within a drainage easement on the plat — a partial easement is a deficiency.
   166→- **CLOMC timing.** FEMA CLOMC acknowledgment letter must be in the project file **before** preliminary plan or site plan permit issues — not after. Budget 6–12 months.
   167→- **PE no-rise certification format.** Floodway no-rise must be a **separate** PE-sealed letter (LDC § 25-12-54(D)(11)), not implied by the WSE comparison table.
   168→- **ASCE 24-14 letters.** One per structure type in the floodplain — bridges, culverts, retaining walls, structural fill, piers, fencing, buildings. A single combined letter is a common deficiency.
   169→
