- Look up each frontage in the ASMP Street Network Table (`atd.knack.com/asmp`). Document Street Level (0–5) and target half-width.
  - Level 0 = alleys; Level 1 = local/residential collectors; Level 2 = collectors; Level 3 = minor/major arterials; Level 4 = principal/major arterials; Level 5 = TxDOT freeways/interstates.
- Compute the **dedication delta** (future half-width minus existing half-width). Multiply by frontage length to get area lost. Flag if delta > 10 ft on any frontage or if total area lost > 10% of gross site.
- Dedication is **roughly proportionate**; LDC § 25-6-23 requires a City-issued written proportionality determination signed by a City-retained PE before approval. Applicant-prepared SIF worksheets do not satisfy this requirement. Director may require less than full ASMP width but only via this memo.
- Dedication is by recorded **street deed** (metes + bounds + surveyor-sealed sketch, processed through City Legal) or, where ROW is held as easement only, by plat. Recordation must precede site plan approval; instrument number must appear on plan callouts.
- **TxDOT frontages (IH-35, US-290, SH-71, Parmer Lane, etc.)** carry long-term 400-ft ROW needs (200 ft from centerline). Either reserve up to 200 ft or obtain a TxDOT no-additional-dedication letter (LDC § 25-6-54(C)). TxDOT Approval Block required on the cover sheet when any work touches TxDOT ROW.
- **Orange Line corridor**: up to 65 ft from centerline (130 ft total) reservation may apply. Streets to flag include Guadalupe, Lavaca, Congress Ave. Not codified in Bureau — verify against Project Connect System Plan map.
- **Bicycle Priority Network**: streets on this network require All Ages and Abilities (AAA) facilities (Protected Bike Lanes, Shared Use Paths, or Neighborhood Bikeways per TCM 5.1.4); additional ROW beyond standard roadway width may be required.
- **Waiver**: LDC § 25-6-81 — formal written waiver required if full dedication is infeasible; available when ≥ 15% of property is subject to ROW reservation. An informal "infeasible" note on plans does **not** satisfy. ATD usually conditions waiver on a recorded alternative easement (sidewalk or public access).
- **IC math**: ROW pavement counts as IC; sidewalks in ROW or public easement are excluded (LDC § 25-8-63(C)(1)). On Hill Country Roadway sites, ROW > 60 ft from centerline counts in IC denominator (LDC § 25-2-1127), and 40% natural area is measured excluding dedicated ROW (LDC § 25-2-1025).

### TIA threshold and likely findings

- Threshold uses **unadjusted ITE daily trips** — no pass-by, internal capture, or TDM reductions for threshold determination. Only existing on-site occupied uses with documented occupancy may be subtracted.
- < 2,000 trips: no study, but sub-threshold mitigation (sidewalks, signals, traffic calming, bike lanes, RRFB/PHB, urban trails, ROW, TDM) within ¼ mile (or ¾ mile to schools/bus stops/major roads) can still be required under LDC § 25-6-101(B).
- 2,000–4,999 trips: **Transportation Assessment + TDM Plan** (LDC § 25-6-113; TCM 10.2.1).
- ≥ 5,000 trips: **Full TIA + TDM Plan**.
- All TIA work requires a **TDS-approved scope** signed by both the applicant's consultant and the TDS Lead Development Review Engineer *before* the study starts (TIA Guidelines § 4.3.2). Studies prepared without an approved scope will not be reviewed.
- Approved TIAs are valid **5 years** from final memo date or assumed build-out, whichever is earlier (TCM 10.4.3). Plan trip-budgeting accordingly.
- **TIA Compliance Letter** is a separate document from the TIA itself; if a prior TIA exists, expect a TIA Tracking Table on the cover sheet showing allowed/used/remaining VTDs and a 7-element compliance letter.
- **NTA** triggers when project accesses a non-arterial street with ≥ 50% SF-5+ frontage within 1,500 ft AND adds ≥ 300 net new daily trips (or is a public K-12). TDS writes the memo; applicant submits 24-hr tube counts.
- **Table 10-6** (TCM 10.4.4) sets nexus standards for required mitigations by category and study type — review before committing to off-site work.
- **Fiscal surety** under LDC § 25-1-112 must be posted before site plan approval for any unbuilt TIA-required improvements; below-market cost estimates without director approval will be rejected.

### Driveway and access management

- **Driveway type by use + street level** (TCM 7.3.1–7.3.2): Type I (residential) is **prohibited on ASMP Level 3 or 4 streets** regardless of use. Multi-family > 4 units requires Type II.
- **Max driveway width** (TCM 7.5.1.2, Table 7-2): Level 1 typical 20 ft (industrial 25 ft); Level 2 w/ 3-lane fire access 25 ft; high-capacity driveway serving a garage capped at 32 ft. Other Level 2/3/4 widths: verify against current TCM (Bureau data incomplete).
- **Driveway count per frontage** is capped; **opposing-driveway offset** rules can force right-in/right-out only.
- **Spacing minimums** from intersections, adjacent driveways, drainage inlets — confirm via TCM 7.6. Throat storage length per land use.
- **Joint-use driveway** requires a recorded easement with maintenance assigned (TCM 7.6.4) — built into the title package.
- **Hill Country Roadway** corridors (Loop 360 US-290W to US-183; RM 620 SH-71 to Anderson Mill; RM 2222 Highland Hills to RM 620; RM 2244 Loop 360 to SH-71; Southwest Parkway) impose extra access-spacing, grade, curve, and sight-distance restrictions (covered under guide 31).
- **Curb return radii** per TCM Table 7-1; downtown / ERC / UNO / NBG have overlay-specific values.

### Scenic Roadway constraints

- **Scenic Roadway Sign District** (LDC § 25-10-81(3); LDC § 25-10-124) — applies to land within **1,000 ft of a Hill Country Roadway corridor** OR **200 ft of any of the 23 Scenic Roadways** enumerated in LDC § 25-10-7 (e.g., Barton Springs Rd, Lake Austin Blvd, MoPac, Loop 360, RM 2222, RM 2244, William Cannon, Riverside Dr, SH 130). Governs sign size, height, lighting, setback.
- Historic and expressway sign districts override scenic per LDC § 25-10-82.
- Note: the user prompt referenced LDC § 25-2-871 (scenic roadway). The bureau guides cite § 25-10-7 / § 25-10-81 / § 25-10-124 for the **sign district**, and Hill Country Roadway development standards at LDC § 25-2-1025 / § 25-2-1127 for the *development* envelope. Confirm the controlling section against current code before drafting findings.
- For **Hill Country Roadway** sites the more material development constraints are the 40% natural-area requirement (excluding dedicated ROW; LDC § 25-2-1025), grade/cut-fill limits along the corridor, and ROW > 60 ft from centerline counting in IC denominator (LDC § 25-2-1127).

### Sidewalk, transit, and bike obligations

- **Sidewalk required on every street frontage** unless approved fee-in-lieu (LDC § 25-6-354; TCM 4.1.6). Minimum clear widths: Level 1 = 5 ft; Level 2 = 6 ft (constrained 5 ft w/ approval). Downtown Great Streets = 18 ft total streetscape zone; Core Transit Corridors = 15 ft total zone.
- **Bicycle facilities** on the ASMP Bicycle Priority Network must be AAA-grade (Protected Bike Lane, Shared Use Path, or Neighborhood Bikeway per TCM 5.1.4). Planting-zone width: 8 ft (Level 2–3 recommended), 10 ft (Level 4 recommended), 6.5 ft constrained.
- **Bus stop integration**: CapMetro coordination required where a stop fronts the site; floating bus stop platforms (where bike lane runs behind the stop) carry specific TCM dimensions.
- **Bicycle parking** required citywide under LDC § 25-6-477 regardless of motor-vehicle parking; short-term + long-term split by use; TOD overlays add requirements.
- **Accessible parking** is the only motor-vehicle parking minimum that survived the November 2023 elimination of general parking minimums (LDC §§ 25-6-471(B), 25-6-474(A)(3)). Calculated at 100% Appendix A → Building Code table; van-accessible 1 per 6 (IBC 1106.5).

### Street Impact Fees

- Applies to virtually all building-permit development (LDC § 25-6-662). Independent of TIA — a TIA waiver does *not* waive SIF.
- **Assessed** at plat or building permit application; **collected** at building permit issuance (LDC § 25-6-663(B)). Plan notes stating SIF is paid at site plan approval are incorrect.
- Process: applicant submits SIF Estimator Worksheet via ATD KNACK portal → TDS Engineering issues SIF Formal Calculation Memo → payment at each building permit.
- SIF can be used as the proportionality measure under § 25-6-23.
- Offset agreements available under § 25-6-669 for developer-constructed Roadway Capacity Plan improvements.
- Required cover-sheet note: *"Development of structures that require a building permit within this Site Plan, or revisions thereof, are required to comply with the City of Austin Street Impact Fee Ordinances, as applicable, and must be paid upon completion of the building permit plan review for each building. Reference: LDC 25-6-662."*

## Opportunities to evaluate

- **TIA-driven public improvements**: TIAs frequently identify intersection improvements that the city or TxDOT may co-fund or accelerate; coordinate with TDS during scoping.
- **Sub-threshold projects can structure SIF offsets** by constructing on-Roadway-Capacity-Plan improvements (LDC § 25-6-669) rather than paying full SIF.
- **Fee-in-lieu of sidewalk** under LDC § 25-6-354 / TCM 4.1.6 — useful where physical sidewalk install conflicts with trees, drainage, or existing utilities.
- **TIA waiver** under LDC § 25-6-117 — does not waive mitigation, but can streamline timeline if scope is genuinely limited.
- **Cross-access / shared driveway** with neighboring sites reduces driveway count, can satisfy joint-use easement (TCM 7.6.4), and is preferred by ATD on arterials.
- **Regulating plan bonuses**: ERC, NBG, and TOD districts include reduced parking maxima and active-edge incentives that can be leveraged in concept design.
- **Project Connect / ETOD proximity** — ETOD-zoned sites (LDC § 25-2-182) carry density bonuses tied to transit corridor presence; verify against ETOD subdistrict layer.

## Inputs needed from Phase 2

- **transportation.md** — for each street frontage: existing ROW width (survey), ASMP Street Level + target half-width, Bicycle Priority Network status, AADT (TxDOT for state-maintained), functional class, posted speed, Project Connect / scenic / Hill Country flags.
- **property-records.md** — recorded street deeds, existing access easements, joint-use driveway easements, vacated street documentation, prior ROW dedication instrument numbers.
- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — proposed land use mix (with ITE codes), gross square footage / unit counts, proposed driveway locations + count, design vehicle (WB-50 vs. WB-62), parking garage proposed (high-capacity driveway?).
- **zoning / overlays** — regulating plan membership (NBG, ERC, MLK TOD, Plaza Saltillo, Lamar/Justin Lane), Hill Country Roadway corridor flag, Scenic Roadway flag, UNO / NCCD overlays, ETOD subdistrict.
- **adjacent_context** (surveyor `property_profile` + `adjacent_context`) — abutting ASMP/AMTP segments, neighbor zoning for NTA frontage test.

## Output structure

Standard discipline output shape; cite `references/phase3-disciplines.md`.

## Severity heuristics

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| Future ROW dedication consumes > 10% of gross site OR > 15% of any one frontage's developable depth | `significant` |
| Project triggers Full TIA (≥ 5,000 unadjusted trips) with likely off-site mitigation obligations | `significant` |
| TxDOT frontage with unresolved 200-ft long-term ROW reservation (IH-35, US-290, SH-71, Parmer) | `significant` |
| Orange Line / Project Connect corridor reservation plausibly applies (Guadalupe, Lavaca, Congress) | `significant` (flag for human verification) |
| Project triggers Transportation Assessment (2,000–4,999 trips) with TDM Plan | `moderate` to `significant` |
| Proposed driveway location conflicts with TCM 7.6 spacing or Type I prohibited on Level 3/4 | `moderate` |
| NTA likely triggered (≥ 300 net new trips + residential frontage) | `moderate` |
| Hill Country Roadway corridor frontage (Loop 360, RM 620/2222/2244, SW Parkway) | `moderate` |
| Site within 200 ft of a § 25-10-7 Scenic Roadway (sign + character constraints) | `moderate` |
| Bicycle Priority Network frontage requiring AAA facility ROW beyond standard | `moderate` |
| Site requires sidewalk fee-in-lieu or shared-access agreement | `note` to `moderate` |
| Adequate existing ROW + sub-2,000-trip use + no overlay frontage | `note` |

## Common pitfalls

- **Citing existing ROW instead of future ASMP ROW** when sizing setbacks or area calculations. The legal dedication obligation is from centerline to ASMP target half-width, not from the existing property line.
- **Applying pass-by, internal-capture, or TDM reductions to TIA threshold trips.** Threshold determination uses *unadjusted* ITE rates only. Reductions can be claimed in the TIA itself, never in the determination.
- **Treating SIF as paid at site plan approval.** SIF is **collected at building permit issuance** per LDC § 25-6-663(B). Cover sheet notes asserting otherwise are a checklist deficiency.
- **Submitting applicant-engineer SIF worksheet as the § 25-6-23 proportionality determination.** The determination must be a City-issued memo signed by a City-retained PE.
- **Starting TIA work before TDS-signed scope.** Studies prepared before scope approval will not be reviewed.
- **Confusing functional class with jurisdictional ownership.** ASMP Level 5 = TxDOT; streets prefixed IH/US/SH = TxDOT-maintained. ASMP Level 4 includes service roads/ramps, which surveyor data flags as *not* highways.
- **Missing Scenic Roadway Sign District** — applies up to 200 ft from any of 23 named roadways and 1,000 ft from Hill Country Roadway corridors. Easy to miss because the *sign* district lives in Chapter 25-10 rather than the transportation chapter.
- **Confusing Scenic Roadway sign rules (Ch. 25-10) with Hill Country Roadway development rules (LDC §§ 25-2-1025, 25-2-1127).** Different overlays, different impacts — site can be in one but not the other.
- **Citing 65 ft / 130 ft Orange Line reservation as a Bureau-codified requirement.** It is not in TCM or LDC; it comes from the Project Connect System Plan map. Always flag for external verification.
- **Type I driveway proposed on a Level 3 or Level 4 street.** Always prohibited regardless of use (TCM 7.3.1.C).
- **Plat used to dedicate easements** (sidewalk, sight distance, public access). Plat approval is not acceptance of dedication (LDC § 30-2-39); separate easement instruments using City templates are required.
- **Assuming general motor-vehicle parking minimums still apply.** Austin eliminated minimums in November 2023; only accessible parking + bicycle parking minimums survive.
- **Ignoring the 5-year TIA validity window.** Older TIAs need TDS written confirmation of continued validity or an updated study (TCM 10.4.3).

1→# Water & Wastewater Planning Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Austin Water (AW) service availability for potable water, wastewater, and reclaimed water; tap sizing, capital recovery (impact) fees, Service Extension Requests (SERs); ETJ / MUD / WCID / private-utility complications; OSSF (septic) eligibility where no public main is reachable; reclaimed water mandatory-connection thresholds and Onsite Water Reuse System (OWRS) mandates. Bridges to fire (FWP) on fire-flow adequacy and to SDUF on rainwater/condensate reuse intersecting with stormwater.
     6→
     7→## Authoritative sources
     8→
     9→- Water/wastewater/reclaimed service area: Austin Water utility coverage = the AW "impact fee boundary" (UCM 2.2.1). Confirm against AW's GIS service-area layer; do not infer from full-purpose corporate limits alone.
    10→- Utility Criteria Manual (UCM) — primary design + procedural code for AW (UCM 2.x).
    11→- Land Development Code (LDC) Chapter 25-9 — Water and Wastewater Subchapter (SERs, impact fees, mandatory reclaimed connection).
    12→- Tap fees / capital recovery fees: LDC § 25-9-321 (impact fee authority) + AWU Water Impact Fee Ordinance No. 20111215-115 (fee schedule). Tap permit + inspection fees per UCM 2.6.1.
    13→- Service Extension Policy: LDC § 25-9-31 through § 25-9-41; UCM 2.2.
    14→- Reclaimed / OWRS: LDC § 25-9-412 (mandatory connection); LDC § 25-9-414 + City Code § 15-13-7 (OWRS mandate, effective April 1, 2024).
    15→- OSSF (septic) for parcels with no reachable public main: Austin City Code Chapter 15-5 (abandonment + within-corporate-limits OSSF); Travis County / Hays County / Williamson County permitting under TCEQ Chapter 285 in the ETJ.
    16→- Industrial Waste Control Program (Chapter 15-10) — applies when AW is wastewater provider and discharge is non-domestic.
    17→- Water Benchmarking Application (WBA/WBC): LDC § 25-9-413 (site plan submittal requirement).
    18→
    19→## Regulatory pathway
    20→
    21→| Action | Path / authority | Typical timing |
    22→|---|---|---|
    23→| Confirm service area + provider (AW vs MUD/WCID/CCN-holder) | AW GIS + PUC CCN map; LDC § 25-9-33(C)(2) | Day 0 (diligence) |
    24→| Service availability letter (water + WW) | AW; must be dated within 6 months of review | 4-8 weeks |
    25→| Pre-application meeting w/ AW for capacity questions | Informal; AWPE | 2-4 weeks lead |
    26→| Service Extension Request (SER) — if triggered | LDC § 25-9-33; AW Pipeline Engineering (AWPE) | 3-9 months; approved SER is NOT a capacity reservation (UCM 2.2.3(E)) |
    27→| WW SER multi-department review (AFD + Industrial Waste) | LDC § 25-9-33(C)(3), § 25-9-34(B) | Folded into SER timeline |
    28→| Water Benchmarking Application (WBA/WBC) | LDC § 25-9-413(A); at site plan submittal | Concurrent with site plan |
    29→| Large-development (GFA ≥ 250,000 SF) director consultation | LDC § 25-9-413(B) | Before site plan filing |
    30→| AULCC (utility coordination) review for ROW work | UCM 3.2.0 | Plan set delivered 2 weeks before meeting |
    31→| Reclaimed connection eligibility check (250 / 500 ft) | LDC § 25-9-412 | At concept; verify with AW Reclaimed Group |
    32→| OWRS engineering report + permit (if mandated) | City Code § 15-13-7 / -10 / -11 | Adds ~6-12 mo; PE-stamped O&M manual |
    33→| Tap permit issuance + capital recovery fee payment | LDC § 25-9-321; UCM 2.6.1 | At/before building permit |
    34→| OSSF permit (ETJ, where no public main within 100 ft) | TCEQ Chapter 285 via county | Soil eval + 30-90 days |
    35→| Easement recordation (if AW infrastructure outside ROW) | UCM 2.9.1.A.1-A.4; AWPE pre-recordation review | Before AW plan approval |
    36→
    37→## Constraints to evaluate
    38→
    39→### Service area + provider
    40→
    41→- **Is the parcel inside Austin Water's retail service area?** AW serves within its impact-fee boundary (UCM 2.2.1). Full-purpose annexation does not automatically mean AW is the retail provider. Common Austin-area alternatives:
    42→  - **Northtown MUD** (north Austin / Pflugerville fringe) — UCM 2.5.1.B requires its prior written approval before AW will sign anything.
    43→  - **Southwest Water / Mid-Tex** — west / southwest ETJ.
    44→  - **City of Manor** — eastern fringe.
    45→  - **WCIDs** — scattered (e.g., WCID 17 in westlake).
    46→- If a non-AW provider holds the CCN, expect a CCN release or transfer through PUC before AW can serve (LDC § 25-9-33(C)(2)). This adds 6-18 months and is not always achievable.
    47→- If site is **inside the ETJ**, design must still meet COA standards but Industrial Waste plans go directly to the IW office, not through DSD (UCM 2.5.1.F).
    48→
    49→### Capacity — water
    50→
    51→- AW does **not** publish reservation; an approved SER is "acknowledgment of intent to serve" only (UCM 2.2.3(E)).
    52→- **Pressure Concern Area** — administrative AW designation where existing infrastructure cannot maintain 20 psi residual at peak day + fire flow (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.d) or stays under 10 fps emergency velocity (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.c). Triggers a Water SER under LDC § 25-9-33(A)(3). Not mappable from public data — confirm via AW correspondence.
    53→- **Pressure zone** must be designated on the AW General Info Sheet; affects pump sizing on tall buildings.
    54→- Minimum public water main = 8 inches (UCM 2.9.2.A.4.a). Mains ≥24 inches are **transmission mains** (LDC § 25-9-32(15)) — no meter or fire-line tap permitted without a Director exception, even with an approved SER.
    55→- Fire flow per FPCM Table 507-1: 1,000 gpm floor for SF < 3,600 SF; 2,500-3,500 gpm typical for multifamily / commercial. The 1,000 gpm number is a floor, not a default.
    56→
    57→### Capacity — wastewater
    58→
    59→- **Wastewater Capacity Concern Area** — administrative AW designation; not codified or mapped publicly. Triggers a WW SER under LDC § 25-9-33(A)(3). Confirm via AW correspondence; do not assume capacity from a 5-year-old AW master-plan study.
    60→- **Living Unit Equivalent (LUE)** = 1 residential dwelling = 245 gpd average flow (UCM 2.9.4.A.1). Commercial flows are calculated separately (70 gpd/capita or case-by-case). LUE counts must reconcile to the approved SER; exceeding triggers an SER revision (LDC § 25-9-39(C)(3)).
    61→- **Wastewater interceptor** = ≥18 inches (LDC § 25-9-32(14)) — direct connections prohibited without Director exception.
    62→- **Service-connection ceiling**: UCM 2.9.4.G.3 prohibits direct service taps to any wastewater main >15 inches — applies to 16" and 17" mains even though they don't independently trigger the interceptor SER.
    63→- Gravity service is required where feasible (UCM 2.9.4.J); lift stations are disfavored. If the city main is a **force main**, a grinder station at the property line is required and distance from property line to a gravity main must be ≤200 ft (UCM 2.9.4.J.18).
    64→
    65→### SER triggers (LDC § 25-9-33(A))
    66→
    67→An SER is required when any of:
    68→1. Nearest accessible main is **>100 ft** from the property boundary.
    69→2. Proposed connection is to a transmission main (≥24") or interceptor (≥18").
    70→3. Existing main is unsuitable / insufficient (pressure concern, capacity concern, lot-line-crossing private piping, alley main connections, water meters on private lines, force-main extensions, public WW extension >100 ft, etc.).
    71→4. Service is from a decentralized WW system the Director recommends the City operate.
    72→
    73→Additional design-time triggers that may not strictly trigger an SER but constrain layout:
    74→- Wastewater direct service tap prohibited to any main >15" (UCM 2.9.4.G.3) — applies even where the LDC § 25-9-32(14) interceptor threshold (≥18") isn't met.
    75→- Water meters must be placed in public ROW or in an easement immediately adjacent to ROW; meters inside fences or on private lines are non-compliant (UCM 2.9.2.E.3).
    76→- Utility easements outside ROW: minimum 15 ft wide or 2× the infrastructure depth (flowline-to-grade), whichever is greater, with infrastructure centered (UCM 2.9.1.A.1).
    77→
    78→**SER carries an expiration**: 180 days from approval (post-April 2013, LDC § 25-9-39(C)) — extended by a pending or approved development application, indefinite for recorded-plat portions. SER amendment required for any change in lot configuration (re-plat, lot split, parcel merger), land use, or anticipated demand (LDC § 25-9-39(C)(3)) — even if LUE count is unchanged.
    79→
    80→**SER ≠ capacity reservation** (UCM 2.2.3(E)). An approved SER is "acknowledgment of intent to serve." If a project sits on an approved SER for 12+ months while permits trail, the underlying capacity assumptions may have changed and an SER amendment may be needed.
    81→
    82→### Fees
    83→
    84→- **Water + wastewater capital recovery (impact) fees** — LDC § 25-9-321; schedule set by AWU Water Impact Fee Ordinance No. 20111215-115. Authorized under Texas Local Government Code Chapter 395. Calculated per LUE / meter size; paid at tap-permit application. (Note: comment letters citing § 25-12-11 for water impact fees are wrong — § 25-12-11 governs airport noise.)
    85→  - Fees scale roughly with meter size; a 3/4" or 1" domestic residential meter is the unit basis, larger commercial meters scale by AWWA equivalence factors. Confirm the current fee table on AW's website at diligence time — the ordinance has been periodically updated.
    86→  - A new SER does not reserve capacity OR lock in the fee schedule; fees are assessed at the schedule in effect when the tap permit is pulled.
    87→- **Tap fee** — service installation fee, separate from impact fees; per UCM 2.6.1.
    88→- **DSD inspection fees + City inspection fees** — UCM 2.6.1; paid before excavation permit issuance and before construction inspection. Often missed by GCs at hand-off and delays close-out.
    89→- **Water Quality fee-in-lieu** (urban watershed projects) — ECM Appendix T; documented in WBA/WBC. Optional path where on-site water-quality controls are infeasible.
    90→- **Industrial Waste Control Permit (IWCP) fees** — when non-domestic discharge applies (Chapter 15-10); annual operating fees + permit application fees.
    91→
    92→### Mandatory reclaimed water connection (LDC § 25-9-412)
    93→
    94→- **Small project** (GFA < 250,000 SF, multifamily 5+ / mixed-use / commercial): must connect if a reclaimed main is within **250 ft** along closest practicable access route.
    95→- **Large project** (GFA ≥ 250,000 SF, same use categories): must connect within **500 ft**.
    96→- **SF-only projects are exempt** (Article 5 of Ch. 25-9 applies only to MF 5+ / mixed-use / commercial).
    97→- Relief paths:
    98→  - Director discretionary variance — financial hardship (small projects only) or public-health/safety use (§ 25-9-412(C)).
    99→  - Mandatory affordable-housing exemption — ≥50% income-restricted units, Housing Director certification (§ 25-9-412(E)).
   100→  - The auto-variance under § 25-9-412(D) for large MF at 250-500 ft **expired April 1, 2024** — do not rely on it.
   101→
   102→### OWRS (Onsite Water Reuse System) — LDC § 25-9-414 / City Code § 15-13-7
   103→
   104→- Required for large development (GFA ≥ 250,000 SF) — multifamily / mixed-use / commercial — for site plan applications **filed on or after April 1, 2024**.
   105→- Separate trigger: any project with cooling-tower capacity ≥ 100 tons must capture condensate as makeup water (§ 15-13-7(B)).
   106→- Exceptions: director-approved fee-in-lieu (qualifying MF >500 ft from centralized reclaimed system, written request at submittal, commit to non-potable plumbing pre-CO); affordable-housing exemption.
   107→- Adds substantial cost: cistern + treatment + dedicated non-potable plumbing + PE-stamped O&M manual + Operating Permit.
   108→
   109→### Septic / OSSF (mostly ETJ + outlying parcels)
   110→
   111→- **Mandatory public connection within 100 ft of a public WW main** — LDC § 25-4-192.
   112→- OSSF allowed only when documented as one of: written denial of service from AW, AW written determination of infeasibility, or AW approval of continued use of an existing facility.
   113→- Existing OSSF must be abandoned per Austin City Code Chapter 15-5 before connecting to city wastewater. Abandonment inspection records required — frequently missing on infill redevelopment parcels.
   114→- In the ETJ, OSSF permitted by the county (Travis / Williamson / Hays) acting as TCEQ Chapter 285 delegate. Constraints to evaluate:
   115→  - **Soil class** — TCEQ Class I-IV; Class IV (clays, shallow soils) requires aerobic + spray field or non-standard.
   116→  - **Lot size** — conventional septic typically requires ≥1 acre; aerobic systems allowed on smaller lots but add O&M cost (annual maintenance contract mandatory).
   117→  - **Depth to limestone / groundwater** — Edwards Aquifer recharge / contributing zone parcels almost always require engineered aerobic systems and additional TCEQ Edwards Aquifer Protection Plan review.
   118→  - **Setback distances** from wells, property lines, water features.
   119→- For a multi-lot development on septic in the ETJ, expect each lot to require its own permit and capacity study; cumulative density can be limited by soils long before zoning.
   120→
   121→### Industrial Waste (when AW serves wastewater)
   122→
   123→- Chapter 15-10 (City Code Title 15, **not** LDC Title 25 — a common citation error). Applies to non-domestic discharges: food service (grease interceptors), parking garages (sand/oil interceptors), fueling (hazardous-materials interceptors), auto repair, pools, pet washes, dental/lab.
   124→- Pretreatment device sizing must be approved by AW's IW Division — do not self-apply capacities.
   125→
   126→### Demand calculation methodology (for Phase 3 sizing)
   127→

# Water & Wastewater Planning Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

Austin Water (AW) service availability for potable water, wastewater, and reclaimed water; tap sizing, capital recovery (impact) fees, Service Extension Requests (SERs); ETJ / MUD / WCID / private-utility complications; OSSF (septic) eligibility where no public main is reachable; reclaimed water mandatory-connection thresholds and Onsite Water Reuse System (OWRS) mandates. Bridges to fire (FWP) on fire-flow adequacy and to SDUF on rainwater/condensate reuse intersecting with stormwater.

## Authoritative sources

- Water/wastewater/reclaimed service area: Austin Water utility coverage = the AW "impact fee boundary" (UCM 2.2.1). Confirm against AW's GIS service-area layer; do not infer from full-purpose corporate limits alone.
- Utility Criteria Manual (UCM) — primary design + procedural code for AW (UCM 2.x).
- Land Development Code (LDC) Chapter 25-9 — Water and Wastewater Subchapter (SERs, impact fees, mandatory reclaimed connection).
- Tap fees / capital recovery fees: LDC § 25-9-321 (impact fee authority) + AWU Water Impact Fee Ordinance No. 20111215-115 (fee schedule). Tap permit + inspection fees per UCM 2.6.1.
- Service Extension Policy: LDC § 25-9-31 through § 25-9-41; UCM 2.2.
- Reclaimed / OWRS: LDC § 25-9-412 (mandatory connection); LDC § 25-9-414 + City Code § 15-13-7 (OWRS mandate, effective April 1, 2024).
- OSSF (septic) for parcels with no reachable public main: Austin City Code Chapter 15-5 (abandonment + within-corporate-limits OSSF); Travis County / Hays County / Williamson County permitting under TCEQ Chapter 285 in the ETJ.
- Industrial Waste Control Program (Chapter 15-10) — applies when AW is wastewater provider and discharge is non-domestic.
- Water Benchmarking Application (WBA/WBC): LDC § 25-9-413 (site plan submittal requirement).

## Regulatory pathway

| Action | Path / authority | Typical timing |
|---|---|---|
| Confirm service area + provider (AW vs MUD/WCID/CCN-holder) | AW GIS + PUC CCN map; LDC § 25-9-33(C)(2) | Day 0 (diligence) |
| Service availability letter (water + WW) | AW; must be dated within 6 months of review | 4-8 weeks |
| Pre-application meeting w/ AW for capacity questions | Informal; AWPE | 2-4 weeks lead |
| Service Extension Request (SER) — if triggered | LDC § 25-9-33; AW Pipeline Engineering (AWPE) | 3-9 months; approved SER is NOT a capacity reservation (UCM 2.2.3(E)) |
| WW SER multi-department review (AFD + Industrial Waste) | LDC § 25-9-33(C)(3), § 25-9-34(B) | Folded into SER timeline |
| Water Benchmarking Application (WBA/WBC) | LDC § 25-9-413(A); at site plan submittal | Concurrent with site plan |
| Large-development (GFA ≥ 250,000 SF) director consultation | LDC § 25-9-413(B) | Before site plan filing |
| AULCC (utility coordination) review for ROW work | UCM 3.2.0 | Plan set delivered 2 weeks before meeting |
| Reclaimed connection eligibility check (250 / 500 ft) | LDC § 25-9-412 | At concept; verify with AW Reclaimed Group |
| OWRS engineering report + permit (if mandated) | City Code § 15-13-7 / -10 / -11 | Adds ~6-12 mo; PE-stamped O&M manual |
| Tap permit issuance + capital recovery fee payment | LDC § 25-9-321; UCM 2.6.1 | At/before building permit |
| OSSF permit (ETJ, where no public main within 100 ft) | TCEQ Chapter 285 via county | Soil eval + 30-90 days |
| Easement recordation (if AW infrastructure outside ROW) | UCM 2.9.1.A.1-A.4; AWPE pre-recordation review | Before AW plan approval |

## Constraints to evaluate

### Service area + provider

- **Is the parcel inside Austin Water's retail service area?** AW serves within its impact-fee boundary (UCM 2.2.1). Full-purpose annexation does not automatically mean AW is the retail provider. Common Austin-area alternatives:
  - **Northtown MUD** (north Austin / Pflugerville fringe) — UCM 2.5.1.B requires its prior written approval before AW will sign anything.
  - **Southwest Water / Mid-Tex** — west / southwest ETJ.
  - **City of Manor** — eastern fringe.
  - **WCIDs** — scattered (e.g., WCID 17 in westlake).
- If a non-AW provider holds the CCN, expect a CCN release or transfer through PUC before AW can serve (LDC § 25-9-33(C)(2)). This adds 6-18 months and is not always achievable.
- If site is **inside the ETJ**, design must still meet COA standards but Industrial Waste plans go directly to the IW office, not through DSD (UCM 2.5.1.F).

### Capacity — water

- AW does **not** publish reservation; an approved SER is "acknowledgment of intent to serve" only (UCM 2.2.3(E)).
- **Pressure Concern Area** — administrative AW designation where existing infrastructure cannot maintain 20 psi residual at peak day + fire flow (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.d) or stays under 10 fps emergency velocity (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.c). Triggers a Water SER under LDC § 25-9-33(A)(3). Not mappable from public data — confirm via AW correspondence.
- **Pressure zone** must be designated on the AW General Info Sheet; affects pump sizing on tall buildings.
- Minimum public water main = 8 inches (UCM 2.9.2.A.4.a). Mains ≥24 inches are **transmission mains** (LDC § 25-9-32(15)) — no meter or fire-line tap permitted without a Director exception, even with an approved SER.
- Fire flow per FPCM Table 507-1: 1,000 gpm floor for SF < 3,600 SF; 2,500-3,500 gpm typical for multifamily / commercial. The 1,000 gpm number is a floor, not a default.

### Capacity — wastewater

- **Wastewater Capacity Concern Area** — administrative AW designation; not codified or mapped publicly. Triggers a WW SER under LDC § 25-9-33(A)(3). Confirm via AW correspondence; do not assume capacity from a 5-year-old AW master-plan study.
- **Living Unit Equivalent (LUE)** = 1 residential dwelling = 245 gpd average flow (UCM 2.9.4.A.1). Commercial flows are calculated separately (70 gpd/capita or case-by-case). LUE counts must reconcile to the approved SER; exceeding triggers an SER revision (LDC § 25-9-39(C)(3)).
- **Wastewater interceptor** = ≥18 inches (LDC § 25-9-32(14)) — direct connections prohibited without Director exception.
- **Service-connection ceiling**: UCM 2.9.4.G.3 prohibits direct service taps to any wastewater main >15 inches — applies to 16" and 17" mains even though they don't independently trigger the interceptor SER.
- Gravity service is required where feasible (UCM 2.9.4.J); lift stations are disfavored. If the city main is a **force main**, a grinder station at the property line is required and distance from property line to a gravity main must be ≤200 ft (UCM 2.9.4.J.18).

### SER triggers (LDC § 25-9-33(A))

An SER is required when any of:
1. Nearest accessible main is **>100 ft** from the property boundary.
2. Proposed connection is to a transmission main (≥24") or interceptor (≥18").
3. Existing main is unsuitable / insufficient (pressure concern, capacity concern, lot-line-crossing private piping, alley main connections, water meters on private lines, force-main extensions, public WW extension >100 ft, etc.).
4. Service is from a decentralized WW system the Director recommends the City operate.

Additional design-time triggers that may not strictly trigger an SER but constrain layout:
- Wastewater direct service tap prohibited to any main >15" (UCM 2.9.4.G.3) — applies even where the LDC § 25-9-32(14) interceptor threshold (≥18") isn't met.
- Water meters must be placed in public ROW or in an easement immediately adjacent to ROW; meters inside fences or on private lines are non-compliant (UCM 2.9.2.E.3).
- Utility easements outside ROW: minimum 15 ft wide or 2× the infrastructure depth (flowline-to-grade), whichever is greater, with infrastructure centered (UCM 2.9.1.A.1).

**SER carries an expiration**: 180 days from approval (post-April 2013, LDC § 25-9-39(C)) — extended by a pending or approved development application, indefinite for recorded-plat portions. SER amendment required for any change in lot configuration (re-plat, lot split, parcel merger), land use, or anticipated demand (LDC § 25-9-39(C)(3)) — even if LUE count is unchanged.

**SER ≠ capacity reservation** (UCM 2.2.3(E)). An approved SER is "acknowledgment of intent to serve." If a project sits on an approved SER for 12+ months while permits trail, the underlying capacity assumptions may have changed and an SER amendment may be needed.

### Fees

- **Water + wastewater capital recovery (impact) fees** — LDC § 25-9-321; schedule set by AWU Water Impact Fee Ordinance No. 20111215-115. Authorized under Texas Local Government Code Chapter 395. Calculated per LUE / meter size; paid at tap-permit application. (Note: comment letters citing § 25-12-11 for water impact fees are wrong — § 25-12-11 governs airport noise.)
  - Fees scale roughly with meter size; a 3/4" or 1" domestic residential meter is the unit basis, larger commercial meters scale by AWWA equivalence factors. Confirm the current fee table on AW's website at diligence time — the ordinance has been periodically updated.
  - A new SER does not reserve capacity OR lock in the fee schedule; fees are assessed at the schedule in effect when the tap permit is pulled.
- **Tap fee** — service installation fee, separate from impact fees; per UCM 2.6.1.
- **DSD inspection fees + City inspection fees** — UCM 2.6.1; paid before excavation permit issuance and before construction inspection. Often missed by GCs at hand-off and delays close-out.
- **Water Quality fee-in-lieu** (urban watershed projects) — ECM Appendix T; documented in WBA/WBC. Optional path where on-site water-quality controls are infeasible.
- **Industrial Waste Control Permit (IWCP) fees** — when non-domestic discharge applies (Chapter 15-10); annual operating fees + permit application fees.

### Mandatory reclaimed water connection (LDC § 25-9-412)

- **Small project** (GFA < 250,000 SF, multifamily 5+ / mixed-use / commercial): must connect if a reclaimed main is within **250 ft** along closest practicable access route.
- **Large project** (GFA ≥ 250,000 SF, same use categories): must connect within **500 ft**.
- **SF-only projects are exempt** (Article 5 of Ch. 25-9 applies only to MF 5+ / mixed-use / commercial).
- Relief paths:
  - Director discretionary variance — financial hardship (small projects only) or public-health/safety use (§ 25-9-412(C)).
  - Mandatory affordable-housing exemption — ≥50% income-restricted units, Housing Director certification (§ 25-9-412(E)).
  - The auto-variance under § 25-9-412(D) for large MF at 250-500 ft **expired April 1, 2024** — do not rely on it.

### OWRS (Onsite Water Reuse System) — LDC § 25-9-414 / City Code § 15-13-7

- Required for large development (GFA ≥ 250,000 SF) — multifamily / mixed-use / commercial — for site plan applications **filed on or after April 1, 2024**.
- Separate trigger: any project with cooling-tower capacity ≥ 100 tons must capture condensate as makeup water (§ 15-13-7(B)).
- Exceptions: director-approved fee-in-lieu (qualifying MF >500 ft from centralized reclaimed system, written request at submittal, commit to non-potable plumbing pre-CO); affordable-housing exemption.
- Adds substantial cost: cistern + treatment + dedicated non-potable plumbing + PE-stamped O&M manual + Operating Permit.

### Septic / OSSF (mostly ETJ + outlying parcels)

- **Mandatory public connection within 100 ft of a public WW main** — LDC § 25-4-192.
- OSSF allowed only when documented as one of: written denial of service from AW, AW written determination of infeasibility, or AW approval of continued use of an existing facility.
- Existing OSSF must be abandoned per Austin City Code Chapter 15-5 before connecting to city wastewater. Abandonment inspection records required — frequently missing on infill redevelopment parcels.
- In the ETJ, OSSF permitted by the county (Travis / Williamson / Hays) acting as TCEQ Chapter 285 delegate. Constraints to evaluate:
  - **Soil class** — TCEQ Class I-IV; Class IV (clays, shallow soils) requires aerobic + spray field or non-standard.
  - **Lot size** — conventional septic typically requires ≥1 acre; aerobic systems allowed on smaller lots but add O&M cost (annual maintenance contract mandatory).
  - **Depth to limestone / groundwater** — Edwards Aquifer recharge / contributing zone parcels almost always require engineered aerobic systems and additional TCEQ Edwards Aquifer Protection Plan review.
  - **Setback distances** from wells, property lines, water features.
- For a multi-lot development on septic in the ETJ, expect each lot to require its own permit and capacity study; cumulative density can be limited by soils long before zoning.

### Industrial Waste (when AW serves wastewater)

- Chapter 15-10 (City Code Title 15, **not** LDC Title 25 — a common citation error). Applies to non-domestic discharges: food service (grease interceptors), parking garages (sand/oil interceptors), fueling (hazardous-materials interceptors), auto repair, pools, pet washes, dental/lab.
- Pretreatment device sizing must be approved by AW's IW Division — do not self-apply capacities.

- Cooling tower (reclaimed/OWRS makeup): 28 gal/ton of cooling (UCM 2.9.3.A.2).
- Fire flow: per FPCM Table 507-1; verify with AW fire-flow test data (test reports valid 1 year typically).
- All values must appear on the AW General Information & Construction Notes Sheet's FIRE/DOMESTIC/IRRIGATION DEMAND DATA table and reconcile to the approved SER.

- **Water Benchmarking Application** is mandatory anyway (LDC § 25-9-413) but completing it early surfaces optimization (rainwater capture, condensate reuse, low-flow fixtures) before pro forma lock.
- **Alternative water sources** (well, rainwater harvesting, graywater, condensate): registered under § 15-1-19; ≤500-gallon residential outdoor systems are exempt from RPZ containment (§ 15-1-14(C)(33)(c)). These can reduce both potable demand (and impact fees) and stormwater retention obligations on the SDUF side.

| Inside AW service area, ≤100 ft from adequate main, no concern areas, no SER required, fees within pro forma | `note` |

## Common pitfalls

- **Treating ETJ parcels as AW-served.** Check the AW service-area layer and PUC CCN map. Northtown MUD, Southwest Water, City of Manor, and various WCIDs hold large chunks of the Austin metro fringe.
- **Reporting "capacity available" from an old AW planning study.** Capacity Concern Areas are administrative and change. Get AW correspondence for diligence-quality answers.
- **Missing capital recovery fees in the pro forma.** They are separate from tap fees and inspection fees, and they scale by meter size + LUE count.
- **Assuming an approved SER reserves capacity.** It does not (UCM 2.2.3(E)). LUE allocations can lapse with SER expiration.
- **Citing LDC § 25-12-11 for impact fees** (that's airport noise) — correct cite is LDC § 25-9-321 + Ordinance No. 20111215-115.
- **Counting straight-line distance for the 250/500-ft reclaimed connection trigger.** LDC § 25-9-412 uses *closest practicable access route*, not straight line.
- **Assuming the expired § 25-9-412(D) auto-variance still works** for large MF at 250-500 ft. It expired April 1, 2024.
- **Citing Chapter 15-10 as "LDC §15-10-..."** — it's in City Code Title 15, not LDC Title 25; AW review comments that get this wrong are still common.
- **Forgetting the OWRS condensate sub-trigger.** Even small projects (< 250,000 SF GFA) hit § 15-13-7(B) if combined cooling-tower capacity is ≥100 tons.
- **Underestimating SER timeline.** AFD and Industrial Waste approvals are part of WW SER technical review; multi-department concurrence takes 3-9 months, longer for capacity-constrained corridors.
- **Showing a fire line tap off a transmission main without a Director exception.** UCM 2.9.2.E.2 prohibits it even when an SER for the project is otherwise in hand.
- **Failing to check for an existing OSSF on infill / redevelopment parcels.** Abandonment under City Code Chapter 15-5 is required before tying into AW; documentation is often missing on older parcels.
- **Assuming Industrial Waste won't apply on a "non-industrial" project.** Restaurants, parking garages with floor drains, car washes, fueling, pet washes, dental, dumpster wash areas all trigger IW pretreatment review.

1→# Fire Feasibility — Austin, TX
     2→
     3→## Domain
     4→
     5→Fire department access (apparatus roads, turning, dead-ends, aerial operations), water supply for firefighting (hydrant coverage, spacing, fire flow at 20 psi residual, FDC siting), building code triggers (occupancy, construction type, high-rise classification at 75 ft, standpipe trigger at 30 ft), sprinkler-system selection (NFPA 13/13R/13D) and the fire-flow reductions they unlock, Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) zoning, and the procedural pathway through Austin Fire Department (AFD) including AMOC pre-approvals. Bridges to: Austin Water (wwp/utilities — fire main capacity, hydrant taps), Transportation (driveway geometry, ASMP street level), and Zoning (high-rise massing implications).
     6→
     7→Scope excludes: building permit-stage sprinkler shop drawings, NFPA 13 hydraulic head calcs, fire alarm system design — those are post-site-plan deliverables. AFD WUI applies only within Full Purpose and Limited Purpose Jurisdiction; ETJ parcels are exempt from WUI but defer to the applicable county ESD for fire access.
     8→
     9→## Authoritative sources
    10→
    11→- **Fire code:** 2024 International Fire Code, adopted via LDC § 25-12-171 (Ord. 20250410-039, effective July 10, 2025). Submittals with original submission date before July 10, 2025 governed by 2021 IFC. Appendix D **not** adopted — apparatus access is governed by LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503–507.5 with local amendments.
    12→- **Local amendments:** LDC § 25-12-173 (IFC), LDC § 25-12-183 (IWUIC), LDC § 25-12-1 (IBC). NFPA editions per LDC § 25-12-173 Chapter 80 (NFPA 13—2025, 14—2024, 20—2025, 24—2022, 72—2025, 855—2023).
    13→- **Fire Protection Criteria Manual (FPCM):** §§ 4.4.0 (general), 4.7.0 (NFPA 13), 4.8.0 (NFPA 14 / standpipes), 4.9.0 (NFPA 20 / pumps), 4.10.0 (WUI); Appendix E §§ 1.1.0, 2.1.0, 2.4.0, 3.2.x (submittal content).
    14→- **Utilities Criteria Manual (UCM):** § 2.9.2 (water/fire flow); UCM 2.9.2.D.1 (hydrant spacing); UCM 2.9.2.B.6 (fire line material, BFP, flow detection).
    15→- **Standard Specifications Manual (SSM):** Item 511.4.B (hydrant physical placement); Standards 901S-1, 901S-2, 901S-5, 901S-6 (apparatus access, turnarounds, fire-zone signs).
    16→- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM):** §§ 7.3, 7.5 (driveways serving fire lanes); ASMP Street Network Map for street-level lookup.
    17→- **Hydrant flow data:** AFD hydrant flow test report (Fire Marshal-witnessed; ≤1 year old). Fire Flow Map "Box" number on AW General Info & Construction Notes Sheet.
    18→- **WUI map:** 2024 WUI Code Map (dark blue/teal = Zones A & B combined; light blue = Zone C). Map does not distinguish A from B — AFD Wildfire Division field-measures.
    19→
    20→## Regulatory pathway
    21→
    22→Fire review runs **concurrently** with civil/site plan review through Development Services Department, but AFD has independent sign-off authority. Plans with fire lines additionally require both AFD and DSD approval before Austin Water Processing and Evaluation (AWPE) will approve (UCM 2.5.1.D).
    23→
    24→- **Pre-application:** AFD pre-app meeting strongly advisable for high-rise, podium, mixed-construction, WUI, alternative-surface fire lanes, or any site requiring an AMOC. AFD will not issue AMOC approval numbers during site plan cycle — AMOC must be a **separate standalone submittal**, approved before site plan submission.
    25→- **AMOC track (IFC § 104.8):** Required when standard IFC requirements cannot be met — most commonly to reduce minimum commercial fire flow below 1,500 gpm (floor: 1,000 gpm), reduce hydrant coverage, or approve pyrophoric gas storage. AMOC must be pre-approved with an AFD-issued approval number and date noted in the AFD Fire Analysis Table. "Pending"/"submitted" entries are deficient.
    26→- **WUI track (FPCM 4.10.0):** Concurrent review by AFD Wildfire Division. Required for any property within Full/Limited Purpose Jurisdiction that the 2024 WUI Code Map covers or that AFD Wildfire designates. Separate WUI approval stamp required before final site plan approval. Map status is rebuttable only by AFD Wildfire Division — self-declared "not in WUI" is a deficiency.
    27→- **High-rise track (IBC § 202 via LDC § 25-12-1):** Any occupied floor >75 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access triggers IBC § 403 high-rise requirements: Fire Command Center (1-hr fire barrier; exterior access or 2-hr rated passageway; FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.13 equipment list), dual remote FDCs (NFPA 14 § 7.12.2), fire pump room, dual water mains (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.e), AEDs each occupied level, simultaneous stairway-unlock controls (LDC § 25-12-173 § 508.1.6). For buildings >420 ft, mains must be in **different streets** (IFC § 914.3.1.2). Buildings between ~65–75 ft must carry three pre-CO survey notes (ZLU-29.10/.11/.12).
    28→- **Decision body:** Fire Marshal's office; Wildfire Division (for WUI); final sign-off on cover sheet approval block.
    29→- **Timeline reality:** AMOC review adds ~6–12 weeks before site plan submission becomes viable. WUI concurrent review rarely controls the critical path. High-rise pre-app + dual-main coordination with Austin Water can add 1–2 cycles. Any post-approval change to fire lanes, hydrants, FDCs, fire service routing, riser/pump rooms, or electric disconnect requires AFD resubmission.
    30→
    31→## Constraints to evaluate
    32→
    33→**Apparatus access (LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503.1.1, 503.2.1, 503.2.4 with City amendments; Appendix D not adopted).**
    34→- Fire apparatus access road within **150 ft** (path-of-travel, not arc) of all portions of all exterior walls of the first story. AFD routinely extends to **200 ft** for buildings fully sprinklered per NFPA 13 (not 13R/13D) under Exception 1.1, but the increase is **discretionary** — plans showing 200 ft must reflect AFD authorization; high-piled combustible storage buildings (>12,000 sf area + storage >12 ft height) are locked at 150 ft regardless of sprinklers (IFC § 3206.6). High-piled storage also requires one FD access door per 100 LF of exterior wall facing the access road, max 125 ft center-to-center (IFC § 3206.6.1, § 3206.7.5).
    35→- Measurement: actual ground-level path around obstructions ≥4 ft tall (buildings, walls, fences, grade changes); never through/under buildings; never across water-quality features; AFD will not lay supply hose across ASMP Level 3+ arterials, expressways, parkways, freeways, or toll roads. Routes that cross property lines require a recorded **JUAE or UDA** (§ 503.1.1 Exception 3).
    36→- **Minimum unobstructed width 25 ft** face-of-curb to face-of-curb (sidewalk does not count); 14 ft minimum vertical clearance for the full width; **inside turning radius 25 ft / outside 50 ft** (§ 503.2.4). Wider than 25 ft lanes may reduce to 20-in/40-out. Divided fire lanes where aerial is not anticipated: two 15-ft lanes (Exception 2.d). Security gates: 25 ft two-way / 15 ft one-way (20 ft two-way only with prior Fire Prevention Division written approval). Throat at Level 1/2 street crosswalk: 20 ft permitted (Exception 2.e). Curb-return radii at fire-access driveways from public streets follow TCM 7.5.1.1 Table 7-1 "Fire Access" column — typically 15 ft on Level 1/2 streets (vs. 10 ft typical). Turning movements onto opposing traffic lanes or where ASMP proposes a raised median are prohibited.
    37→- **Grade:** asphalt ≤ 13%; concrete ≤ 15%; maximum 10% change in any 20 ft; aerial setup areas ≤ ~12–13% running and 3.5% cross-slope; driveway grade change in a fire lane ≤ 6% (TCM 7.5.2.1.E, more restrictive). Where max grades cannot be met, a fully protected sprinkler system approved by AFD may substitute. Minimum drainage: 2% vegetated / alternative; 1% asphalt; 0.5% concrete.
    38→- **Surface:** HS-20 loading (16 kips/wheel, 80,000 lbs total) for all fire lanes and all structural elements within them (manhole covers, vault lids, trench grates). Final asphalt/concrete must be in place before combustible construction begins. Alternative surfaces (grasscrete, pavers, PICP, porous asphalt/concrete) limited to ≤25% of building-perimeter fire protection, require slip-resistant surfaces at turns and 40 LF at building corners for aerial operations, reinforced mountable curb when no Type I/II apron is present, and a post-completion PE-of-record concurrence letter (§ 503.2.3.1). Pervious or decorative paving **within 100 ft of any building** requires AFD approval + PE design for 80,000 lb live load even when not formally a fire lane.
    39→
    40→**Aerial apparatus (LDC § 25-12-173 § 503.2.6.1; AFD operational practice).**
    41→- Aerial-clearance review begins at ~73 ft per AFD practice (2 ft before the 75-ft high-rise threshold). For high-rise and near-high-rise buildings, plans must demonstrate clear staging adjacent to the building face — typically a 25-ft setback envelope plus overhead clearance for the boom. Divided 15-ft lanes are not permitted where aerial deployment is expected; full 25-ft lane required.
    42→- Elevated surfaces (podium slabs, plaza decks) that serve as fire apparatus access must be designed for the greater of IFC § 503.2.6 apparatus loads or IBC § 1607.8.1 live load (LDC § 25-12-3 § 1607.8.2). **Outrigger loads:** **43,200 lbs on one outrigger** or **28,600 lbs each on two adjacent outriggers** at 18-ft center spacing on 24"×24" contact (§ 503.2.6.1). Engineer of record must sign a post-completion concurrence letter. Access hatches, vault covers, and trench grates in the apparatus path must individually carry the 43,200-lb single-outrigger rating.
    43→- Bridges/elevated fire lane crossings: AASHTO HB-17 (or current LRFD) design; load-limit signs at both entrances (§ 503.2.6).
    44→
    45→**Dead-ends and turnarounds.**
    46→- Dead-end fire lane >150 ft requires a turnaround per Standard 901S-2: cul-de-sac with 50-ft unobstructed radius **or** hammerhead/T 25 ft × 80 ft with 10 ft additional clearance and no obstructions over 1 ft (FPCM 4.4.0).
    47→- Turnaround pavement must be marked fire lane on all sides; hose-lay extension from the turnaround counts toward apparatus-to-building distance.
    48→
    49→**Hydrant coverage and spacing (LDC § 25-12-173 § 507.5.1; UCM § 2.9.2.D).**
    50→- Primary hydrant hose-lay to all exterior walls: **400 ft** non-sprinklered (non-R-3/U); **500 ft** for buildings sprinklered throughout per NFPA 13 or 13R; **600 ft** for Group R-3 and U regardless of sprinklers.
    51→- **Second hydrant within 500 ft (600 ft for R-3/U) when required fire flow ≥1,500 gpm; additional hydrants within 1,000 ft when fire flow >2,500 gpm. One hydrant per 1,250 gpm (or fraction).** Multi-hydrant calcs must show all required hydrants flowing simultaneously, starting at the most hydraulically remote.
    52→- **Spacing:** **300 ft** maximum interval in commercial/high-density areas (CBD, DMU, W/LO, CS, CH, MF-4/5/6, or inside the Downtown Austin Project Coordination Zone); **600 ft** max interval elsewhere; hydrant at every major intersection; hydrants on **both sides** of any divided road regardless of arterial class (UCM 2.9.2.D.2).
    53→- **Placement (SSM 511.4.B):** 3–6 ft behind curb gutter face; steamer center ≥18 in above grade; steamer perpendicular to and facing the curb/fire lane; ≥20 ft from curb tangency at corners; ≥9 ft (any direction) from sanitary sewer line/lateral/service/manhole (UCM 2.9.2.D.4); ≥5 ft from storm drain; ≥3 ft clear circumference; bollards where exposed to vehicles; lead line ≤55 ft from main and cannot cross a divided road.
    54→- **Field-verified fire flow test:** AFD-conducted or AFD-witnessed only (IFC § 507.4 as locally amended); ≤1 year old at site-plan submission; on hydrants on the same main/zone serving the connection point; full FPCM Appendix E § 2.4.0 data set (static, residual, pitot, flow rate, hydrant IDs, date/time, conductor, equipment, gauge elevations).
    55→- **Required fire flow at 20 psi residual** from IFC Appendix B Table B105.1(2) using IBC construction type + fire-flow calculation area per LDC § 25-12-173 B104.1. Commercial floor: 1,500 gpm (reducible to 1,000 gpm only with pre-approved AMOC). Sprinkler reductions per Table B105.2: NFPA 13 → 75%; NFPA 13R → 50% (capped at 50% for Type III/IV/V); NFPA 13D → 25%. **No reduction** for Group H or S-1/S-2 with high-piled or rack storage.
    56→- Hydraulic calc C-factors are fixed by FPCM 4.4.0 Table 507-2: C=80 (iron/steel) or C=110 (plastic/copper) — software defaults of 140/150 are non-compliant. **Velocity ≤10 fps** upstream of the 6-in hydrant tap; the 6-in lead downstream is the only velocity exception.
    57→
    58→**FDC siting (IFC § 912; LDC § 25-12-173 § 912.5; NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4).**
    59→- Each separate sprinkler or standpipe system requires its own FDC (NFPA 13D excluded; stand-alone local <20-head systems excluded per FPCM 4.7.0). Street side, oriented to fire apparatus access, fully visible. Prohibited: under building overhangs, inside parking garages (even sprinklered), behind walls/fences, in 100-yr floodplain, in covered courtyards.
    60→- **FDC-to-hydrant travel distance:** **100 ft** for standpipe systems (NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4); **300 ft** for sprinklered buildings without Class I standpipe (IFC § 507.5.1.1). Working space: 36 in W × 36 in D × 78 in H; mounting 18–48 in above grade.
    61→- High-rise: minimum **two remotely located FDCs** on separate building walls as far apart as possible (NFPA 14 § 7.12.2). For multi-zone standpipe systems, at least two FDCs per zone. FDC pressure demand ceiling: **150 psi** non-high-rise / **350 psi** high-rise (FPCM 4.8.0).
    62→- Austin-amended FDC sign: white reflective letters on red, "FDC" ≥6 in tall, other words ≥2 in, approved text strings only ("FDC", "AUTOMATIC SPRINKLERS", "STANDPIPES", "TEST CONNECTION", combinations) — "FIRE DEPARTMENT CONNECTION" is **not** an approved string. Manual standpipes must indicate "MANUAL" + "WET"/"DRY"; PRV-equipped systems indicate floor range served.
    63→
    64→**Fire area and high-rise classification.**
    65→- Fire-flow calculation area = total gross floor area of all stories, mezzanines, basements, mechanical, and parking levels under exterior walls and horizontal roof projections (LDC § 25-12-173 B104.1). Exceptions: Type IA/IB → three largest successive floors (construction-type-based, **not** high-rise-based); open parking garage of IA/IB per IBC § 406.5 → single largest floor; R-3/R-4/townhouse/1–2-family separated <10 ft → combined.
    66→- Fire walls per IBC § 706 create separate fire areas **only with zero openings**. Any fire door, damper, or utility penetration disqualifies the separation.
    67→- Podium exclusion of garage from upper fire area (IBC § 510.2) requires **both** a 3-hr fire-rated horizontal assembly with no openings **and** NFPA 13 (not 13R) in the garage.
    68→- High-rise threshold: any occupied floor >75 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access (lowest finished grade of any adjacent fire lane / street; sloped sites use the downhill side). Standpipe trigger: highest floor >30 ft above same datum (IFC § 905.3.1). NFPA 13R disallowed for buildings ≥4 stories or with highest occupied floor ≥30 ft above lowest FD access (IFC § 903.3.1.2).
    69→- Aerial-apparatus clearance review begins at ~73 ft per AFD operational practice — design overhead, planter, and side-yard clearances accordingly.
    70→
    71→**WUI (LDC § 25-12-183).** Proximity Zones A (≤50 ft from ≥40 ac wildland), B (>50 ≤150 ft), C (>150 ft ≤0.5 mi from ≥40 ac, or within 1.5 mi of ≥750 ac). Most restrictive zone applies to the entire structure when it spans multiple zones. ETJ exempt.
    72→
    73→**Underground fire main + utility interface (UCM 2.9.2.B.6; NFPA 13/24).**
    74→- Service from public main to property line: **ductile iron** (DI); gate valve at the tap to the public main; backflow preventer inside property line, accessible for City inspection; **flow detection device** on every unmetered fire line, positioned so ≤100 gallons sit between the device and the public main.
    75→- **NFPA 13 minimum fire service main: 6 in** (NFPA 13 § 24.1.3.1); smaller permitted only with PE-sealed hydraulic calc from a TX-licensed RME sprinkler designer. **Underground may extend ≤10 ft under building** (NFPA 13 § 10.4.3.1; NFPA 24 § 10.6.1); >10 ft triggers trench requirements (rigid walls, noncombustible base, accessible from within, drain, restrained joints, shutoff valve, freeze protection).
    76→- Sectional control valves required when the private fire main serves **≥7 fire-protection connections** (NFPA 24 § 6.6.1). Each private hydrant gets a gate valve at the tee, restrained to the main with bolt-through connection (UCM 2.9.2.C.1). Fully restrained joints throughout (UCM 2.9.2.D).
    77→- **NFPA 13 exterior shutoff** (NFPA 13 § 8.16.1) — one of: underground PIV ≥40 ft from building; wall-mounted PIV; exterior door direct to riser room within 15 ft walking distance (not under overhang); BFP vault (no hydrants downstream of BFP, no PIV upstream of BFP, no other valves in vault). PIVs not required for NFPA 13R/13D.
    78→- High-rise fire pumps require **two water main connections** with independent supply piping each sized for full pump demand (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.e). Same-main exception only with valving between tap points. Buildings >420 ft: connections must be in **different streets** (IFC § 914.3.1.2). Parallel supply mains require ≥10 ft separation.
    79→
    80→**Knox Box / Knox Switch (FPCM 4.4.0; FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.16; IFC § 506.1).**
    81→- Knox Key Box required for any commercial structure with fire-protection systems (sprinklers, alarm, standpipe) **or** any site with physical access barriers (locked gates, fenced perimeters, bollards). Knox is the only approved brand in Austin. Must be called out on plans with a specific leader-line — a general note is insufficient.
    82→- **Knox Key Switch** (electrical, not a key vault) required for any motorized/power-operated gate on a fire apparatus access road, ingress side. Substituting a Knox Box for a Switch at a motorized gate is deficient.
    83→- High-rise: additional Knox Key Box per FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.13(A.5), distinct from the riser-room Knox Box.
    84→
    85→**Construction-phase fire protection (IFC § 3313; FPCM 4.4.0 General Note 3).**
    86→- When combustible materials arrive on site, **≥500 gpm within 500 ft** must be available (IFC § 3313). For Type I/II construction, vertical work may proceed once this supply is in place, ahead of full permanent fire flow.
    87→- Required fire-protection infrastructure (mains, private hydrants, apparatus roadways) must be installed and operational before any combustible/vertical construction begins (IFC § 501.4). Final asphalt or concrete on apparatus access surfaces must be in place before combustible construction begins.
    88→- Existing hydrants and FDCs must remain in service through all phases; replacement hydrants must be accepted as operational before the existing hydrant they replace is removed. Modifications to private fire mains require advance email notification to FirePrevention@austintexas.gov (IFC § 901.7.4) and return-to-service notice (§ 901.7.6).
    89→
    90→**Pipeline ordinance (LDC §§ 25-4-134, 25-2-516).** Two-prong test: hazardous liquid per 49 CFR § 195.2 **AND** ≥8-in inside diameter. Natural gas (49 CFR Part 192) does not qualify. AFD Fire Analysis Table field must read "YES" when a qualifying pipeline is on or adjacent to the site.
    91→
    92→## Opportunities to evaluate
    93→
    94→- **NFPA 13 sprinklers → 75% fire-flow reduction** (cap by post-reduction floor of 1,000 gpm). Often unlocks a workable supply scenario on sites with marginal Box-number capacity. For Type III/IV/V wood-frame construction, NFPA 13R is capped at 50%; pushing to non-combustible (II-B) construction can unlock the full 75% reduction.
    95→- **AMOC to drop the commercial minimum to 1,000 gpm** (FPCM Appendix D). Viable for small commercial buildings where the standard 1,500-gpm floor would otherwise force a new tap or main upsize. Must be approved before site plan submission — budget 6–12 weeks.
    96→- **Podium construction (IBC § 510.2)** excludes the garage from upper-fire-area calcs and can drop fire flow by a tier — but requires 3-hr horizontal assembly with no openings **and** NFPA 13 in the garage, which costs more than NFPA 13R-throughout in soft sites.
    97→- **200-ft sprinklered apparatus access (Exception 1.1)** is AFD-routine for NFPA 13 buildings and meaningfully expands the buildable envelope on sites where a 150-ft constraint would force unnecessary internal drives or rated breezeways.
    98→- **Rated breezeway** (2-hr fire-rated walls + ceiling, full sprinkler, open both ends, 14-ft clearance, required signage) can satisfy apparatus access for landlocked rear-of-building exterior points where a perimeter loop is infeasible.
    99→- **Alternative-surface fire lanes** (grasscrete, PICP, pavers) preserve open-space and water-quality goals but capped at 25% of building perimeter fire protection and require PE concurrence — useful for compact urban infill but rarely sufficient as the primary route.
   100→- **Limited area wet pipe (NFPA 13 § 4.2)** for freestanding R-2 amenity buildings (clubhouses, leasing offices) in 13R projects — avoids forcing a full NFPA 13 design on an otherwise unsprinklered ancillary structure (FPCM 4.4.0).
   101→- **Bureau programs:** check `bureau/jurisdictions/austin/programs/` for any AFD expedited-review or pre-approved-typology programs that may apply.
   102→
   103→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
   104→
   105→- **wwp.md** — Fire Flow Map Box number; AFD hydrant flow test report (≤1 yr, AFD-conducted/witnessed) with static/residual/flow and AWWA-projected available flow at 20 psi; existing hydrant locations and IDs within 500 ft; whether an SER is anticipated; existing main sizes/materials.
   106→- **transportation.md** — ASMP Street Level of all frontages (governs apparatus turning radii per TCM Tables 7-1/7-2 and the "no hose lay across major roadway" rule); adjacent ROW widths; presence of medians/divided roadways; driveway approach geometry.
   107→- **zoning.md / sde.md** — Base zoning district (drives 300 vs. 600 ft hydrant spacing); DAPCZ status; setback envelope (controls apparatus-to-building distance feasibility); building height envelope (drives 30-ft standpipe and 75-ft high-rise triggers).
   108→- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — Building footprints, story count, highest occupied floor elevation, IBC construction type assumption, fire-flow calculation area per building, intended occupancy classifications, gate locations, parking-garage open/enclosed determination, podium configuration if any.
   109→- **phase1-extraction/site-context.md** — WUI map status; proximity to ≥40 ac and ≥750 ac wildland; any hazardous-liquid pipelines (commodity + ID); floodplain boundaries (FDCs may not be in 100-yr floodplain); 2024 WUI Code Map screenshot.
   110→
   111→## Output structure
   112→
   113→Standard discipline output shape per `references/phase3-disciplines.md`. Include the AFD Fire Analysis Table fields as a structured findings table — IFC edition (governed by **original** submission date), construction type, high-rise Yes/No (with the 75-ft datum), fire area (with calc method), IWUIC edition + Proximity Zone, AMOC status, pipeline-ordinance Yes/No — because Phase 4 will lift these into the diligence report.
   114→
   115→## Severity heuristics
   116→
   117→| Finding | Severity |
   118→|---|---|
   119→| Required fire flow (post-sprinkler reduction) exceeds AWWA-calculated available flow at 20 psi — capacity upgrade (new tap, main upsize, SER, or storage tank + fire pump) required | `significant` |
   120→| Building >75 ft above lowest FD access without dual-main supply, fire pump, FCC, or required high-rise envelope — concept needs redesign or alternative procurement track | `significant` |
   121→| Property in WUI Zone A or B without site-design accommodation (defensible space, ignition-resistant exterior, modified setbacks); or qualifying hazardous pipeline triggers buffer/easement constraint | `significant` |
   122→| Aerial apparatus required (highest occupied floor approaching 75 ft) but setbacks, overhead clearances, or HS-20 setup pads don't accommodate it | `significant` |
   123→| Apparatus access path-of-travel exceeds 200 ft to one or more exterior building points on a sprinklered building, or >150 ft non-sprinklered, with no rated-breezeway or second-passage option | `significant` |
   124→| Fire-area calc method depends on Type IA/IB classification, podium § 510.2 exclusion, or fire-wall separation that materially changes required fire flow tier — design margin is thin | `moderate` |
   125→| AMOC needed to clear commercial 1,500 gpm floor (down to 1,000 gpm) — schedule risk of 6–12 weeks pre-submittal | `moderate` |
   126→| Dead-end aisle >150 ft without turnaround, or cul-de-sac/hammerhead geometry below 901S-2 spec | `moderate` |
   127→| Hydrant nominally beyond required spacing but workable with new tap on existing main; second-hydrant trigger at 1,500 gpm not yet addressed | `moderate` |
   128→| Cross-property fire access requires a JUAE/UDA not yet recorded | `moderate` |
   129→| Alternative-surface fire lane proposed for >25% of perimeter, or pervious paving within 100 ft of buildings without AFD PE-design pathway | `moderate` |
   130→| Standard commercial/multifamily occupancy with adequate hydrant coverage, NFPA 13 sprinklers, and apparatus access within standard envelope | `note` |
   131→| AFD General Notes verbatim from FPCM § 4.4.0; AFD Fire Analysis Table complete with correct IFC edition for original submission date | `note` |
   132→
   133→## Common pitfalls
   134→
   135→- **Citing IFC Appendix D for apparatus access** — Austin does not adopt Appendix D. Access is governed by LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503–507.5 with local amendments.
   136→- **Using the wrong IFC edition.** Original submission date governs, not resubmittal: 2012 IFC (pre 1/7/18) → 2015 IFC → 2021 IFC (9/1/21–7/9/25) → **2024 IFC (7/10/25 onward).** FPCM Appendix D still internally references 2012 IFC; LDC governs.
   137→- **Substituting the Fire Flow Map Box nominal value for an AWWA-calculated available flow** at 20 psi from actual AFD test data. The Box is a modeled value; the calculated flow must come from the test.
   138→- **Confusing high-rise (height) and Type IA/IB (construction type).** Three-largest-floors fire-area exception is **construction-type-based**. A Type IIIA high-rise does not get it; a Type IA low-rise does.
   139→- **NFPA 13R applied to a 4-story or ≥30-ft-occupied-floor building** — disallowed; full NFPA 13 required (IFC § 903.3.1.2). The 30-ft datum is the lowest level of fire department vehicle access, not average grade or primary entry.
   140→- **Assuming the 200-ft sprinklered access distance is automatic.** It is a discretionary increase by the fire code official; high-piled storage buildings (>12,000 sf + >12 ft storage) are locked at 150 ft.
   141→- **Hose-lay measured as straight-line, arc, or through a water-quality pond.** Path of travel only, around obstructions ≥4 ft tall, never across major arterials/expressways/parkways/freeways/toll roads, never diagonally across intersections.
   142→- **Self-declaring "not in WUI."** Only AFD Wildfire Division determines applicability and Proximity Zone, regardless of map status. ETJ parcels are exempt.
   143→- **AMOC entered as "pending" or "submitted"** in the AFD Fire Analysis Table — must be an AFD-issued approval number and date from a separate, prior, standalone submittal.
   144→- **C-factor 140 or 150** in private fire-main hydraulic calcs (software defaults). Required: C=80 iron/steel; C=110 plastic/copper/resin-lined (FPCM 4.4.0 Table 507-2).
   145→- **Hydrants placed within 9 ft of any sanitary sewer** (any direction) or in/within 6 in of a sidewalk/ramp — both are common SSM 511.4.B / UCM 2.9.2.D.4 fails.
   146→- **Mistaking a natural-gas pipeline for a "hazardous pipeline."** The ordinance requires hazardous liquid under 49 CFR Part 195 **and** ≥8-in ID. Natural gas (Part 192) does not qualify.
   147→- **ETJ parcels: ESD authority.** Within Travis County (ESD #2), Hays County, Williamson County, or city limits of Buda etc., AFD does not govern — confirm the correct fire authority before applying any Austin-specific rule.
   148→- **Knox Box in a general note only.** FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.16 requires a specific leader-line callout with location and size; a plan note saying "Knox Box to be provided" is deficient.
   149→- **"IFC 503.3.3.2" cited on plans.** This section does not exist in Austin's adopted code; correct authority for fire-zone marking is FPCM 4.4.0 General Construction Notes and LDC § 25-12-173 § 503.3.2.
   150→- **Fire lane labels on water utility easement drawings.** Fire-zone designation is exclusively AFD jurisdiction (§§ 503.3, 503.1.4); placing fire-lane labels on AW utility easement plats implies utility-department enforcement and is a deficiency.
   151→- **Bare "IFC" terminology in fire-flow demand tables.** UCM 2.9.2.A.3.b requires "City of Austin Fire Code" terminology, with "City of Austin Local Amendments" attached to every IFC section citation.
   152→- **AFD General Notes modified from FPCM § 4.4.0 verbatim language** or augmented with Knox Box specs or non-AFD jurisdictions (Travis County ESD #2, etc.) — must be exact FPCM text, six notes only.
   153→- **AFD Fire Analysis Table combined with the Austin Water Project Information Table.** Must be a standalone table on the cover sheet with nine required left-column fields verbatim (FPCM § 4.4.0).
   154→- **Treating the Fire Flow Zone Box number as the available flow.** The Box reflects modeled capacity; available flow at 20 psi must be AWWA-calculated from actual AFD test data, and the two values must reconcile on plans.
   155→- **Fire main interconnected with domestic supply or backed up by a domestic meter.** Prohibited (NFPA 13 § 16.9.3.1); cross-connection protection by reduced-pressure backflow assembly is required (IFC § 507.6 as locally amended).
   156→
