# Fire Feasibility — Austin, TX

## Domain

Fire department access (apparatus roads, turning, dead-ends, aerial operations), water supply for firefighting (hydrant coverage, spacing, fire flow at 20 psi residual, FDC siting), building code triggers (occupancy, construction type, high-rise classification at 75 ft, standpipe trigger at 30 ft), sprinkler-system selection (NFPA 13/13R/13D) and the fire-flow reductions they unlock, Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) zoning, and the procedural pathway through Austin Fire Department (AFD) including AMOC pre-approvals. Bridges to: Austin Water (wwp/utilities — fire main capacity, hydrant taps), Transportation (driveway geometry, ASMP street level), and Zoning (high-rise massing implications).

Scope excludes: building permit-stage sprinkler shop drawings, NFPA 13 hydraulic head calcs, fire alarm system design — those are post-site-plan deliverables. AFD WUI applies only within Full Purpose and Limited Purpose Jurisdiction; ETJ parcels are exempt from WUI but defer to the applicable county ESD for fire access.

## Authoritative sources

- **Fire code:** 2024 International Fire Code, adopted via LDC § 25-12-171 (Ord. 20250410-039, effective July 10, 2025). Submittals with original submission date before July 10, 2025 governed by 2021 IFC. Appendix D **not** adopted — apparatus access is governed by LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503–507.5 with local amendments.
- **Local amendments:** LDC § 25-12-173 (IFC), LDC § 25-12-183 (IWUIC), LDC § 25-12-1 (IBC). NFPA editions per LDC § 25-12-173 Chapter 80 (NFPA 13—2025, 14—2024, 20—2025, 24—2022, 72—2025, 855—2023).
- **Fire Protection Criteria Manual (FPCM):** §§ 4.4.0 (general), 4.7.0 (NFPA 13), 4.8.0 (NFPA 14 / standpipes), 4.9.0 (NFPA 20 / pumps), 4.10.0 (WUI); Appendix E §§ 1.1.0, 2.1.0, 2.4.0, 3.2.x (submittal content).
- **Utilities Criteria Manual (UCM):** § 2.9.2 (water/fire flow); UCM 2.9.2.D.1 (hydrant spacing); UCM 2.9.2.B.6 (fire line material, BFP, flow detection).
- **Standard Specifications Manual (SSM):** Item 511.4.B (hydrant physical placement); Standards 901S-1, 901S-2, 901S-5, 901S-6 (apparatus access, turnarounds, fire-zone signs).
- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM):** §§ 7.3, 7.5 (driveways serving fire lanes); ASMP Street Network Map for street-level lookup.
- **Hydrant flow data:** AFD hydrant flow test report (Fire Marshal-witnessed; ≤1 year old). Fire Flow Map "Box" number on AW General Info & Construction Notes Sheet.
- **WUI map:** 2024 WUI Code Map (dark blue/teal = Zones A & B combined; light blue = Zone C). Map does not distinguish A from B — AFD Wildfire Division field-measures.

## Regulatory pathway

Fire review runs **concurrently** with civil/site plan review through Development Services Department, but AFD has independent sign-off authority. Plans with fire lines additionally require both AFD and DSD approval before Austin Water Processing and Evaluation (AWPE) will approve (UCM 2.5.1.D).

- **Pre-application:** AFD pre-app meeting strongly advisable for high-rise, podium, mixed-construction, WUI, alternative-surface fire lanes, or any site requiring an AMOC. AFD will not issue AMOC approval numbers during site plan cycle — AMOC must be a **separate standalone submittal**, approved before site plan submission.
- **AMOC track (IFC § 104.8):** Required when standard IFC requirements cannot be met — most commonly to reduce minimum commercial fire flow below 1,500 gpm (floor: 1,000 gpm), reduce hydrant coverage, or approve pyrophoric gas storage. AMOC must be pre-approved with an AFD-issued approval number and date noted in the AFD Fire Analysis Table. "Pending"/"submitted" entries are deficient.
- **WUI track (FPCM 4.10.0):** Concurrent review by AFD Wildfire Division. Required for any property within Full/Limited Purpose Jurisdiction that the 2024 WUI Code Map covers or that AFD Wildfire designates. Separate WUI approval stamp required before final site plan approval. Map status is rebuttable only by AFD Wildfire Division — self-declared "not in WUI" is a deficiency.
- **High-rise track (IBC § 202 via LDC § 25-12-1):** Any occupied floor >75 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access triggers IBC § 403 high-rise requirements: Fire Command Center (1-hr fire barrier; exterior access or 2-hr rated passageway; FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.13 equipment list), dual remote FDCs (NFPA 14 § 7.12.2), fire pump room, dual water mains (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.e), AEDs each occupied level, simultaneous stairway-unlock controls (LDC § 25-12-173 § 508.1.6). For buildings >420 ft, mains must be in **different streets** (IFC § 914.3.1.2). Buildings between ~65–75 ft must carry three pre-CO survey notes (ZLU-29.10/.11/.12).
- **Decision body:** Fire Marshal's office; Wildfire Division (for WUI); final sign-off on cover sheet approval block.
- **Timeline reality:** AMOC review adds ~6–12 weeks before site plan submission becomes viable. WUI concurrent review rarely controls the critical path. High-rise pre-app + dual-main coordination with Austin Water can add 1–2 cycles. Any post-approval change to fire lanes, hydrants, FDCs, fire service routing, riser/pump rooms, or electric disconnect requires AFD resubmission.

## Constraints to evaluate

**Apparatus access (LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503.1.1, 503.2.1, 503.2.4 with City amendments; Appendix D not adopted).**
- Fire apparatus access road within **150 ft** (path-of-travel, not arc) of all portions of all exterior walls of the first story. AFD routinely extends to **200 ft** for buildings fully sprinklered per NFPA 13 (not 13R/13D) under Exception 1.1, but the increase is **discretionary** — plans showing 200 ft must reflect AFD authorization; high-piled combustible storage buildings (>12,000 sf area + storage >12 ft height) are locked at 150 ft regardless of sprinklers (IFC § 3206.6). High-piled storage also requires one FD access door per 100 LF of exterior wall facing the access road, max 125 ft center-to-center (IFC § 3206.6.1, § 3206.7.5).
- Measurement: actual ground-level path around obstructions ≥4 ft tall (buildings, walls, fences, grade changes); never through/under buildings; never across water-quality features; AFD will not lay supply hose across ASMP Level 3+ arterials, expressways, parkways, freeways, or toll roads. Routes that cross property lines require a recorded **JUAE or UDA** (§ 503.1.1 Exception 3).
- **Minimum unobstructed width 25 ft** face-of-curb to face-of-curb (sidewalk does not count); 14 ft minimum vertical clearance for the full width; **inside turning radius 25 ft / outside 50 ft** (§ 503.2.4). Wider than 25 ft lanes may reduce to 20-in/40-out. Divided fire lanes where aerial is not anticipated: two 15-ft lanes (Exception 2.d). Security gates: 25 ft two-way / 15 ft one-way (20 ft two-way only with prior Fire Prevention Division written approval). Throat at Level 1/2 street crosswalk: 20 ft permitted (Exception 2.e). Curb-return radii at fire-access driveways from public streets follow TCM 7.5.1.1 Table 7-1 "Fire Access" column — typically 15 ft on Level 1/2 streets (vs. 10 ft typical). Turning movements onto opposing traffic lanes or where ASMP proposes a raised median are prohibited.
- **Grade:** asphalt ≤ 13%; concrete ≤ 15%; maximum 10% change in any 20 ft; aerial setup areas ≤ ~12–13% running and 3.5% cross-slope; driveway grade change in a fire lane ≤ 6% (TCM 7.5.2.1.E, more restrictive). Where max grades cannot be met, a fully protected sprinkler system approved by AFD may substitute. Minimum drainage: 2% vegetated / alternative; 1% asphalt; 0.5% concrete.
- **Surface:** HS-20 loading (16 kips/wheel, 80,000 lbs total) for all fire lanes and all structural elements within them (manhole covers, vault lids, trench grates). Final asphalt/concrete must be in place before combustible construction begins. Alternative surfaces (grasscrete, pavers, PICP, porous asphalt/concrete) limited to ≤25% of building-perimeter fire protection, require slip-resistant surfaces at turns and 40 LF at building corners for aerial operations, reinforced mountable curb when no Type I/II apron is present, and a post-completion PE-of-record concurrence letter (§ 503.2.3.1). Pervious or decorative paving **within 100 ft of any building** requires AFD approval + PE design for 80,000 lb live load even when not formally a fire lane.

**Aerial apparatus (LDC § 25-12-173 § 503.2.6.1; AFD operational practice).**
- Aerial-clearance review begins at ~73 ft per AFD practice (2 ft before the 75-ft high-rise threshold). For high-rise and near-high-rise buildings, plans must demonstrate clear staging adjacent to the building face — typically a 25-ft setback envelope plus overhead clearance for the boom. Divided 15-ft lanes are not permitted where aerial deployment is expected; full 25-ft lane required.
- Elevated surfaces (podium slabs, plaza decks) that serve as fire apparatus access must be designed for the greater of IFC § 503.2.6 apparatus loads or IBC § 1607.8.1 live load (LDC § 25-12-3 § 1607.8.2). **Outrigger loads:** **43,200 lbs on one outrigger** or **28,600 lbs each on two adjacent outriggers** at 18-ft center spacing on 24"×24" contact (§ 503.2.6.1). Engineer of record must sign a post-completion concurrence letter. Access hatches, vault covers, and trench grates in the apparatus path must individually carry the 43,200-lb single-outrigger rating.
- Bridges/elevated fire lane crossings: AASHTO HB-17 (or current LRFD) design; load-limit signs at both entrances (§ 503.2.6).

**Dead-ends and turnarounds.**
- Dead-end fire lane >150 ft requires a turnaround per Standard 901S-2: cul-de-sac with 50-ft unobstructed radius **or** hammerhead/T 25 ft × 80 ft with 10 ft additional clearance and no obstructions over 1 ft (FPCM 4.4.0).
- Turnaround pavement must be marked fire lane on all sides; hose-lay extension from the turnaround counts toward apparatus-to-building distance.

**Hydrant coverage and spacing (LDC § 25-12-173 § 507.5.1; UCM § 2.9.2.D).**
- Primary hydrant hose-lay to all exterior walls: **400 ft** non-sprinklered (non-R-3/U); **500 ft** for buildings sprinklered throughout per NFPA 13 or 13R; **600 ft** for Group R-3 and U regardless of sprinklers.
- **Second hydrant within 500 ft (600 ft for R-3/U) when required fire flow ≥1,500 gpm; additional hydrants within 1,000 ft when fire flow >2,500 gpm. One hydrant per 1,250 gpm (or fraction).** Multi-hydrant calcs must show all required hydrants flowing simultaneously, starting at the most hydraulically remote.
- **Spacing:** **300 ft** maximum interval in commercial/high-density areas (CBD, DMU, W/LO, CS, CH, MF-4/5/6, or inside the Downtown Austin Project Coordination Zone); **600 ft** max interval elsewhere; hydrant at every major intersection; hydrants on **both sides** of any divided road regardless of arterial class (UCM 2.9.2.D.2).
- **Placement (SSM 511.4.B):** 3–6 ft behind curb gutter face; steamer center ≥18 in above grade; steamer perpendicular to and facing the curb/fire lane; ≥20 ft from curb tangency at corners; ≥9 ft (any direction) from sanitary sewer line/lateral/service/manhole (UCM 2.9.2.D.4); ≥5 ft from storm drain; ≥3 ft clear circumference; bollards where exposed to vehicles; lead line ≤55 ft from main and cannot cross a divided road.
- **Field-verified fire flow test:** AFD-conducted or AFD-witnessed only (IFC § 507.4 as locally amended); ≤1 year old at site-plan submission; on hydrants on the same main/zone serving the connection point; full FPCM Appendix E § 2.4.0 data set (static, residual, pitot, flow rate, hydrant IDs, date/time, conductor, equipment, gauge elevations).
- **Required fire flow at 20 psi residual** from IFC Appendix B Table B105.1(2) using IBC construction type + fire-flow calculation area per LDC § 25-12-173 B104.1. Commercial floor: 1,500 gpm (reducible to 1,000 gpm only with pre-approved AMOC). Sprinkler reductions per Table B105.2: NFPA 13 → 75%; NFPA 13R → 50% (capped at 50% for Type III/IV/V); NFPA 13D → 25%. **No reduction** for Group H or S-1/S-2 with high-piled or rack storage.
- Hydraulic calc C-factors are fixed by FPCM 4.4.0 Table 507-2: C=80 (iron/steel) or C=110 (plastic/copper) — software defaults of 140/150 are non-compliant. **Velocity ≤10 fps** upstream of the 6-in hydrant tap; the 6-in lead downstream is the only velocity exception.

**FDC siting (IFC § 912; LDC § 25-12-173 § 912.5; NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4).**
- Each separate sprinkler or standpipe system requires its own FDC (NFPA 13D excluded; stand-alone local <20-head systems excluded per FPCM 4.7.0). Street side, oriented to fire apparatus access, fully visible. Prohibited: under building overhangs, inside parking garages (even sprinklered), behind walls/fences, in 100-yr floodplain, in covered courtyards.
- **FDC-to-hydrant travel distance:** **100 ft** for standpipe systems (NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4); **300 ft** for sprinklered buildings without Class I standpipe (IFC § 507.5.1.1). Working space: 36 in W × 36 in D × 78 in H; mounting 18–48 in above grade.
- High-rise: minimum **two remotely located FDCs** on separate building walls as far apart as possible (NFPA 14 § 7.12.2). For multi-zone standpipe systems, at least two FDCs per zone. FDC pressure demand ceiling: **150 psi** non-high-rise / **350 psi** high-rise (FPCM 4.8.0).
- Austin-amended FDC sign: white reflective letters on red, "FDC" ≥6 in tall, other words ≥2 in, approved text strings only ("FDC", "AUTOMATIC SPRINKLERS", "STANDPIPES", "TEST CONNECTION", combinations) — "FIRE DEPARTMENT CONNECTION" is **not** an approved string. Manual standpipes must indicate "MANUAL" + "WET"/"DRY"; PRV-equipped systems indicate floor range served.

**Fire area and high-rise classification.**
- Fire-flow calculation area = total gross floor area of all stories, mezzanines, basements, mechanical, and parking levels under exterior walls and horizontal roof projections (LDC § 25-12-173 B104.1). Exceptions: Type IA/IB → three largest successive floors (construction-type-based, **not** high-rise-based); open parking garage of IA/IB per IBC § 406.5 → single largest floor; R-3/R-4/townhouse/1–2-family separated <10 ft → combined.
- Fire walls per IBC § 706 create separate fire areas **only with zero openings**. Any fire door, damper, or utility penetration disqualifies the separation.
- Podium exclusion of garage from upper fire area (IBC § 510.2) requires **both** a 3-hr fire-rated horizontal assembly with no openings **and** NFPA 13 (not 13R) in the garage.
- High-rise threshold: any occupied floor >75 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access (lowest finished grade of any adjacent fire lane / street; sloped sites use the downhill side). Standpipe trigger: highest floor >30 ft above same datum (IFC § 905.3.1). NFPA 13R disallowed for buildings ≥4 stories or with highest occupied floor ≥30 ft above lowest FD access (IFC § 903.3.1.2).
- Aerial-apparatus clearance review begins at ~73 ft per AFD operational practice — design overhead, planter, and side-yard clearances accordingly.

**WUI (LDC § 25-12-183).** Proximity Zones A (≤50 ft from ≥40 ac wildland), B (>50 ≤150 ft), C (>150 ft ≤0.5 mi from ≥40 ac, or within 1.5 mi of ≥750 ac). Most restrictive zone applies to the entire structure when it spans multiple zones. ETJ exempt.

**Underground fire main + utility interface (UCM 2.9.2.B.6; NFPA 13/24).**
- Service from public main to property line: **ductile iron** (DI); gate valve at the tap to the public main; backflow preventer inside property line, accessible for City inspection; **flow detection device** on every unmetered fire line, positioned so ≤100 gallons sit between the device and the public main.
- **NFPA 13 minimum fire service main: 6 in** (NFPA 13 § 24.1.3.1); smaller permitted only with PE-sealed hydraulic calc from a TX-licensed RME sprinkler designer. **Underground may extend ≤10 ft under building** (NFPA 13 § 10.4.3.1; NFPA 24 § 10.6.1); >10 ft triggers trench requirements (rigid walls, noncombustible base, accessible from within, drain, restrained joints, shutoff valve, freeze protection).
- Sectional control valves required when the private fire main serves **≥7 fire-protection connections** (NFPA 24 § 6.6.1). Each private hydrant gets a gate valve at the tee, restrained to the main with bolt-through connection (UCM 2.9.2.C.1). Fully restrained joints throughout (UCM 2.9.2.D).
- **NFPA 13 exterior shutoff** (NFPA 13 § 8.16.1) — one of: underground PIV ≥40 ft from building; wall-mounted PIV; exterior door direct to riser room within 15 ft walking distance (not under overhang); BFP vault (no hydrants downstream of BFP, no PIV upstream of BFP, no other valves in vault). PIVs not required for NFPA 13R/13D.
- High-rise fire pumps require **two water main connections** with independent supply piping each sized for full pump demand (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.e). Same-main exception only with valving between tap points. Buildings >420 ft: connections must be in **different streets** (IFC § 914.3.1.2). Parallel supply mains require ≥10 ft separation.

**Knox Box / Knox Switch (FPCM 4.4.0; FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.16; IFC § 506.1).**
- Knox Key Box required for any commercial structure with fire-protection systems (sprinklers, alarm, standpipe) **or** any site with physical access barriers (locked gates, fenced perimeters, bollards). Knox is the only approved brand in Austin. Must be called out on plans with a specific leader-line — a general note is insufficient.
- **Knox Key Switch** (electrical, not a key vault) required for any motorized/power-operated gate on a fire apparatus access road, ingress side. Substituting a Knox Box for a Switch at a motorized gate is deficient.
- High-rise: additional Knox Key Box per FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.13(A.5), distinct from the riser-room Knox Box.

**Construction-phase fire protection (IFC § 3313; FPCM 4.4.0 General Note 3).**
- When combustible materials arrive on site, **≥500 gpm within 500 ft** must be available (IFC § 3313). For Type I/II construction, vertical work may proceed once this supply is in place, ahead of full permanent fire flow.
- Required fire-protection infrastructure (mains, private hydrants, apparatus roadways) must be installed and operational before any combustible/vertical construction begins (IFC § 501.4). Final asphalt or concrete on apparatus access surfaces must be in place before combustible construction begins.
- Existing hydrants and FDCs must remain in service through all phases; replacement hydrants must be accepted as operational before the existing hydrant they replace is removed. Modifications to private fire mains require advance email notification to FirePrevention@austintexas.gov (IFC § 901.7.4) and return-to-service notice (§ 901.7.6).

**Pipeline ordinance (LDC §§ 25-4-134, 25-2-516).** Two-prong test: hazardous liquid per 49 CFR § 195.2 **AND** ≥8-in inside diameter. Natural gas (49 CFR Part 192) does not qualify. AFD Fire Analysis Table field must read "YES" when a qualifying pipeline is on or adjacent to the site.

## Opportunities to evaluate

- **NFPA 13 sprinklers → 75% fire-flow reduction** (cap by post-reduction floor of 1,000 gpm). Often unlocks a workable supply scenario on sites with marginal Box-number capacity. For Type III/IV/V wood-frame construction, NFPA 13R is capped at 50%; pushing to non-combustible (II-B) construction can unlock the full 75% reduction.
- **AMOC to drop the commercial minimum to 1,000 gpm** (FPCM Appendix D). Viable for small commercial buildings where the standard 1,500-gpm floor would otherwise force a new tap or main upsize. Must be approved before site plan submission — budget 6–12 weeks.
- **Podium construction (IBC § 510.2)** excludes the garage from upper-fire-area calcs and can drop fire flow by a tier — but requires 3-hr horizontal assembly with no openings **and** NFPA 13 in the garage, which costs more than NFPA 13R-throughout in soft sites.
- **200-ft sprinklered apparatus access (Exception 1.1)** is AFD-routine for NFPA 13 buildings and meaningfully expands the buildable envelope on sites where a 150-ft constraint would force unnecessary internal drives or rated breezeways.
- **Rated breezeway** (2-hr fire-rated walls + ceiling, full sprinkler, open both ends, 14-ft clearance, required signage) can satisfy apparatus access for landlocked rear-of-building exterior points where a perimeter loop is infeasible.
- **Alternative-surface fire lanes** (grasscrete, PICP, pavers) preserve open-space and water-quality goals but capped at 25% of building perimeter fire protection and require PE concurrence — useful for compact urban infill but rarely sufficient as the primary route.
- **Limited area wet pipe (NFPA 13 § 4.2)** for freestanding R-2 amenity buildings (clubhouses, leasing offices) in 13R projects — avoids forcing a full NFPA 13 design on an otherwise unsprinklered ancillary structure (FPCM 4.4.0).
- **Bureau programs:** check `bureau/jurisdictions/austin/programs/` for any AFD expedited-review or pre-approved-typology programs that may apply.

## Inputs needed from Phase 2

- **wwp.md** — Fire Flow Map Box number; AFD hydrant flow test report (≤1 yr, AFD-conducted/witnessed) with static/residual/flow and AWWA-projected available flow at 20 psi; existing hydrant locations and IDs within 500 ft; whether an SER is anticipated; existing main sizes/materials.
- **transportation.md** — ASMP Street Level of all frontages (governs apparatus turning radii per TCM Tables 7-1/7-2 and the "no hose lay across major roadway" rule); adjacent ROW widths; presence of medians/divided roadways; driveway approach geometry.
- **zoning.md / sde.md** — Base zoning district (drives 300 vs. 600 ft hydrant spacing); DAPCZ status; setback envelope (controls apparatus-to-building distance feasibility); building height envelope (drives 30-ft standpipe and 75-ft high-rise triggers).
- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — Building footprints, story count, highest occupied floor elevation, IBC construction type assumption, fire-flow calculation area per building, intended occupancy classifications, gate locations, parking-garage open/enclosed determination, podium configuration if any.
- **phase1-extraction/site-context.md** — WUI map status; proximity to ≥40 ac and ≥750 ac wildland; any hazardous-liquid pipelines (commodity + ID); floodplain boundaries (FDCs may not be in 100-yr floodplain); 2024 WUI Code Map screenshot.

## Output structure

Standard discipline output shape per `references/phase3-disciplines.md`. Include the AFD Fire Analysis Table fields as a structured findings table — IFC edition (governed by **original** submission date), construction type, high-rise Yes/No (with the 75-ft datum), fire area (with calc method), IWUIC edition + Proximity Zone, AMOC status, pipeline-ordinance Yes/No — because Phase 4 will lift these into the diligence report.

## Severity heuristics

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| Required fire flow (post-sprinkler reduction) exceeds AWWA-calculated available flow at 20 psi — capacity upgrade (new tap, main upsize, SER, or storage tank + fire pump) required | `significant` |
| Building >75 ft above lowest FD access without dual-main supply, fire pump, FCC, or required high-rise envelope — concept needs redesign or alternative procurement track | `significant` |
| Property in WUI Zone A or B without site-design accommodation (defensible space, ignition-resistant exterior, modified setbacks); or qualifying hazardous pipeline triggers buffer/easement constraint | `significant` |
| Aerial apparatus required (highest occupied floor approaching 75 ft) but setbacks, overhead clearances, or HS-20 setup pads don't accommodate it | `significant` |
| Apparatus access path-of-travel exceeds 200 ft to one or more exterior building points on a sprinklered building, or >150 ft non-sprinklered, with no rated-breezeway or second-passage option | `significant` |
| Fire-area calc method depends on Type IA/IB classification, podium § 510.2 exclusion, or fire-wall separation that materially changes required fire flow tier — design margin is thin | `moderate` |
| AMOC needed to clear commercial 1,500 gpm floor (down to 1,000 gpm) — schedule risk of 6–12 weeks pre-submittal | `moderate` |
| Dead-end aisle >150 ft without turnaround, or cul-de-sac/hammerhead geometry below 901S-2 spec | `moderate` |
| Hydrant nominally beyond required spacing but workable with new tap on existing main; second-hydrant trigger at 1,500 gpm not yet addressed | `moderate` |
| Cross-property fire access requires a JUAE/UDA not yet recorded | `moderate` |
| Alternative-surface fire lane proposed for >25% of perimeter, or pervious paving within 100 ft of buildings without AFD PE-design pathway | `moderate` |
| Standard commercial/multifamily occupancy with adequate hydrant coverage, NFPA 13 sprinklers, and apparatus access within standard envelope | `note` |
| AFD General Notes verbatim from FPCM § 4.4.0; AFD Fire Analysis Table complete with correct IFC edition for original submission date | `note` |

## Common pitfalls

- **Citing IFC Appendix D for apparatus access** — Austin does not adopt Appendix D. Access is governed by LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503–507.5 with local amendments.
- **Using the wrong IFC edition.** Original submission date governs, not resubmittal: 2012 IFC (pre 1/7/18) → 2015 IFC → 2021 IFC (9/1/21–7/9/25) → **2024 IFC (7/10/25 onward).** FPCM Appendix D still internally references 2012 IFC; LDC governs.
- **Substituting the Fire Flow Map Box nominal value for an AWWA-calculated available flow** at 20 psi from actual AFD test data. The Box is a modeled value; the calculated flow must come from the test.
- **Confusing high-rise (height) and Type IA/IB (construction type).** Three-largest-floors fire-area exception is **construction-type-based**. A Type IIIA high-rise does not get it; a Type IA low-rise does.
- **NFPA 13R applied to a 4-story or ≥30-ft-occupied-floor building** — disallowed; full NFPA 13 required (IFC § 903.3.1.2). The 30-ft datum is the lowest level of fire department vehicle access, not average grade or primary entry.
- **Assuming the 200-ft sprinklered access distance is automatic.** It is a discretionary increase by the fire code official; high-piled storage buildings (>12,000 sf + >12 ft storage) are locked at 150 ft.
- **Hose-lay measured as straight-line, arc, or through a water-quality pond.** Path of travel only, around obstructions ≥4 ft tall, never across major arterials/expressways/parkways/freeways/toll roads, never diagonally across intersections.
- **Self-declaring "not in WUI."** Only AFD Wildfire Division determines applicability and Proximity Zone, regardless of map status. ETJ parcels are exempt.
- **AMOC entered as "pending" or "submitted"** in the AFD Fire Analysis Table — must be an AFD-issued approval number and date from a separate, prior, standalone submittal.
- **C-factor 140 or 150** in private fire-main hydraulic calcs (software defaults). Required: C=80 iron/steel; C=110 plastic/copper/resin-lined (FPCM 4.4.0 Table 507-2).
- **Hydrants placed within 9 ft of any sanitary sewer** (any direction) or in/within 6 in of a sidewalk/ramp — both are common SSM 511.4.B / UCM 2.9.2.D.4 fails.
- **Mistaking a natural-gas pipeline for a "hazardous pipeline."** The ordinance requires hazardous liquid under 49 CFR Part 195 **and** ≥8-in ID. Natural gas (Part 192) does not qualify.
- **ETJ parcels: ESD authority.** Within Travis County (ESD #2), Hays County, Williamson County, or city limits of Buda etc., AFD does not govern — confirm the correct fire authority before applying any Austin-specific rule.
- **Knox Box in a general note only.** FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.16 requires a specific leader-line callout with location and size; a plan note saying "Knox Box to be provided" is deficient.
- **"IFC 503.3.3.2" cited on plans.** This section does not exist in Austin's adopted code; correct authority for fire-zone marking is FPCM 4.4.0 General Construction Notes and LDC § 25-12-173 § 503.3.2.
- **Fire lane labels on water utility easement drawings.** Fire-zone designation is exclusively AFD jurisdiction (§§ 503.3, 503.1.4); placing fire-lane labels on AW utility easement plats implies utility-department enforcement and is a deficiency.
- **Bare "IFC" terminology in fire-flow demand tables.** UCM 2.9.2.A.3.b requires "City of Austin Fire Code" terminology, with "City of Austin Local Amendments" attached to every IFC section citation.
- **AFD General Notes modified from FPCM § 4.4.0 verbatim language** or augmented with Knox Box specs or non-AFD jurisdictions (Travis County ESD #2, etc.) — must be exact FPCM text, six notes only.
- **AFD Fire Analysis Table combined with the Austin Water Project Information Table.** Must be a standalone table on the cover sheet with nine required left-column fields verbatim (FPCM § 4.4.0).
- **Treating the Fire Flow Zone Box number as the available flow.** The Box reflects modeled capacity; available flow at 20 psi must be AWWA-calculated from actual AFD test data, and the two values must reconcile on plans.
- **Fire main interconnected with domestic supply or backed up by a domestic meter.** Prohibited (NFPA 13 § 16.9.3.1); cross-connection protection by reduced-pressure backflow assembly is required (IFC § 507.6 as locally amended).

     7→Excludes: detailed trail design (covered by `ta` discipline for off-street network connectivity; on-site trail geometric design pulled from PARD/TCM is referenced here only as it bears on amenity cost and feasibility), and landscape/tree protection (covered by `el` discipline).

     9→## Authoritative sources
    10→
    11→- **Current ordinance:** Austin LDC Chapter 25-1, Article 14, §§ 25-1-601 through 25-1-612 (effective January 1, 2024 per Ord. 20231130-087, which fully repealed and renumbered the prior Article 14)
    12→- **Operating procedures:** PDOP Rule R161-16.15 (uses pre-2024 LDC cross-references; cite by PDOP section, not embedded LDC numbers)
    13→- **Determination:** LDC § 25-1-610 (Parkland Dedication Determination, replacing the informal "PED letter")
    14→- **Construction on City parkland:** Texas Parks and Wildlife Code, Chapter 26, operationalized by ECM § 5.4.1
    15→- **Fee schedule:** PARD annual fee schedule, updated October 1 each year. State formula set by Texas HB 1526 (2023); the City has no discretion over formula structure.
    16→- **Urban trail design (if amenities include trail):** TCM § 5.3 and Standard Detail 1302S-1
    17→- **District overlays:** ERC Regulating Plan § 4.10.3; NBG 3.5.8.D; LDC Subchapter E § 2.7 (private common open space) and § 2.3.1 (Table B connectivity)
    18→
    19→## Regulatory pathway
    20→
    21→Parkland dedication in Austin attaches at **site plan** (for multifamily and hotel/motel) and at **subdivision** (for single-family residential). Commercial, retail, and industrial uses are **not** subject to parkland dedication — the prior commercial requirement (Ord. 20220915-053) was repealed January 1, 2024. Civic uses (43 classifications in LDC § 25-2-6(B)) are also outside the scope of § 25-1-601(C).
    22→
    23→Sequence:
    24→1. **Pre-application:** Request a **Parkland Dedication Determination** from the PARD Director under LDC § 25-1-610. The Director specifies the satisfaction method (land, fee, easement, or combination), required acreage, preferred dedication location, off-site proximity limit, and any trail/connectivity conditions. Validity: lesser of 2 years (LDC § 25-1-610(D)) or 1 year (PDOP 14.3.5(B)) — assume 1 year. The Determination becomes stale if unit count changes by more than 10%.
    25→2. **At site plan submittal:** Coversheet note must reference the Determination, current LDC Article 14, satisfaction method, unit counts, exempt units, and CO-timing for any unpaid multifamily fee.
    26→3. **Before site plan release** (multifamily) **or final plat approval** (single-family): legal instruments executed — fee simple deed and ORS-coordinated transfer package; or recorded park easement; or recorded private parkland access easement under LDC § 25-1-605(E).
    27→4. **Before CO** (multifamily): fee paid per LDC § 25-1-609(B).
    28→5. **If construction touches existing City parkland:** Chapter 26 process (Parks Board hearing → City Council easement) plus PIA/PIMA — months-long timeline, not a paperwork item.
    29→
    30→Decision body: PARD Director administers; Land Use Commission for Subchapter E waivers; City Council for Chapter 26 easements.
    31→
    32→## Constraints to evaluate
    33→
    34→### Applicability and exemptions
    35→
    36→- **Use types subject:** residential dwelling units and hotel/motel rooms only. Verify all units are non-exempt before relying on a fee figure (LDC § 25-1-601(C)).
    37→- **Exempt unit categories** (LDC § 25-1-601(D)): SMART Housing-certified units (D)(3); units income-restricted under any municipal/county/state/federal affordable housing program (D)(4) — broader than SMART, includes LIHTC, HUD Section 8, etc.; prior dedication credits (D)(1); Travis County ETJ (D)(2). The (D)(3) and (D)(4) exemptions are independent — a project may stack them across different units.
    38→- **Site in ETJ:** parkland dedication does **not** apply at site plan stage (LDC § 25-1-601(D)(2)). Confirm jurisdictional status; sites that straddle city limits must address each portion separately.
    39→
    40→### Calculation — multifamily
    41→
    42→- Formula: `[(# MF units × 0.005) + (# hotel/motel rooms × 0.004)] × Avg Land Value × (1/Density Factor)` where Density Factor = 1 Suburban, 4 Urban, 40 CBD (LDC § 25-1-608).
    43→- **Geographic Area designation is not self-selectable.** The Suburban/Urban/CBD boundary ordinance is not in Bureau. Confirm via the Determination letter or explicit PARD comment. Do **not** infer from neighborhood name or zoning.
    44→- Land dedication cap: 10% of gross site area (LDC § 25-1-603(D)).
    45→- Payment timing: **before CO**, not site plan release (LDC § 25-1-609(B)).
    46→- Reference rates (per multifamily unit, FY 2025): CBD $2,427.65; Urban $4,676.52; Suburban $2,544.94. Rates update October 1 — verify current schedule before relying on these for pro forma.
    47→
    48→### Calculation — single-family
    49→
    50→- Density-based residents-per-unit multipliers (LDC § 25-1-602(C)): Low Density ≤6 DU/acre = 2.8; Medium 6–12 DU/acre = 2.2; High >12 DU/acre = 1.7.
    51→- Urban Core single-family cap: **15% of gross site area** (LDC § 25-1-602(E)). This is a ceiling, not a minimum; formula amounts above 15% are converted to fee-in-lieu for the remainder.
    52→- Two distinct single-family fees apply: fee-in-lieu (§ 25-1-606) and the parkland development fee (§ 25-1-607). Both due before plat/site plan approval.
    53→
    54→### Land dedication — physical eligibility (PDOP § 14.3.7)
    55→
    56→- **Minimum parcel size:** ¼ acre per dedicated parcel (§ 14.3.7(A)(7)(a)).
    57→- **Visibility:** interior *should* be visible from public ROW — ≥200 ft frontage per 2 acres for parks ≥2 acres; ≥half the widest dimension for parks <2 acres (§ 14.3.7(A)(1); "should," not "shall").
    58→- **Grade and active-play:** ≥50% *should* be ≤10% grade, well-drained, suitable for active play (§ 14.3.7(A)(2); "should"). Exception for trail connections or environmental/cultural resource preservation.
    59→- **Utility connections (mandatory):** potable water on all park sites; sewer on sites ≥2 acres (§ 14.3.7(A)(4)).
    60→- **Encumbrances (mandatory):** no recorded easement that prevents amenity construction (§ 14.3.7(A)(3)). AE electrical easements and utility easements within the parkland boundary are common disqualifiers. Transmission easement land cannot be labeled or dedicated as parkland (UCM § 1.14.7).
    61→- **Creek/water-body adjacency:** dedication must be by **fee simple deed**, not park easement (PARD reviewer convention — uniformly enforced).
    62→- **Off-site dedication proximity:** ¼ mile within the Parkland Dedication Urban Core; ½ mile outside (PDOP § 14.3.7(B)). No 1½-mile alternative exists in current code despite older references.
    63→
    64→### Partial credit framework (PDOP § 14.3.8)
    65→
    66→The credit table must break out by encumbrance category. Common rates:
    67→
    68→| Land condition | Credit |
    69→|---|---|
    70→| Unencumbered upland | up to 100% |
    71→| 25-year floodplain | **0%** (must still be dedicated; no exception) |
    72→| 100-year floodplain (outside 25-yr) | 50% — only if adjacent 25-yr floodplain is also included |
    73→| CEF buffer / CWQZ where amenities **allowed** | 50% |
    74→| CEF buffer / CWQZ where amenities **not allowed** | 0% |
    75→| Water quality / detention pond with PARD-approved amenities | 50% |
    76→| Fire lane functioning as a trail connecting to a larger system | 50% |
    77→
    78→No 60% credit for trail or park easements exists in current PDOP — a credit table showing this is incorrect.
    79→
    80→### Private parkland credit (LDC § 25-1-605)
    81→
    82→- Up to 100% credit for privately owned, publicly accessible parkland meeting PDOP § 14.3.10 standards.
    83→- Recreational easement must include all five required provisions (PDOP § 14.3.10(B)(3)): maintenance, capital replacement, City inspection rights, future construction rights, penalties; plus a repayment clause if released (PDOP § 14.3.10(B)(4)).
    84→- Charter Article II § 7(A) declaration earns 30% weighted credit boost (PDOP § 14.3.10(C)(2)).
    85→- Separate access easement recorded before site plan approval (LDC § 25-1-605(E)).
    86→
    87→### Construction on existing City parkland — Chapter 26 trigger
    88→
    89→Any construction — including drainage outfalls, utility crossings, trail work, grading, staging, or temporary access — on land labeled "City of Austin (Parkland)" or "Dedicated Parkland" triggers Texas Parks and Wildlife Code Chapter 26 (ECM § 5.4.1). Zero de minimis. Required: (1) Parks Board hearing, (2) City Council hearing + easement, (3) field notes, (4) mitigation plan, (5) no-feasible-alternative finding, (6) harm-minimization plan. **Timeline: typically 6–9 months** including the Council easement; assume this is a long-pole item if any project work touches existing parkland.
    90→
    91→PIA (Parkland Improvement Agreement) and PIMA (Parkland Improvement and Maintenance Agreement) are PARD administrative instruments layered on top of Chapter 26. PARD maintains **concrete** trails but does **not** maintain DG or other non-concrete surfaces — PIMA must assign DG maintenance to a non-PARD party.
    92→
    93→### District overlays (use-specific stacking)
    94→
    95→- **ERC sites ≥20 acres:** minimum 5% of gross site area dedicated on-site, regardless of formula amount (ERC § 4.10.3(B)). ERC Development Bonus PAOS layer is independent — see "Opportunities."
    96→- **NBG / ERC:** mandatory pedestrian/bicycle connection to adjacent public parkland (NBG 3.5.8.D; ERC 3.5.7.b.3) when site is adjacent to parkland.
    97→- **LDC Subchapter E § 2.7:** all site plans ≥2 acres OR all MF/condo uses must devote ≥5% of gross site area to private common open space. This is separate from parkland dedication — qualifying types include landscape areas (≥650 sf, 20 ft min dim), multi-use trails, pools, play areas. Multi-use trails connecting to an UTMP corridor qualify (§ 2.7.3.A.8).
    98→- **LDC Subchapter E § 2.3.1:** Table B Option 6 (multi-use trail easement) is an optional connectivity measure for sites ≥3 ac non-residential OR <3 ac with parking between building and street. Option 6 requires Director of Public Works approval — a common deficiency is selecting Option 6 without the DPW letter.
    99→
   100→### Fiscal surety
   101→
   102→- For private parkland with amenities (LDC § 25-1-605(C)): surety = fee-in-lieu + development fee.
   103→- For amenity construction in lieu of development fee (LDC § 25-1-607(C)): surety = development fee amount.
   104→- **PARD written notification prerequisite (PDOP § 14.3.10(E)):** PARD must notify applicant and Development Services Fiscal Office in writing stating amenities and surety amount **before** posting. Applicant cannot self-calculate.
   105→- Acceptable instruments (LDC § 25-1-112): cash, performance bond, letter of credit. Amount = estimated **City** cost (not applicant cost), by a qualified professional, Director-approved.
   106→
   107→### PUD / development agreement projects
   108→
   109→PUD ordinance may impose different or additional parkland obligations (LDC § 25-1-601(F)). Estancia and Domain are governed by project-specific instruments not in Bureau. For PUDs with Parkland Improvement Agreements, the PIA controls schedule and per-unit fee structure — verify against the ordinance.
   110→
   111→## Opportunities to evaluate
   112→
   113→- **SMART Housing or income-restricted unit certification fully exempts those units** from parkland dedication. For a 300-unit Urban MF project at $4,676.52/unit, full SMART certification erases ~$1.4M in fees (see `bureau/jurisdictions/austin/programs/parkland-dedication.md` and `programs/smart-housing.md`). Even a partial DB90-style 12% affordable carve-out saves ~$140K. **This is typically the largest available fee reduction lever.**
   114→- **CBD vs. Urban geographic area** — CBD rate ($2,427.65) is ~48% lower than Urban ($4,676.52). For sites near the boundary, request PARD confirmation of CBD designation in the Determination — the geographic boundary ordinance is not on plan documents.
   115→- **Land dedication in lieu of fee** — if the site has an unencumbered upland parcel that PARD wants in a deficient park area, land dedication may be cheaper than the formula fee. Land value × acres dedicated offsets the fee on a $/acre basis (§ 25-1-608(F) hybrid formula).
   116→- **Amenity construction in lieu of development fee** (LDC § 25-1-607(C) for SF; LDC § 25-1-608(H) for MF): credit up to the fee amount for PARD-approved on-site amenities. Useful when an amenity is being built anyway for project marketing (playgrounds, fitness stations, dog parks, picnic areas).
   117→- **Multi-use trail as Subchapter E § 2.7 open space amenity** — counts toward the 5% private common open space requirement AND can satisfy Subchapter E § 2.3.1 Table B Option 6 connectivity (with DPW approval). When site abuts an Urban Trails Plan corridor, the trail you'd build anyway can knock out two requirements.
   118→- **ERC Development Bonus PAOS** — for ERC bonus projects, 25% of the Bonus Area must be PAOS; this PAOS is **in addition to** baseline parkland and § 2.7 open space, but it does mean the project gets bonus density for open space it might dedicate anyway. Cannot combine with ERC § 4.9/4.10 fee-in-lieu (§ 6.4.2.B.9).
   119→- **Charter Article II § 7(A) declaration** in a private parkland easement = 30% credit boost (PDOP § 14.3.10(C)(2)). Costs nothing to include.
   120→- **Stormwater/water quality pond as 50%-credit parkland** — if the project has a detention pond, designing it with PARD-approved recreational amenities (perimeter walking path, benches) yields 50% credit toward the dedication. Combines a required engineering feature with parkland credit.
   121→
   122→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
   123→
   124→- **programs.md** — current SMART Housing eligibility, parkland fee schedule, ERC PAOS path, DB90 affordability set-asides
   125→- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — proposed unit count (MF + SF + hotel/motel rooms), gross site area, site boundary, drainage and amenity features
   126→- **zoning-pathway.md** — base zoning, overlay districts (WO, CVC, NBG, ERC, ETOD), PUD designation, ETJ vs. full-purpose jurisdiction status
   127→- **environmental.md** — floodplain delineation (25-yr and 100-yr), CEF locations and buffers, CWQZ boundary, creek/waterway adjacency, transmission easements
   128→- **affordability-strategy.md** — % SMART/income-restricted units planned, which density bonus program is being pursued (drives parkland exemption count directly)
   129→- **PARD Parkland Dedication Determination letter** — if the project is far enough along to have requested one; otherwise flag as a required pre-application step
   130→
   131→## Output structure
   132→
   133→Standard discipline output shape per `references/phase3-disciplines.md`. Lead with a fee/dedication estimate range (with confidence flag if Geographic Area is unconfirmed), then constraints, then opportunities (SMART exemption first).
   134→
   135→## Severity heuristics
   136→
   137→| Finding | Severity |
   138→|---|---|
   139→| Multifamily fee estimate > 5% of total project hard costs and no SMART/affordability path identified | `significant` |
   140→| Existing City parkland on or directly adjacent to site requiring construction access — Chapter 26 process required | `significant` (6–9 month critical path) |
   141→| Site is creek/water-body adjacent and dedication has been assumed via easement (must be fee simple deed) | `significant` |
   142→| Geographic Area (CBD/Urban/Suburban) cannot be confirmed; fee estimate is range only | `data-gap` |
   143→| ERC site ≥20 acres — 5% on-site dedication required regardless of formula | `moderate` |
   144→| Land dedication being considered but site has no contiguous ¼-acre parcel meeting PDOP § 14.3.7 standards | `moderate` (fee-only path; raise budget) |
   145→| 25-year floodplain on site being counted toward parkland credit | `moderate` (mandatory 0% credit) |
   146→| AE / transmission easement on site overlapping prospective parkland boundary | `moderate` (cannot label as parkland) |
   147→| Determination letter not yet requested; project past concept stage | `moderate` (precondition for any fee/method certainty) |
   148→| SMART Housing certification feasible and not currently planned | `note` (opportunity — call out fee savings) |
   149→| Project includes a detention pond that could double as parkland at 50% credit | `note` (opportunity) |
   150→| Site is in ETJ; no parkland dedication applies | `note` (confirm and move on) |
   151→| Civic/commercial-only project (no residential or hotel/motel units) | `note` (out of scope; no obligation) |
   152→| Fee schedule referenced is more than 12 months old | `data-gap` (rates change Oct 1) |
   153→
   154→## Common pitfalls
   155→
   156→- **Citing the repealed 2016 Ordinance (Ord. 20160128-086)** on a coversheet for a post-2024 application. Current authority is LDC Article 14 as restructured by Ord. 20231130-087.
   157→- **Treating commercial square footage as fee-bearing.** Commercial parkland was repealed January 1, 2024. Don't include retail, office, or industrial in fee calcs.
   158→- **Self-assigning a Geographic Area** ("we think we're Urban") without PARD confirmation in the Determination. The boundary ordinance is not on plans and not in Bureau.
   159→- **Stating multifamily fee due "before site plan approval."** It's due before CO (LDC § 25-1-609(B)). Single-family fees are due before plat/site plan approval — different rule.
   160→- **Assuming Geographic Area = Parkland Dedication Urban Core.** These are two distinct concepts. Urban Core governs the 15% SF cap and off-site proximity; Geographic Area governs the multifamily fee amount only.
   161→- **Counting the 15% Urban Core figure as a minimum** dedication. It's the maximum — formula above 15% converts to fee-in-lieu for the overage.
   162→- **Assuming a park easement is fine for creek-adjacent parkland.** PARD requires fee simple deed for waterway-adjacent dedications by consistent reviewer convention.
   163→- **Counting 25-year floodplain at any nonzero credit.** Always 0% (PDOP § 14.3.8). The land may still need to be included but earns no credit.
   164→- **Forgetting that the Determination expires.** Treat as expired at 1 year (PDOP 14.3.5(B)) or upon a >10% unit count change. Long-running entitlement timelines outlast Determinations.
   165→- **Skipping the Chapter 26 process** for "minor" work on existing parkland (utility tie-ins, staging, drainage outfalls). There is no de minimis exception — flag the full 6-step process.
   166→- **Posting fiscal surety based on a self-calculated cost estimate** without the PARD written notification letter (PDOP § 14.3.10(E)). PARD sets the surety amount in writing to the Fiscal Office; applicant cannot front-run it.
   167→- **Treating a PIA as a substitute for the Chapter 26 Council easement** (or vice versa). These are distinct, layered requirements when work occurs on dedicated parkland.
   168→- **Confusing private common open space (Subchapter E § 2.7)** with dedicated parkland. They satisfy different requirements; the § 2.7 5% does not satisfy parkland dedication and vice versa.
   169→- **Assuming the PARD amenity pricing guide and Geographic Area boundaries are in Bureau.** They're external documents — flag for PARD verification at cost-estimate and fee-confirmation steps.
   170→

- **District overlays:** ERC Regulating Plan § 4.10.3; NBG 3.5.8.D; LDC Subchapter E § 2.7 (private common open space) and § 2.3.1 (Table B connectivity)

## Regulatory pathway

Parkland dedication in Austin attaches at **site plan** (for multifamily and hotel/motel) and at **subdivision** (for single-family residential). Commercial, retail, and industrial uses are **not** subject to parkland dedication — the prior commercial requirement (Ord. 20220915-053) was repealed January 1, 2024. Civic uses (43 classifications in LDC § 25-2-6(B)) are also outside the scope of § 25-1-601(C).

- **Exempt unit categories** (LDC § 25-1-601(D)): SMART Housing-certified units (D)(3); units income-restricted under any municipal/county/state/federal affordable housing program (D)(4) — broader than SMART, includes LIHTC, HUD Section 8, etc.; prior dedication credits (D)(1); Travis County ETJ (D)(2). The (D)(3) and (D)(4) exemptions are independent — a project may stack them across different units.
- **Site in ETJ:** parkland dedication does **not** apply at site plan stage (LDC § 25-1-601(D)(2)). Confirm jurisdictional status; sites that straddle city limits must address each portion separately.

### Calculation — multifamily

- Formula: `[(# MF units × 0.005) + (# hotel/motel rooms × 0.004)] × Avg Land Value × (1/Density Factor)` where Density Factor = 1 Suburban, 4 Urban, 40 CBD (LDC § 25-1-608).
- **Geographic Area designation is not self-selectable.** The Suburban/Urban/CBD boundary ordinance is not in Bureau. Confirm via the Determination letter or explicit PARD comment. Do **not** infer from neighborhood name or zoning.
- Land dedication cap: 10% of gross site area (LDC § 25-1-603(D)).
- Payment timing: **before CO**, not site plan release (LDC § 25-1-609(B)).
- Reference rates (per multifamily unit, FY 2025): CBD $2,427.65; Urban $4,676.52; Suburban $2,544.94. Rates update October 1 — verify current schedule before relying on these for pro forma.

### Calculation — single-family

- Density-based residents-per-unit multipliers (LDC § 25-1-602(C)): Low Density ≤6 DU/acre = 2.8; Medium 6–12 DU/acre = 2.2; High >12 DU/acre = 1.7.
- Urban Core single-family cap: **15% of gross site area** (LDC § 25-1-602(E)). This is a ceiling, not a minimum; formula amounts above 15% are converted to fee-in-lieu for the remainder.
- Two distinct single-family fees apply: fee-in-lieu (§ 25-1-606) and the parkland development fee (§ 25-1-607). Both due before plat/site plan approval.

### Land dedication — physical eligibility (PDOP § 14.3.7)

- **Minimum parcel size:** ¼ acre per dedicated parcel (§ 14.3.7(A)(7)(a)).
- **Visibility:** interior *should* be visible from public ROW — ≥200 ft frontage per 2 acres for parks ≥2 acres; ≥half the widest dimension for parks <2 acres (§ 14.3.7(A)(1); "should," not "shall").
- **Grade and active-play:** ≥50% *should* be ≤10% grade, well-drained, suitable for active play (§ 14.3.7(A)(2); "should"). Exception for trail connections or environmental/cultural resource preservation.
- **Utility connections (mandatory):** potable water on all park sites; sewer on sites ≥2 acres (§ 14.3.7(A)(4)).
- **Encumbrances (mandatory):** no recorded easement that prevents amenity construction (§ 14.3.7(A)(3)). AE electrical easements and utility easements within the parkland boundary are common disqualifiers. Transmission easement land cannot be labeled or dedicated as parkland (UCM § 1.14.7).
- **Creek/water-body adjacency:** dedication must be by **fee simple deed**, not park easement (PARD reviewer convention — uniformly enforced).
- **Off-site dedication proximity:** ¼ mile within the Parkland Dedication Urban Core; ½ mile outside (PDOP § 14.3.7(B)). No 1½-mile alternative exists in current code despite older references.

### Partial credit framework (PDOP § 14.3.8)

The credit table must break out by encumbrance category. Common rates:

| Land condition | Credit |
|---|---|
| Unencumbered upland | up to 100% |
| 25-year floodplain | **0%** (must still be dedicated; no exception) |
| 100-year floodplain (outside 25-yr) | 50% — only if adjacent 25-yr floodplain is also included |
| CEF buffer / CWQZ where amenities **allowed** | 50% |
| CEF buffer / CWQZ where amenities **not allowed** | 0% |
| Water quality / detention pond with PARD-approved amenities | 50% |
| Fire lane functioning as a trail connecting to a larger system | 50% |

No 60% credit for trail or park easements exists in current PDOP — a credit table showing this is incorrect.

### Private parkland credit (LDC § 25-1-605)

- Up to 100% credit for privately owned, publicly accessible parkland meeting PDOP § 14.3.10 standards.
- Recreational easement must include all five required provisions (PDOP § 14.3.10(B)(3)): maintenance, capital replacement, City inspection rights, future construction rights, penalties; plus a repayment clause if released (PDOP § 14.3.10(B)(4)).
- Charter Article II § 7(A) declaration earns 30% weighted credit boost (PDOP § 14.3.10(C)(2)).
- Separate access easement recorded before site plan approval (LDC § 25-1-605(E)).

### Construction on existing City parkland — Chapter 26 trigger

Any construction — including drainage outfalls, utility crossings, trail work, grading, staging, or temporary access — on land labeled "City of Austin (Parkland)" or "Dedicated Parkland" triggers Texas Parks and Wildlife Code Chapter 26 (ECM § 5.4.1). Zero de minimis. Required: (1) Parks Board hearing, (2) City Council hearing + easement, (3) field notes, (4) mitigation plan, (5) no-feasible-alternative finding, (6) harm-minimization plan. **Timeline: typically 6–9 months** including the Council easement; assume this is a long-pole item if any project work touches existing parkland.

PIA (Parkland Improvement Agreement) and PIMA (Parkland Improvement and Maintenance Agreement) are PARD administrative instruments layered on top of Chapter 26. PARD maintains **concrete** trails but does **not** maintain DG or other non-concrete surfaces — PIMA must assign DG maintenance to a non-PARD party.

### District overlays (use-specific stacking)

- **ERC sites ≥20 acres:** minimum 5% of gross site area dedicated on-site, regardless of formula amount (ERC § 4.10.3(B)). ERC Development Bonus PAOS layer is independent — see "Opportunities."
- **NBG / ERC:** mandatory pedestrian/bicycle connection to adjacent public parkland (NBG 3.5.8.D; ERC 3.5.7.b.3) when site is adjacent to parkland.
- **LDC Subchapter E § 2.7:** all site plans ≥2 acres OR all MF/condo uses must devote ≥5% of gross site area to private common open space. This is separate from parkland dedication — qualifying types include landscape areas (≥650 sf, 20 ft min dim), multi-use trails, pools, play areas. Multi-use trails connecting to an UTMP corridor qualify (§ 2.7.3.A.8).
- **LDC Subchapter E § 2.3.1:** Table B Option 6 (multi-use trail easement) is an optional connectivity measure for sites ≥3 ac non-residential OR <3 ac with parking between building and street. Option 6 requires Director of Public Works approval — a common deficiency is selecting Option 6 without the DPW letter.

### Fiscal surety

- For private parkland with amenities (LDC § 25-1-605(C)): surety = fee-in-lieu + development fee.
- For amenity construction in lieu of development fee (LDC § 25-1-607(C)): surety = development fee amount.
- **PARD written notification prerequisite (PDOP § 14.3.10(E)):** PARD must notify applicant and Development Services Fiscal Office in writing stating amenities and surety amount **before** posting. Applicant cannot self-calculate.
- Acceptable instruments (LDC § 25-1-112): cash, performance bond, letter of credit. Amount = estimated **City** cost (not applicant cost), by a qualified professional, Director-approved.

### PUD / development agreement projects

PUD ordinance may impose different or additional parkland obligations (LDC § 25-1-601(F)). Estancia and Domain are governed by project-specific instruments not in Bureau. For PUDs with Parkland Improvement Agreements, the PIA controls schedule and per-unit fee structure — verify against the ordinance.

## Opportunities to evaluate

- **SMART Housing or income-restricted unit certification fully exempts those units** from parkland dedication. For a 300-unit Urban MF project at $4,676.52/unit, full SMART certification erases ~$1.4M in fees (see `bureau/jurisdictions/austin/programs/parkland-dedication.md` and `programs/smart-housing.md`). Even a partial DB90-style 12% affordable carve-out saves ~$140K. **This is typically the largest available fee reduction lever.**
- **CBD vs. Urban geographic area** — CBD rate ($2,427.65) is ~48% lower than Urban ($4,676.52). For sites near the boundary, request PARD confirmation of CBD designation in the Determination — the geographic boundary ordinance is not on plan documents.
- **Land dedication in lieu of fee** — if the site has an unencumbered upland parcel that PARD wants in a deficient park area, land dedication may be cheaper than the formula fee. Land value × acres dedicated offsets the fee on a $/acre basis (§ 25-1-608(F) hybrid formula).
- **Amenity construction in lieu of development fee** (LDC § 25-1-607(C) for SF; LDC § 25-1-608(H) for MF): credit up to the fee amount for PARD-approved on-site amenities. Useful when an amenity is being built anyway for project marketing (playgrounds, fitness stations, dog parks, picnic areas).
- **Multi-use trail as Subchapter E § 2.7 open space amenity** — counts toward the 5% private common open space requirement AND can satisfy Subchapter E § 2.3.1 Table B Option 6 connectivity (with DPW approval). When site abuts an Urban Trails Plan corridor, the trail you'd build anyway can knock out two requirements.
- **ERC Development Bonus PAOS** — for ERC bonus projects, 25% of the Bonus Area must be PAOS; this PAOS is **in addition to** baseline parkland and § 2.7 open space, but it does mean the project gets bonus density for open space it might dedicate anyway. Cannot combine with ERC § 4.9/4.10 fee-in-lieu (§ 6.4.2.B.9).
- **Charter Article II § 7(A) declaration** in a private parkland easement = 30% credit boost (PDOP § 14.3.10(C)(2)). Costs nothing to include.
- **Stormwater/water quality pond as 50%-credit parkland** — if the project has a detention pond, designing it with PARD-approved recreational amenities (perimeter walking path, benches) yields 50% credit toward the dedication. Combines a required engineering feature with parkland credit.

## Inputs needed from Phase 2

- **programs.md** — current SMART Housing eligibility, parkland fee schedule, ERC PAOS path, DB90 affordability set-asides
- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — proposed unit count (MF + SF + hotel/motel rooms), gross site area, site boundary, drainage and amenity features
- **zoning-pathway.md** — base zoning, overlay districts (WO, CVC, NBG, ERC, ETOD), PUD designation, ETJ vs. full-purpose jurisdiction status
- **environmental.md** — floodplain delineation (25-yr and 100-yr), CEF locations and buffers, CWQZ boundary, creek/waterway adjacency, transmission easements
- **affordability-strategy.md** — % SMART/income-restricted units planned, which density bonus program is being pursued (drives parkland exemption count directly)
- **PARD Parkland Dedication Determination letter** — if the project is far enough along to have requested one; otherwise flag as a required pre-application step

## Output structure

Standard discipline output shape per `references/phase3-disciplines.md`. Lead with a fee/dedication estimate range (with confidence flag if Geographic Area is unconfirmed), then constraints, then opportunities (SMART exemption first).

## Severity heuristics

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| Multifamily fee estimate > 5% of total project hard costs and no SMART/affordability path identified | `significant` |
| Existing City parkland on or directly adjacent to site requiring construction access — Chapter 26 process required | `significant` (6–9 month critical path) |
| Site is creek/water-body adjacent and dedication has been assumed via easement (must be fee simple deed) | `significant` |
| Geographic Area (CBD/Urban/Suburban) cannot be confirmed; fee estimate is range only | `data-gap` |
| ERC site ≥20 acres — 5% on-site dedication required regardless of formula | `moderate` |
| Land dedication being considered but site has no contiguous ¼-acre parcel meeting PDOP § 14.3.7 standards | `moderate` (fee-only path; raise budget) |
| 25-year floodplain on site being counted toward parkland credit | `moderate` (mandatory 0% credit) |
| AE / transmission easement on site overlapping prospective parkland boundary | `moderate` (cannot label as parkland) |
| Determination letter not yet requested; project past concept stage | `moderate` (precondition for any fee/method certainty) |
| SMART Housing certification feasible and not currently planned | `note` (opportunity — call out fee savings) |
| Project includes a detention pond that could double as parkland at 50% credit | `note` (opportunity) |
| Site is in ETJ; no parkland dedication applies | `note` (confirm and move on) |
| Civic/commercial-only project (no residential or hotel/motel units) | `note` (out of scope; no obligation) |
| Fee schedule referenced is more than 12 months old | `data-gap` (rates change Oct 1) |

## Common pitfalls

- **Citing the repealed 2016 Ordinance (Ord. 20160128-086)** on a coversheet for a post-2024 application. Current authority is LDC Article 14 as restructured by Ord. 20231130-087.
- **Treating commercial square footage as fee-bearing.** Commercial parkland was repealed January 1, 2024. Don't include retail, office, or industrial in fee calcs.
- **Self-assigning a Geographic Area** ("we think we're Urban") without PARD confirmation in the Determination. The boundary ordinance is not on plans and not in Bureau.
- **Stating multifamily fee due "before site plan approval."** It's due before CO (LDC § 25-1-609(B)). Single-family fees are due before plat/site plan approval — different rule.
- **Assuming Geographic Area = Parkland Dedication Urban Core.** These are two distinct concepts. Urban Core governs the 15% SF cap and off-site proximity; Geographic Area governs the multifamily fee amount only.
- **Counting the 15% Urban Core figure as a minimum** dedication. It's the maximum — formula above 15% converts to fee-in-lieu for the overage.
- **Assuming a park easement is fine for creek-adjacent parkland.** PARD requires fee simple deed for waterway-adjacent dedications by consistent reviewer convention.
- **Counting 25-year floodplain at any nonzero credit.** Always 0% (PDOP § 14.3.8). The land may still need to be included but earns no credit.
- **Forgetting that the Determination expires.** Treat as expired at 1 year (PDOP 14.3.5(B)) or upon a >10% unit count change. Long-running entitlement timelines outlast Determinations.
- **Skipping the Chapter 26 process** for "minor" work on existing parkland (utility tie-ins, staging, drainage outfalls). There is no de minimis exception — flag the full 6-step process.
- **Posting fiscal surety based on a self-calculated cost estimate** without the PARD written notification letter (PDOP § 14.3.10(E)). PARD sets the surety amount in writing to the Fiscal Office; applicant cannot front-run it.
- **Treating a PIA as a substitute for the Chapter 26 Council easement** (or vice versa). These are distinct, layered requirements when work occurs on dedicated parkland.
- **Confusing private common open space (Subchapter E § 2.7)** with dedicated parkland. They satisfy different requirements; the § 2.7 5% does not satisfy parkland dedication and vice versa.
- **Assuming the PARD amenity pricing guide and Geographic Area boundaries are in Bureau.** They're external documents — flag for PARD verification at cost-estimate and fee-confirmation steps.

**Finding:** Based on the site's upland suburban location (Zone X, no floodplain), the property is not expected to contain jurisdictional wetlands. The NWI Wetlands Mapper should be consulted for definitive confirmation, but the Scofield subdivision is a fully built-out residential neighborhood on well-drained upland soils with no surface water features on or adjacent to the subject lot. No Section 404 Clean Water Act permit or Army Corps of Engineers coordination is anticipated. A formal wetland delineation has not been performed -- this is a minor data gap given the low probability of wetland presence.
**Confidence:** Inferred (NWI map review recommended for formal confirmation)

---

### 9. Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (ESA)

**Citation:** ASTM E1527-21 (Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments)
**Finding:** **No Phase I ESA has been commissioned for this property.** This is a recognized data gap. The property has been in residential use (single-family home) since the Scofield subdivision was developed in the 1980s-1990s. Prior to subdivision development, the area was primarily agricultural/ranching land. The residential use history suggests low risk of Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs). However, without a Phase I ESA, potential concerns such as historical agricultural chemical use, underground storage tanks on adjacent parcels, or vapor intrusion from nearby commercial areas cannot be formally ruled out. A Phase I ESA is recommended before demolition, particularly to assess for asbestos-containing materials (ACM) and lead-based paint (LBP) in the existing structure, which would require an asbestos survey under TCEQ Asbestos NESHAP regulations prior to demolition.
**Confidence:** Unconfirmed (data gap acknowledged)

---

### 10. Prior Use History and Contamination Risk

**Citation:** TCEQ State Superfund and LUST databases; historical aerial imagery
**Finding:** The Scofield subdivision was platted and developed as a residential community in the 1980s-1990s. Prior land use was predominantly undeveloped rangeland/agricultural use. No known TCEQ State Superfund sites, EPA National Priorities List (NPL) sites, or Leaking Underground Storage Tank (LUST) sites have been identified at this address. The surrounding area is residential and low-density commercial (Scofield Farms retail corridor). The contamination risk profile is **low**, consistent with typical suburban residential land. A formal database search (EDR or equivalent) through a Phase I ESA would provide definitive documentation.
**Confidence:** Inferred (formal database search not performed)

---

### 11. Watershed Protection Ordinance -- Demolition and Redevelopment

**Citation:** Austin LDC Ch. 25-8 Subchapter A; City of Austin Development Services Department
**Finding:** Demolition of the existing single-family home and construction of a new duplex constitutes **redevelopment** under Austin's Watershed Protection Ordinance. In a suburban watershed, redevelopment may not increase impervious cover beyond the limits prescribed in Sec. 25-8-392. The redevelopment must comply with current water quality requirements, including providing water quality controls for the developed area. The applicant will need to file a site plan (unless exempt as a single-lot residential project) and demonstrate compliance with IC limits and water quality standards. For a single-lot duplex, the site plan exemption process and applicable Watershed Protection review requirements should be confirmed with Development Services early in the entitlement process.
**Confidence:** Verified

---

### 12. Tree Protection

**Citation:** Austin LDC Ch. 25-8 Subchapter B (Tree and Natural Area Protection); City Arborist
**Finding:** Austin's tree protection ordinance applies to all development. Trees 19 inches in diameter or greater (measured at 4.5 feet above grade) are classified as **Heritage Trees** and require a permit for removal with mitigation. Trees 8 inches in diameter or greater are **Protected Trees** and require mitigation if removed during development. The existing lot at 12713 Cinchring Ln may contain mature trees established during or after subdivision development. A tree survey will be required as part of the building permit application, and any protected or heritage trees must be preserved or mitigated per the ordinance. Tree mitigation can be satisfied through on-site replanting or payment into the City's tree fund.
**Confidence:** Verified

---

## Summary of Key Environmental Constraints

|---|---|---|
| Floodplain | Zone X -- not in floodplain | None |
| Watershed | Walnut Creek -- Suburban | IC limits + water quality controls apply |
| Edwards Aquifer | Not in recharge/contributing zone | No EAPP required |
| CEFs | None known; low probability | ERI form at site plan |
| Endangered Species | BCCP participation area | BCCP fee at permit |
| Wetlands | None expected | NWI check recommended |
| Phase I ESA | Not performed | Recommended before demolition |
| Contamination | Low risk (residential history) | Confirm via Phase I |
| Tree Protection | Applies to all development | Tree survey required |

---

## Procedural Pathway

### Site Plan Exemption

Under Austin LDC, **residential uses of four or fewer units are exempt from site plan requirements**. A duplex (2 units) qualifies for this exemption. No administrative site plan is required.

### Building Permit

The duplex can proceed via a **residential building permit** application through Austin Development Services (DSD). Under HOME Phase 1, applications have been accepted since February 5, 2024.

**Permit review path:**

1. **Residential Plan Review** -- submit building plans through Austin DSD
2. Plans reviewed for compliance with LDC dimensional standards, IRC/IBC building codes, and applicable environmental/drainage requirements
3. No zoning change, conditional use permit, or Board of Adjustment variance is needed (assuming the lot meets dimensional standards)

### Site Plan Lite (HOME Phase 2 -- March 2025)

Site Plan Lite is a streamlined review process adopted March 6, 2025, primarily for HOME Phase 2 subdivision and small-lot projects. It is **not required** for a duplex on an existing lot that already meets SF-2 minimum lot size. However, if the owner later pursues subdivision of the lot (e.g., into two small lots), Site Plan Lite would apply.

### Demolition Permit

A separate **demolition permit** is required to remove the existing house. Austin DSD processes demo permits administratively; typical turnaround is 2-4 weeks. Asbestos survey may be required for pre-2000 construction (this house was built 1993).

### Tree Permits

Austin's tree ordinance (LDC Ch. 25-8, Subchapter B) protects trees with trunk diameter >= 19 inches (heritage trees >= 24 inches). A tree survey may be required, and mitigation fees or replacement may apply if protected trees must be removed.

**Citation:** [Austin DSD -- Residential Plan Review](https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/residential-plan-review); [Austin DSD -- Site Plans and Exemptions](https://www.austintexas.gov/siteplans); [HOME Amendments Page](https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/home-amendments)

---

## Recent Ordinances

| Ordinance | Effective | Impact on This Project |
|---|---|---|
| **HOME Phase 1** (Ord. 20231207-001) | Feb 5, 2024 | Permits duplex/two-unit on SF-2 lots; reduces front setback to 15 ft, rear to 5 ft |
| **Parking Minimums Elimination** (C20-2023-010) | Nov 12, 2023 | No minimum parking required for duplex |
| **HOME Phase 2** (adopted May 2024) | Nov 16, 2024 (citywide) | Allows small-lot SF down to 1,800 sq ft; not directly required for duplex but enables future subdivision |
| **Site Plan Lite & Infill Plat** (March 2025) | June 16, 2025 | Streamlined review for subdivisions; not required for duplex on existing lot |

---

## Open Questions

1. **Confirm base zoning via Austin GIS/Property Profile.** While research strongly indicates SF-2, the official zoning should be verified on the [Austin Zoning Map](https://www.austintexas.gov/page/zoning-resources-site-regulations) or via the Property Profile tool. One listing source referenced "residential multi family" which may reflect HOME-amended permitted uses rather than the base district code.

2. **Platted building line enforcement.** Does Austin DSD enforce the 25 ft platted building line through the building permit process, or is it treated as a private covenant enforceable only by adjacent lot owners? If enforced, the front setback is 25 ft (not 15 ft), reducing the buildable envelope by ~10 ft of depth.

3. **Lot width.** Confirm the lot width meets the 50 ft minimum required for duplex use. At 0.18 acres (~7,840 sq ft), the lot geometry needs verification from the plat.

4. **Watershed impervious cover.** Confirm the Walnut Creek suburban watershed impervious cover limit for this specific parcel. The 45% zoning limit is likely controlling, but verify via Austin's watershed GIS layer.

5. **HOA restrictions.** Scofield Farms has an HOA ($125/quarter per listing data). HOA covenants, conditions, and restrictions (CC&Rs) may prohibit or restrict duplex construction, impose architectural review, or set additional setback/height/design requirements independent of city zoning. Review the recorded CC&Rs and any deed restrictions on Lot 12, Block M.

6. **Tree survey.** Confirm whether any protected or heritage trees exist on the lot that would require mitigation.

7. **Drainage review.** For demolition and new construction on an existing lot (not a new subdivision), confirm whether drainage/grading plan review is required or if the project falls under the four-unit residential exemption.

8. **WUI status.** Confirm whether the property is within the Wildland-Urban Interface boundary, which may impose additional fire-resistant construction standards.

---

## Summary Assessment

A ground-up duplex at 12713 Cinchring Ln is **permitted by right** under HOME Phase 1 on this SF-2 lot. The project can proceed via **residential building permit only** -- no rezoning, conditional use permit, site plan, or Board of Adjustment action is required. Key constraints are the 40% building coverage / 0.40 FAR cap, the 45% impervious cover limit, and the potential 25 ft front building line from the plat (versus the 15 ft HOME setback). The most significant non-zoning risk is the Scofield Farms HOA CC&Rs, which should be reviewed before design proceeds.
